body.text: Ratnagotravibhāgo Mahāyānottaratantraśāstram
body.translated_text: <s>Ratnagotravibhāga</s>, the <s>Mahāyānottaratantraśāstra</s>

body.text:
1. prathamaḥ paricchedaḥ
oṃ namaḥ śrīvajrasattvāya /
body.translated_text:
1. First Chapter.
Oṃ, homage to the glorious <s>Vajrasattva</s>!

children.text: buddhaśca dharmaśca gaṇaśca dhāturbodhirguṇāḥ karma ca bauddhamantyam /
children.translated_text: <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, community (<s>Gaṇa</s>), element (<s>Dhātu</s>), awakening (<s>Bodhi</s>), qualities (<s>Guṇa</s>), and activity (<s>Karma</s>)—the last pertain to the <s>Buddha</s>—

children.text: kṛtsnasya śāstrasya śarīrametat samāsato vajrapadāni sapta // 1 //
children.translated_text: These are the body of the entire treatise, in brief, the seven <s>vajrapadas</s> (diamond topics). (1)

body.text: vajropamasyādhigamārthasya padaṃ sthānamiti vajrapadam / tatra śruticintāmayajñānaduṣprativedhādanabhilāpyasvabhāvaḥ pratyātmavedanīyo 'rtho vajravadveditavyaḥ / yānyakṣarāṇi tamarthamabhivadanti tatprāptyanukūlamārgābhidyotanatastāni tatpratiṣṭhābhūtatvāt padamityucyante / iti duṣprativedhārthena pratiṣṭhārthena ca vajrapadatvamarthavyañjanayoranugantavyam / tatra katamo 'rthaḥ katamadvyañjanam / artha ucyate saptaprakāro 'dhigamārtho yaduta buddhārtho dharmārthaḥ saṃghārtho dhātvartho bodhyartho guṇārthaḥ
body.translated_text: A <s>vajrapada</s> (diamond topic) is the ground (<s>pada</s>) of the meaning of realization (<s>adhigamārtha</s>) that is diamond-like (<s>vajropama</s>). There, the meaning—which is hard to penetrate by knowledge born of hearing, reflection, and meditation, which is of inexpressible nature, and which is to be individually realized—is to be understood as diamond-like. The syllables that express that meaning, because they illuminate the path conducive to attaining it, are called <s>pada</s> (words) since they serve as the foundation for that attainment. Thus, the diamond-topic nature (<s>vajrapadatva</s>) of both meaning and expression is to be understood through the sense of 'hard to penetrate' and 'foundation.' Among these, what is the meaning and what is the expression? The meaning is said to be the sevenfold meaning of realization, namely: the meaning of <s>Buddha</s>, the meaning of <s>Dharma</s>, the meaning of <s>Saṃgha</s>, the meaning of <s>Dhātu</s> (element), the meaning of <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening), the meaning of <s>Guṇa</s> (qualities),

body.text: karmārthaśca / ayamucyate 'rthaḥ / yairakṣaraireṣa saptaprakāro 'dhigamārthaḥ sūcyate prakāśyata idamucyate vyañjanam / sa caiṣa vajrapadanirdeśo vistareṇa yathāsūtramanugantavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: and the meaning of <s>Karma</s> (activity). This is called the meaning. The expression (<s>vyañjana</s>) is that by whose syllables this sevenfold meaning of realization is indicated and illuminated. And this exposition of the <s>vajrapadas</s> is to be understood in detail according to the sūtras.

body.text: anidarśano hyānanda tathāgataḥ / sa na śakyaścakṣuṣā draṣṭum / anabhilāpyo hyānanda dharmaḥ / sa na śakyaḥ karṇena śrotum / asaṃskṛto hyānanda saṃghaḥ / sa na śakyaḥ kāyena vā cittena vā paryupā situm / itīmāni trīṇi vajrapadāni dṛḍhādhyāśayaparivartānusāreṇānugantavyāni /
body.translated_text: For the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, is beyond exemplification; he cannot be seen with the eye. For the <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, is inexpressible; it cannot be heard with the ear. For the <s>Saṃgha</s>, <s>Ānanda</s>, is unconditioned; it cannot be attended upon by body or mind. These three <s>vajrapadas</s> are to be understood following the <s>Dṛḍhādhyāśayaparivarta</s> (Chapter on Firm Resolve).

body.text: tathāgataviṣayo hi śāriputrāyamarthastathāgatagocaraḥ / sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhairapi tāvacchāriputrāyamartho na śakyaḥ samyak svaprajñayā xxx draṣṭuṃ vā pratyavekṣituṃ vā / prāgeva bālapṛthagjanairanyatra tathāgataśraddhāgamanataḥ / śraddhāgamanīyo hi śāriputra paramārthaḥ / paramārtha iti śāriputra sattvadhātoretadadhivacanam / sattvadhāturiti śāriputra tathāgatagarbhasyaitadadhivacanam / tathāgatagarbha iti śāriputra dharmakāyasyaitadadhivacanam / itīdaṃ caturthaṃ vajrapadamanūnatvāpūrṇatvanirdeśaparivartānusāreṇānugatavyam /
body.translated_text: For this matter, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, the sphere of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. Even all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, cannot by their own wisdom properly see or examine this matter—how much less ordinary foolish people, except through faith in the <s>Tathāgata</s>. For the ultimate truth, <s>Śāriputra</s>, is accessible through faith. 'Ultimate truth,' <s>Śāriputra</s>, is a designation for the <s>sattvadhātu</s> (element of beings). '<s>Sattvadhātu</s>,' <s>Śāriputra</s>, is a designation for the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> (embryo of the Tathāgata). '<s>Tathāgatagarbha</s>,' <s>Śāriputra</s>, is a designation for the <s>dharmakāya</s> (dharma-body). This fourth <s>vajrapada</s> is to be understood following the <s>Anūnatvāpūrṇatvanirdeśaparivarta</s> (Chapter on the Teaching of Neither Decrease Nor Increase).

body.text: anuttarā samyaksaṃbodhiriti bhagavan nirvāṇadhātoretadadhivacanam / nirvāṇadhāturiti bhagavan tathāgatadharmakāyasyaitadadhivacanam / itīdaṃ pañcamaṃ vajrapadamāryaśrīmālāsūtrānusāreṇānugantavyam /
body.translated_text: 'Supreme perfect awakening,' O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is a designation for the <s>nirvāṇadhātu</s> (element of nirvāṇa). '<s>Nirvāṇadhātu</s>,' O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is a designation for the <s>dharmakāya</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' This fifth <s>vajrapada</s> is to be understood following the <s>Āryaśrīmālāsūtra</s>.

body.text: yo 'yaṃ śāriputra tathāgatanirdiṣṭo dharmakāyaḥ so 'yamavinirbhāgadharmā / avinirmuktajñānaguṇo yaduta gaṅgānadīvālikāvyatikrāntaistathāgatadharmaiḥ / itīdaṃ ṣaṣṭhaṃ vajrapadmanūnatvāpūrṇatvanirdeśānusāreṇānugantavyam /
body.translated_text: 'This <s>dharmakāya</s> taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Śāriputra</s>, has inseparable qualities—inseparable knowledge-qualities, that is, <s>Tathāgata</s>-qualities exceeding the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river.' This sixth <s>vajrapada</s> is to be understood following the <s>Anūnatvāpūrṇatvanirdeśa</s> (Teaching of Neither Decrease Nor Increase).

body.text: na mañjuśrīstathāgataḥ kalpayati na vikalpayati / athavāsyānābhogenākalpayato 'vikalpayata iyamevaṃrūpā kriyā pravartate / itīdaṃ saptamaṃ vajrapada tathāgataguṇajñānācintyaviṣayāvatāranirdeśānusāreṇānugantavyam / itīmāni samāsataḥ sapta vajrapadāni sakalasyāsya śāstrasyoddeśamukhasaṃgrāhārthena śarīramiti veditavyam /
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, does not conceptualize nor discriminate. Rather, for him who is without effort, without conceptualizing or discriminating, this kind of activity proceeds.' This seventh <s>vajrapada</s> is to be understood following the <s>Tathāgataguṇajñānācintyaviṣayāvatāranirdeśa</s> (Teaching on Entering the Inconceivable Domain of Tathāgata Qualities and Knowledge). These, in brief, are the seven <s>vajrapadas</s>, which are to be understood as the body of this entire treatise in the sense of comprehending its summary topics.

children.translated_text: These [vajrapadas] are presented according to their own characteristics, in order, in the <s>Dhāraṇīrājasūtra</s>;
From the introductory section, three topics should be known, and four from the distinction of <s>Jina</s>-qualities, [thus knows] the wise one. (2)

body.text: eṣāṃ ca saptānāṃ vajrapadānāṃ svalakṣaṇanirdeśena yathākramamāryadhāraṇīśvararājasūtranidānaparivartānugatāni trīṇi padāni veditavyāni / tata ūrdhvamavaśiṣṭāni catvāri bodhisattvatathāgatadharmanirdeśabhedāditi / tasmādyaduktam /
body.translated_text: Of these seven <s>vajrapadas</s>, by means of their individual characteristic exposition, three topics are to be understood as presented in the introductory chapter of the <s>Āryadhāraṇīśvararājasūtra</s>, in order. The remaining four [are to be understood] above and beyond, from the distinction of the teaching of <s>Bodhisattva</s> and <s>Tathāgata</s> qualities. Therefore it is said:

body.text: bhagavān sarvadharmasamatābhisaṃbuddhaḥ supravartitadharmacakro 'nantaśiṣyagaṇasuvinīta iti / ebhistribhirmūlapadairyathākramaṃ trayāṇāṃ ratnānāmanupūrvasamutpādasamudāgamavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / avaśiṣṭāni catvāri padāni triratnotpattyanurūpahetusamudāgamanirdeśo veditavyaḥ / tatra yato 'ṣṭamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau vartamānaḥ sarvadharmavaśitāprāpto
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Bhagavān</s> has fully awakened to the equality of all dharmas, has well turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, and has well trained an infinite assembly of disciples.' By these three root topics, in order, the successive arising, attainment, and establishment of the Three Jewels is to be understood. The remaining four topics are to be understood as the teaching of the cause for the arising of the Three Jewels in accordance [with them]. There, because one abiding on the eighth <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stage has attained mastery over all dharmas,

body.text: bhavati tasmāt sa bodhimaṇḍavaragataḥ sarvadharmasamatābhisaṃbuddha ityucyate / yato navamyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau vartamāno 'nuttaradharmabhāṇakatvasaṃpannaḥ sarvasattvāśayasuvidhijña indriyaparamapāramitāprāptaḥ sarvasattvakleśavāsanānusaṃdhisamudghātanakuśalo bhavati tasmāt so 'bhisaṃbuddhabodhiḥ supravartitadharmacakra ityucyate / yato daśamyāṃ bhūmāvanuttaratathāgatadharmayauvarājyābhiṣekaprāptyanantaramanābhogabuddhakāryāpratipraśrabdho bhavati tasmāt sa supravartitadharmacakro 'nantaśiṣyagaṇasuvinīta ityucyate / tāṃ punaranantaśiṣyagaṇasuvinītatāṃ tadanantaramanena granthena darśayati / mahatā bhikṣusaṃghena sārdha yāvadaprameyeṇa ca bodhisattvagaṇena sārdhamiti / yathākramaṃ śrāvakabodhau buddhabodhau ca suvinītatvādevaṃguṇa samanvāgatairiti /
body.translated_text: therefore, having gone to the excellent seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), he is called 'fully awakened to the equality of all dharmas.' Because one abiding on the ninth <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stage is endowed with supreme skill in teaching the <s>Dharma</s>, knows well the dispositions of all beings, has attained the utmost perfection of faculties, and is skilled in eradicating the latent impressions of the afflictions of all beings, therefore he, having attained awakening, is called 'one who has well turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>.' Because on the tenth stage, immediately upon attaining the consecration as crown prince of the supreme <s>Tathāgata</s>-dharma, he becomes unceasing in effortless <s>Buddha</s>-activity, therefore he, having well turned the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, is called 'one who has well trained an infinite assembly of disciples.' That quality of having well trained an infinite assembly of disciples is shown immediately after by this passage: 'Together with a great assembly of monks... and together with an immeasurable assembly of <s>Bodhisattvas</s>'—because they are well trained in <s>Śrāvaka</s>-awakening and <s>Buddha</s>-awakening respectively, and are endowed with such qualities.

body.text: tataḥ śrāvakabodhisattvaguṇavarṇanirdeśānantaramacintyabuddhasamādhivṛṣabhitāṃ pratītya vipularatnavyūhamaṇḍalavyūha nirvṛttitathāgatapariṣatsamāvartanavividhadivyadravyapūjāvidhānastutimeghābhisaṃpravarṣaṇato buddharatnaguṇavibhāgavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / tadanantaramudāradharmāsanavyūhaprabhādharmaparyāyanāmaguṇaparikīrtanato dharmaratnaguṇavibhāgavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / tadanantaramanyonyaṃ bodhisattvasamādhigocaraviṣayaprabhāva saṃdarśanatadvicitraguṇavarṇanirdeśataḥ saṃgharatnaguṇavibhāgavyavasthānaṃ veditavyam / tadanantaraṃ
body.translated_text: Then, after the exposition describing the qualities of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the classification of the qualities of the <s>Buddha</s>-jewel is to be understood from the raining down of clouds of praise, worship offerings of various divine substances, the convening of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s retinue, and the manifesting of vast jewel-array <s>maṇḍalas</s>, in dependence upon the might of the inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-<s>samādhi</s>. After that, the classification of the qualities of the <s>Dharma</s>-jewel is to be understood from the glorification of the excellent Dharma-seat array, its radiance, and the names and qualities of the Dharma-teachings. After that, the classification of the qualities of the <s>Saṃgha</s>-jewel is to be understood from the mutual display of the power and sphere of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>samādhi</s>, and the exposition describing their various qualities. After that,

body.text: punarapi buddharaśmyabhiṣekairanuttaradharmarājajyeṣṭhaputraparamavaiśāradyapratibhānopakaraṇatāṃ pratītya tathāgatabhūtaguṇaparamārthastutinirdeśataśca mahāyānaparamadharmakathāvastūpanyasanataśca tatpratipatteḥ paramadharmaiśvaryaphalaprāptisaṃdarśanataśca yathāsaṃkhyameṣāmeva trayāṇāṃ ratnānāmanuttaraguṇavibhāgavyavasthānaṃ nidānaparivartāvasānagatameva draṣṭavyam /
body.translated_text: again, through the consecration by <s>Buddha</s>-rays, in dependence upon being equipped with the supreme confidence and eloquence of the eldest son of the supreme <s>Dharma</s>-king, and from the teaching praising the true qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s> in their ultimate sense, and from the presentation of the subject matter of the supreme <s>Mahāyāna</s> Dharma-discourse, and from the demonstration of attaining the fruit of supreme Dharma-sovereignty through that practice—the classification of the unsurpassed qualities of these same Three Jewels, in due order, is to be seen as contained within the conclusion of the introductory chapter.

body.text: tataḥ sūtranidānaparivartānantaraṃ buddhadhātuḥ ṣaṣṭyākāratadviśuddhiguṇaparikarmanirdeśena paridīpitaḥ / viśodhye 'rthe guṇavati tadviśuddhiparikarmayogāt / imaṃ cārthavaśamupādāya daśasu bodhisattvabhūmiṣu punarjātarūpaparikarmaviśeṣodāharaṇamudāhṛtam / asminneva ca sūtre tathāgatakarmanirdeśānantaramaviṃśuddhavaiḍūryamaṇidṛṣṭāntaḥ kṛtaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, after the introductory chapter of the sūtra, the <s>buddhadhātu</s> (Buddha-element) is illuminated by the teaching of the sixty aspects of its purification-qualities and preparatory practices. Because the object to be purified is endowed with qualities, the practice of its purification [is taught]. And taking up this point, in the ten <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stages, the special illustration of the purification of gold is given. And in this same sūtra, after the teaching of <s>Tathāgata</s>-activity, the simile of the impure <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) gem is given.

body.text: tadyathā kulaputra kuśalo maṇikāro maṇiśuddhisuvidhijñaḥ / sa maṇigotrādaparyavadāpitāni maṇiratnāni gṛhītvā tīkṣṇena khārodakenotkṣālya kṛṣṇena keśakambalaparyavadāpanena paryavadāpayati / na ca tāvanmātreṇa vīrya praśrambhayati / tataḥ paścāt tīkṣṇenāmiṣarasenotkṣālya khaṇḍikāparyavadāpanena paryavadāpayati / na ca tāvanmātreṇa vīrya praśrambhayati / tataḥ sa paścānmahābhaiṣajyarasenotkṣālya sūkṣmavastraparyavadāpanena paryavadāpayati / paryavadāpitaṃ cāpagatakācamabhijātavaiḍūryamityucyate /
body.translated_text: Just as, O son of good family, a skilled jeweler, expert in the purification of gems, having taken gem-stones not yet purified from a gem-mine, washes them with sharp alkaline water and polishes them with a black hair-cloth; and not being content with that much effort, he then washes them with a sharp acidic solution and polishes them with a coarse cloth; and not being content with that much effort, he then washes them with a great medicinal solution and polishes them with a fine cloth; and once polished, free from impurity, it is called a fine <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) gem.

body.text: evameva kulaputra tathāgato 'pyapariśuddhaṃ sattvadhātuṃ viditvānityaduḥkhānātmāśubhodvegakathayā saṃsārābhiratān sattvānudvejayati / ārye ca dharmavinaye 'vatārayati / na ca tāvanmātreṇa vīrya praśrambhayati / tataḥ paścācchūnyānimittapraṇihitakathayā tathāgatanetrīmavabodhayati / na ca tāvanmātreṇa tathāgato vīryaṃ praśrambhayati / tataḥ paścādavivartyadharmacakrakathayā trimaṇḍalapariśuddhikathayā ca tathāgataviṣaye tān sattvānavatārayati nānāprakṛtihetukān / avatīrṇāśca samānāstathāgatadharmatāmadhigamyānuttarā dakṣiṇīyā ityucyanta iti /
body.translated_text: In the same way, O son of good family, the <s>Tathāgata</s> too, having perceived the impure <s>sattvadhātu</s> (element of beings), rouses beings who delight in <s>saṃsāra</s> with the teaching of impermanence, suffering, non-self, and impurity, and causes them to enter the noble <s>Dharma</s> and <s>Vinaya</s>. And not being content with that much effort, he then awakens them to the <s>Tathāgata</s>-guidance through the teaching of emptiness, signlessness, and wishlessness. And not being content with that much effort, the <s>Tathāgata</s> then causes those beings of various dispositions and causes to enter the domain of the <s>Tathāgata</s> through the teaching of the irreversible Dharma-wheel and the teaching of the purity of the three spheres. And having entered, having realized <s>Tathāgata</s>-nature (<s>tathāgatadharmatā</s>), they are called unsurpassed fields of merit.

body.text: etadeva viśuddhagotraṃ tathāgatadhātumabhisaṃdhāyoktam /
body.translated_text: With reference to this very purified lineage, the <s>tathāgatadhātu</s> (Tathāgata-element), it is said:

children.translated_text: Just as gold is not seen in stone-dust,

children.text: parikammena tad diṭṭhaṃ evaṃ loke tathāgatā iti //
children.translated_text: but through purification it is seen—so too are the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the world.

body.text: tatra katame te buddhadhātoḥ ṣaṣṭyākāraviśuddhiparikarmaguṇāḥ / tadyathā caturākāro bodhisattvālaṃkāraḥ / aṣṭākāro bodhisattvāvabhāsaḥ / ṣoḍaśākārī bodhisattvamahākaruṇā / dvātriṃśadākāraṃ bodhisattvakarma /
body.translated_text: Among these, what are the sixty aspects of the purification-qualities and preparatory practices of the <s>buddhadhātu</s>? They are: the fourfold <s>Bodhisattva</s> adornment, the eightfold <s>Bodhisattva</s> radiance, the sixteenfold great compassion of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, and the thirty-twofold <s>Bodhisattva</s> activity.

body.text: tannirdeśānantaraṃ buddhabodhiḥ ṣoḍaśākāramahābodhikaruṇānirdeśena paridīpitā / tannirdeśānantaraṃ buddhaguṇā daśabalacaturvaiśāradyaṣṭādaśāveṇikabuddhadharmanirdeśena paridīpitāḥ / tannirdeśānantaraṃ buddhakarma dvātriṃśadākāra niruttaratathāgatakarmanirdeśena paridīpitam / evamimāni sapta vajrapadāni svalakṣaṇanirdeśato vistareṇa yathāsūtramanugantavyāni / kaḥ punareṣāmanuśleṣaḥ /
body.translated_text: After that teaching, <s>Buddhabodhi</s> (Buddha-awakening) is illuminated by the teaching of the sixteen aspects of great awakening-compassion. After that teaching, the <s>Buddha</s>-qualities are illuminated by the teaching of the ten powers, four fearlessnesses, and eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-dharmas. After that teaching, <s>Buddha</s>-activity is illuminated by the teaching of the thirty-two aspects of unsurpassed <s>Tathāgata</s>-activity. Thus, these seven <s>vajrapadas</s> are to be understood in detail according to the sūtras, through the exposition of their individual characteristics. Now, what is the connection among them?

body.text: buddhāddharmo dharmataścāryasaṃghaḥ saṃghe garbho jñānadhātvāptiniṣṭhaḥ /
body.translated_text: From the <s>Buddha</s> comes the <s>Dharma</s>, from the <s>Dharma</s> comes the noble <s>Saṃgha</s>; in the <s>Saṃgha</s> is the <s>garbha</s> (embryo), whose culmination is the attainment of the <s>jñānadhātu</s> (knowledge-element);

body.text: tajjñānāptiścāgrabodhirbalādyairdhamairyuktā sarvasattvārthakṛdbhiḥ // 3 //
body.translated_text: That attainment of knowledge is supreme <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening), endowed with qualities such as the powers, which accomplish the welfare of all beings. (3)

body.text: uktaḥ śāstrasaṃbandhaḥ /
body.translated_text: The connection of the treatise has been stated.

body.text: idānīṃ ślokānāmartho vaktavyaḥ / ye sattvāstathāgatena vinītāste tathāgataṃ śaraṇaṃ gacchanto dharmatāniṣyandābhiprasādena dharma ca saṃghaṃ ca śaraṇaṃ gacchanti / atastatprathamato buddharatnamadhikṛtya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: Now the meaning of the verses is to be explained. Those beings who have been trained by the <s>Tathāgata</s>, going for refuge to the <s>Tathāgata</s>, through the faith that flows from the nature of <s>Dharma</s>, go for refuge to the <s>Dharma</s> and the <s>Saṃgha</s> as well. Therefore, first, a verse concerning the <s>Buddha</s>-jewel:

children.translated_text: He who, having himself awakened to <s>Buddhahood</s>—which is without beginning, middle, or end, and peaceful—
and having awakened, taught the fearless, steadfast path for the sake of awakening those who are unawakened;
To him who wields the supreme sword-vajra of knowledge and compassion, the sole cutter of the sprouts of suffering,
the breaker of the walls of doubt hidden in the dense thickets of various views—homage! (4)

body.text: anena kiṃ darśayati /
body.translated_text: What does this show?

children.translated_text: Unconditioned, effortless, not arisen from external conditions,
<s>Buddhahood</s> is endowed with knowledge, compassion, and power, and accomplishes the twofold purpose. (5)

body.text: anena samāsato 'ṣṭābhirguṇaiḥ saṃgṛhītaṃ buddhatvamudbhāvitam / aṣṭau guṇāḥ katame / asaṃskṛtatvamanābhogatāparapratyayābhisaṃbodhirjñānaṃ karuṇā śaktiḥ svārthasaṃpat parārthasaṃpaditi /
body.translated_text: By this, <s>Buddhahood</s> is shown to be comprised, in brief, of eight qualities. What are the eight qualities? They are: being unconditioned, effortlessness, awakening not dependent on external conditions, knowledge, compassion, power, accomplishment of one's own purpose, and accomplishment of others' purpose.

body.text: anādimadhyanidhanaprakṛtatvādasaṃskṛtam /
body.translated_text: Because its nature is without beginning, middle, or end, it is unconditioned;

body.text: śāntadharmaśarīratvādanābhogamiti smṛtam // 6 //
body.translated_text: Because of having a body of peaceful <s>dharmas</s>, it is known as 'without deliberate effort' (<s>anābhoga</s>). ||6||

children.translated_text: Because of being realizable through one's own [experience], it arises without dependence on others (<s>aparapratyayodaya</s>);
Knowledge (<s>jñāna</s>) [is explained] thus in three ways through awakening (<s>bodhi</s>); compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) through the teaching of the path. ||7||
Power (<s>śakti</s>), however, [is understood] from knowledge and compassion through the eradication of suffering and afflictions (<s>kleśas</s>);
Self-benefit (<s>svārtha</s>) [is accomplished] by the first three qualities; benefit of others (<s>parārtha</s>) by the last three. ||8||

body.text: saṃskṛtaviparyayeṇāsaṃskṛtaṃ veditayvam / tatra saṃskṛtamucyate yasyotpādo 'pi prajñāyatesthitirapi bhaṅgo 'pi prajñāyate / tadabhāvādbuddhatvamanādimadhyanidhanamasaṃskṛtadharmakāya prabhāvitaṃ draṣṭavyam / sarvaprapañcavikalpopaśāntatvādanābhogam / svayaṃbhūjñānādhigamyatvādaparapratyayodayam / udayo 'trābhisaṃbodho 'bhipretotpādaḥ / ityasaṃskṛtādapravṛttilakṣaṇādapi tathāgatatvādanābhogataḥ sarvasaṃbuddhakṛtyamā saṃsārakoṭeranuparatamanupacchinnaṃ pravartate /
body.translated_text: The unconditioned (<s>asaṃskṛta</s>) is to be understood as the opposite of the conditioned (<s>saṃskṛta</s>). There, the conditioned is said to be that whose arising is perceived, whose persistence is also perceived, and whose decay is also perceived. Due to the absence of those [characteristics], <s>Buddhahood</s> (<s>buddhatva</s>) is to be seen as without beginning, middle, or end, manifesting as the unconditioned <s>Dharmakāya</s>. Because all conceptual proliferation and discrimination (<s>prapañcavikalpa</s>) are pacified, [it is] without deliberate effort (<s>anābhoga</s>). Because it is realizable through self-born knowledge (<s>svayaṃbhūjñāna</s>), it arises without dependence on others. 'Arising' (<s>udaya</s>) here means full awakening (<s>abhisaṃbodha</s>) — this is the intended meaning of 'production.' Thus, from the unconditioned nature characterized by non-activity, from <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood itself, without deliberate effort, all Buddha-activity continues uninterrupted and unceasing until the limit of <s>saṃsāra</s>.

body.text: ityevamatyadbhutācintyaviṣayaṃ buddhatvamaśrutvā parataḥ svayamanācāryakeṇa svayaṃbhūjñānena nirabhilāpyasvabhāvatāmabhisaṃbudhya tadanubodhaṃ pratyabudhānāmapi jātyandhānāṃ pareṣāmanubodhāya tadanugāmimārgavyupadeśakaraṇādanuttarajñānakaruṇānvitatvaṃ veditavyam / mārgasyābhayatvaṃ lokottaratvāt / lokottaratvamapunarāvṛttitaśca / yathākramaṃ paraduḥkhakleśamūlasamudghātaṃ pratyanayoreva tathāgatajñānakaruṇayoḥ śaktirasivajradṛṣṭāntena paridīpitā / tatra duḥkhamūlaṃ samāsato yā kacidbhaveṣu nāmarūpābhinirvṛttiḥ / kleśamūlaṃ ya kācitsatkāyābhiniveśapūrvikā dṛṣṭirvicikitsā ca / tatra nāmarūpasaṃgṛhītaṃ duḥkhamabhinirvṛttilakṣaṇatvādaṅkurasthānīyaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: Thus, without hearing from others about this supremely wondrous and inconceivable domain of <s>Buddhahood</s>, having by oneself, without a teacher, through self-born knowledge, fully awakened to the inexpressible nature [of reality], and in order to awaken others — even those born blind — to that awakening, [the <s>Tathāgata</s>] teaches the path that follows that [awakening]. From this, one should understand [the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s] endowment with unsurpassed knowledge and compassion (<s>jñānakaruṇā</s>). The path is fearless because it is supramundane (<s>lokottara</s>); it is supramundane because of non-return. In due order, the power of these two — <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge and compassion — for uprooting the roots of others' suffering and afflictions has been illustrated by the simile of the sword and the <s>vajra</s>. There, the root of suffering, in brief, is whatever production of name-and-form (<s>nāmarūpa</s>) in [various] existences. The root of afflictions is whatever view (<s>dṛṣṭi</s>) preceded by clinging to a real self (<s>satkāyābhiniveśa</s>), and doubt (<s>vicikitsā</s>). There, suffering comprised of name-and-form, being characterized by production, should be understood as analogous to a sprout.

body.text: tacchettṛtve tathāgatajñānakaruṇāyoḥ śaktirasidṛṣṭantenopamitā veditavyā / dṛṣṭivicikitsāsamgṛhīto darśanamārgapraheyaḥ / kleśo laukikajñānaduravagāho durbhedaṃtvādvanagahanopagūḍhaprākārasadṛśaḥ / tadbhettṛtvāt tathāgatajñānakaruṇayoḥ śaktirvajradṛṣṭāntenopamitā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: The power of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge and compassion to cut that [suffering] is to be understood as compared by the simile of the sword. The affliction comprised of [wrong] views and doubt, to be abandoned by the path of seeing (<s>darśanamārga</s>), is difficult for mundane knowledge to penetrate, and because of its impenetrability is like a wall concealed within a dense forest. Because of its power to break through that, the power of <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge and compassion is to be understood as compared by the simile of the <s>vajra</s>.

body.text: ityete yathāddiṣṭāḥ ṣaṭ tathāgataguṇā vistaravibhāganirdeśato 'nayaivānupūrvyā sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṃkārasūtrānusāreṇānugantavyāḥ / tatra yaduktamanutpādo 'nirodha iti mañjuśrīstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha eṣa ityanena tāvadasaṃskṛtalakṣaṇastathāgata iti paridīpitam / yatpunaranantaraṃ vimalavaiḍūryapṛthivīśakrapratibimbodāharaṇamādiṃ kṛtvā yāvannavabhirudāharaṇairetamevānutpādānirodhatathāgatārthamadhikṛtyāha / evameva mañjuśrīstathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho neñjate na viṭhapati na prapañcayati na kalpayati na vikalpayati / akalpo 'vikalpo 'citto 'manasikāraḥ śītibhūto 'nutpādo 'nirodho 'dṛṣṭo 'śruto 'nāghrāto 'nāsvādito 'spṛṣṭo 'nimitto 'vijñaptiko 'vijñapanīya ityevamādirupaśamaprabhedapradeśanirdeśaḥ / anena svakriyāsu sarvaprapañcavikalpopaśāntatvādanābhogastathāgata iti paridīpitam / tata ūrdhvamudāharaṇanirdeśādavaśiṣṭena granthena sarvadharmadharmatathatābhisaṃbodhamukheṣvaparapratyayābhisaṃbodhastathāgatasya paridīpitaḥ / yatpunarante ṣoḍaśākārāṃ tathāgatabodhiṃ nirdiśyaivamāha / tatra mañjuśrīstathāgatasyaivaṃrūpān sarvadharmānabhisaṃbudhya sattvānāṃ ca dharmadhātuṃ vyavalokyāśuddhamavimalaṃ sāṅganaṃ vikrīḍitā nāma sattveṣu
body.translated_text: Thus these six <s>Tathāgata</s> qualities as indicated are to be followed in the order of their detailed exposition according to the <s>Sarvabuddhaviṣayāvatārajñānālokālaṃkārasūtra</s>. There, the statement 'There is no arising, no cessation, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>; the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One is thus' — by this, the <s>Tathāgata</s> as having the characteristic of the unconditioned is illuminated. Furthermore, immediately following, beginning with the illustration of the reflection-image on a <s>Vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) surface of <s>Śakra</s>, up to nine illustrations, addressing this very meaning of the <s>Tathāgata</s> as non-arising and non-ceasing, he says: 'Thus indeed, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One does not move, does not stir, does not proliferate, does not construct, does not discriminate. He is non-constructing, non-discriminating, without thought, without mental engagement, cooled, non-arising, non-ceasing, unseen, unheard, unsmelled, untasted, untouched, without signs, non-cognizable, not to be made known' — and so forth is the exposition of the divisions and aspects of pacification. By this, the <s>Tathāgata</s> as without deliberate effort (<s>anābhoga</s>) due to the pacification of all conceptual proliferation and discrimination in his own activities is illuminated. From that point onward, by the remaining text after the exposition of illustrations, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s awakening without dependence on others with respect to the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all <s>dharmas</s> is illuminated. Furthermore, at the end, having taught the sixteen aspects of <s>Tathāgata</s>-awakening, he says thus: 'There, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, having fully awakened to all such <s>dharmas</s> and having observed the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (element of reality) of beings as impure, unstainless, and with blemish, a great compassion called "sport" (<s>vikrīḍitā</s>) arises toward beings.'

body.text:
mahākaruṇā pravartata iti / anena tathāgatasyānuttarajñānakaruṇānvitatvamudbhāvitam / tatraivaṃrūpān sarvadharmāniti yathāpūrva nirdiṣṭānabhāvasvabhāvāt / abhisaṃbudhyeti yathābhūtamavikalpabuddhajñānena jñātvā / sattvānāmiti niyatāniyatamithyāniyatarāśivyavaśitānām / dharmadhātumiti svadharmatāprakṛtinirviśiṣṭattathāgatagarbham / vyavalokyeti sarvākāramanāvaraṇena buddhacakṣuṣā dṛṣṭvā / aśuddhaṃ kleśāvaraṇena bālapṛthagjanānām / avimalaṃ jñeyāvaraṇena śrāvakapratyekabuddhānām / sāṅganaṃ tadubhayānyatamaviśiṣṭatayā bodhisattvānām / vikrīḍitā vividhā saṃpannavinayopāyamukheṣu supraviṣṭatvāt / sattveṣu mahākaruṇā pravartata iti samatayā sarvasattvanimittamabhisaṃbuddhabodheḥ svadharmatādhigamasaṃprāpaṇāśayatvāt / yadita ūrdhvamanuttarajñānakaruṇāpravṛtterasamadharmacakrapravartanābhinirhāraprayogāśraṃsanamiyamanayoḥ parārthakaraṇe śaktirveditavyā / tatraiṣāmeva yathākramaṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ tathāgataguṇānāmādyaistribhirasaṃskṛtādibhiryogaḥ
svārthasaṃpat / tribhiravaśiṣṭairjñānādibhiḥ parārthasaṃpat / api khalu jñānena paramanityopaśāntipadasvābhisaṃbodhisthānaguṇāt svārthasaṃpat paridīpitā / karuṇāśaktibhyāmanuttaramahādharmacakrapravṛttisthānaguṇāt parārthasaṃpaditi /
body.translated_text: By this, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s endowment with unsurpassed knowledge and compassion is brought forth. There, 'all such <s>dharmas</s>' means those previously indicated as having the nature of non-existence. 'Having fully awakened' means having known through the <s>Buddha</s>'s non-discriminating knowledge as it truly is. 'Of beings' means those established in the determinate, indeterminate, and wrongly determinate classes. '<s>Dharmadhātu</s>' means the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> (Buddha-nature), undifferentiated from its own nature (<s>svadharmatā</s>) and innate character (<s>prakṛti</s>). 'Having observed' means having seen in every aspect with the unobstructed Buddha-eye. 'Impure' [refers to] the afflictive obstruction (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) of foolish ordinary beings (<s>bālapṛthagjana</s>). 'Unstainless' (<s>avimala</s>) [refers to] the cognitive obstruction (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>) of <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. 'With blemish' (<s>sāṅgaṇa</s>) [refers to] <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, by virtue of their being distinguished by one or both of those [obstructions]. 'Sport' (<s>vikrīḍitā</s>) means 'variegated,' because of being well-versed in the various gateways of skillful means for disciplining [beings]. 'Great compassion arises toward beings' — because [the <s>Tathāgata</s>], having awakened equally for the sake of all beings, intends to bring them to the realization of their own true nature (<s>svadharmatā</s>). From this point onward, the power of unsurpassed knowledge and compassion in accomplishing the benefit of others is to be understood as the unfailing effort of turning the incomparable Dharma-wheel. There, of these very six <s>Tathāgata</s> qualities in due order, with the first three — the unconditioned and so forth — the accomplishment of self-benefit is [achieved]; with the remaining three — knowledge and so forth — the accomplishment of the benefit of others. Moreover, through knowledge, self-benefit is illuminated by the quality of fully awakening to the supreme, permanent, peaceful state; through compassion and power, the benefit of others is illuminated by the quality of turning the unsurpassed great Dharma-wheel.

body.text: ato buddharatnāddharmaratnaprabhāvaneti tadanantaraṃ tadadhikṛtya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, from the Buddha-jewel [comes] the exposition of the Dharma-jewel; and following that, there is a verse (<s>śloka</s>) regarding this:

body.text:
yo nāsanna ca sanna cāpi sadasannānyaḥ sato nāsato
'sakyastarkayituṃ niruktyapagataḥ pratyātmavedyaḥ śivaḥ /
body.translated_text: He who is neither non-existent, nor existent, nor both existent-and-non-existent, nor other than existent or non-existent, who cannot be investigated by logic, who transcends etymological analysis, who is to be known through individual inner experience, who is auspicious —

body.text: tasmai dharmadivākarāya vimalajñānāvabhāsatviṣe
body.translated_text: To that Sun of <s>Dharma</s>, whose radiance is the illumination of stainless knowledge,

body.text: sarvāramvaṇa rāgadoṣatimiravyāghātakartre namaḥ // 9 //
body.translated_text: Who destroys the darkness of all obstructing passion and hatred — homage! ||9||

body.text: anena kiṃ darśitam /
body.translated_text: What is shown by this?

children.translated_text: By [the qualities of] inconceivability, non-duality, non-conceptuality, purity, manifestation, and opposition,

children.text: yo yena ca virāgo 'sau dharmaḥ satyadvilakṣaṇaḥ // 10 //
children.translated_text: That which [constitutes] dispassion (<s>virāga</s>) and that by which there is dispassion — that is the <s>Dharma</s>, characterized by the two truths. ||10||

body.text: anena samāsato 'ṣṭābhirguṇaiḥ saṃgṛhītaṃ dharmaratnamudbhāvitam / aṣṭau guṇāḥ katame / acintyatvamadvayatā nirvikalpatā śuddhirabhivyaktikaraṇaṃ pratiparkṣatā virāgo virāgaheturiti /
body.translated_text: By this, the Dharma-jewel (<s>dharmaratna</s>) endowed with eight qualities in brief is brought forth. What are the eight qualities? Inconceivability (<s>acintyatva</s>), non-duality (<s>advayatā</s>), non-conceptuality (<s>nirvikalpatā</s>), purity (<s>śuddhi</s>), making manifest (<s>abhivyaktikaraṇa</s>), being an antidote (<s>pratipakṣatā</s>), dispassion (<s>virāga</s>), and the cause of dispassion (<s>virāgahetu</s>).

children.translated_text: Dispassion (<s>virāgitā</s>) is encompassed by the truths of cessation (<s>nirodha</s>) and the path (<s>mārga</s>);
And these two [truths] are to be understood through three qualities each, in due order. ||11||

body.text: eṣāmeva yathākramaṃ ṣaṇṇāṃ guṇānāṃ tribhirādyairacintyādvayanirvikalpatāguṇairnirodhasatyaparidīpanādvirāgasaṃgraho veditavyaḥ / tribhiravaśiṣṭaiḥ śuddhyabhivyaktipratipakṣatāguṇairmārgasatyaparidīpanādvirāgahetusaṃgraha iti / yaśca virāgo nirodhasatyaṃ yena ca virāgo mārgasatyena tadubhayamabhisamasya vyavadānasatya dvayalakṣaṇo virāgadharma iti paridīpitam /
body.translated_text: Of these very six qualities in due order, through the first three — the qualities of inconceivability, non-duality, and non-conceptuality — the encompassing of dispassion is to be understood through the illumination of the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>). Through the remaining three — the qualities of purity, manifestation, and being an antidote — the encompassing of the cause of dispassion is to be understood through the illumination of the truth of the path (<s>mārgasatya</s>). That which is dispassion is the truth of cessation; that by which there is dispassion is the truth of the path. Uniting both of these, the <s>Dharma</s> of dispassion, characterized by the two truths of purification (<s>vyavadānasatya</s>), is illuminated.

children.translated_text: The inconceivability of [cessation truth is understood] from its being beyond logic, beyond verbal expression, and [accessible only to] noble knowledge;
Non-duality and non-conceptuality [arise] from its auspicious nature (<s>śivatva</s>); purity and the other three [qualities of the path truth] are like the sun. ||12||

body.text: samāsato nirodhasatyasya tribhiḥ kāraṇairacintyatvaṃ veditavyam / katamaistribhiḥ / asatsatsadasannobhayaprakāraiścaturbhirapi tarkāgocaratvāt / sarvarutaravitaghoṣavākpathaniruktisaṃketavyavahārābhilāpairanabhilāpyatvāt / āryāṇāṃ ca pratyātmavedanīyatvāt /
body.translated_text: In brief, the inconceivability of the truth of cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>) is to be understood through three reasons. Which three? Because it is beyond the range of logic in all four modes — [whether considered as] non-existent, existent, both existent-and-non-existent, or neither. Because it is inexpressible by all utterances, sounds, speech, verbal paths, etymologies, conventions, transactions, and designations. And because it is to be personally experienced by the noble ones (<s>āryas</s>).

body.text: tatra nirodhasatyasya kathamadvayatā nirvikalpatā ca veditavyā / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā / śivo 'yaṃ śāriputra dharmakāyo 'dvayadharmāvikalpadharmā / tatra dvayamucyate karma kleśāṃśca / vikalpa ucyate karmakleśasamudayaheturayoniśomanasikāraḥ / tatprakṛtinirodhaprativedhād dvayavikalpāsamudācārayogena yo duḥkhasyātyantamanutpāda idamucyate duḥkhanirodhasatyam / na khalu kasyaciddharmasya vināśādduḥkhanirodhasatyaṃ paridīpitam / yathoktam / anutpādānirodhe mañjuśrīścittamanovijñānāni na pravartante / yatra cittamanovijñānāni na pravartante tatra na kaścitparikalpo yena parikalpenāyoniśomanasikuryāt / sa yoniśomanasikārapra yukto 'vidyāṃ na samutvāpayati / yaccāvidyāsamutthānaṃ tad dvādaśānāṃ bhavāṅgānāmasamutthānam / sājātiriti vistaraḥ / yathoktam / na khalu bhagavan dharmavināśo duḥkhanirodhaḥ / duḥkhanirodhanāmnā bhagavannanādikāliko 'kṛto 'jāto 'nutpanno 'kṣayaḥ kṣayāpagataḥ nityo dhruvaḥ śivaḥ śāśvataḥ prakṛtipariśuddhaḥ sarvakleśakośavinirmukto gaṅgāvālikāvyativṛttairavinirbhāgairacintyairbuddhadharmaiḥ samanvāgatastathāgatadharmakāyo deśitaḥ / ayameva ca bhagavaṃstathāgatadharmakāyo 'vinirmuktakleśakośastathāgatagarbhaḥ sūcyate / iti sarvavistareṇa yathāsūtrameva duḥkhanirodhasatyavyavasthānamanugantavyam /
body.translated_text: There, how are the non-duality (<s>advayatā</s>) and non-conceptuality (<s>nirvikalpatā</s>) of the truth of cessation to be understood? As the Blessed One has said: 'This <s>Dharmakāya</s> is auspicious (<s>śiva</s>), O <s>Śāriputra</s>, a <s>dharma</s> of non-duality, a <s>dharma</s> of non-discrimination.' There, 'duality' is said to be <s>karma</s> (action) and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions). 'Discrimination' is said to be unwise mental engagement (<s>ayoniśomanasikāra</s>), which is the cause of the arising of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>. Through the penetration of the cessation of their nature, by the non-occurrence of duality and discrimination, the absolute non-arising of suffering — this is called the truth of the cessation of suffering (<s>duḥkhanirodhasatya</s>). It is not the case that the truth of the cessation of suffering is illuminated by the destruction of any <s>dharma</s>. As stated: 'In non-arising and non-cessation, O <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, mind (<s>citta</s>), mentation (<s>manas</s>), and cognition (<s>vijñāna</s>) do not operate. Where mind, mentation, and cognition do not operate, there is no construction by which one might engage in unwise mental engagement. One who is devoted to wise mental engagement does not produce ignorance (<s>avidyā</s>). And the non-arising of ignorance is the non-arising of the twelve limbs of existence (<s>bhavāṅga</s>). That is [the cessation of] birth' — and so on in detail. As stated: 'Indeed, O Blessed One, the cessation of suffering is not the destruction of <s>dharmas</s>. By the name "cessation of suffering," O Blessed One, what is taught is the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s> — beginningless, uncreated, unborn, unarisen, inexhaustible, free from decay, permanent, stable, auspicious, eternal, innately pure, liberated from the sheath of all afflictions, endowed with inconceivable Buddha-qualities that exceed the number of the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> and are inseparable [from it].' And this very <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s>, when not liberated from the sheath of afflictions, is indicated as the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s>. Thus, the entire detailed establishment of the truth of the cessation of suffering is to be followed just as [stated] in the <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: asya khalu duḥkhanirodhasaṃjñitasya tathāgatadharmakāyasya prāptiheturavikalpajñānadarśanabhāvanāmārgastrividhena sādharmyeṇa dinakarasadṛśaḥ veditavyaḥ / maṇḍalaviśuddhisādharmyeṇa sarvopakleśamalavigatatvāt / rūpābhidhyaktikaraṇasādharmyeṇa sarvākārajñeyāvabhāsakatvāt / tamaḥpratipakṣasādharmyeṇa ca sarvākārasatyadarśanavibandhapratipakṣabhūtatvāt /
body.translated_text: The cause of attaining this <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s> designated as 'cessation of suffering' — the path of cultivating non-discriminating knowledge and vision (<s>avikalpajñānadarśanabhāvanāmārga</s>) — is to be understood as resembling the sun through three points of similarity. Through similarity with the purity of the [sun's] disc, because it is free from all secondary defilements and stains. Through similarity with making forms manifest, because it illuminates all knowable objects in every aspect. And through similarity with being the antidote to darkness, because it is the actual antidote to all obstructions to seeing the truth in every aspect.

body.text: vibandha punarabhutavastunimittārambaṇamanasikārapūrvikā rāgadveṣamohotpattiranuśayaparyutthānayogāt / anuśayato hi bālānāma bhūtamatatsvabhāvaṃ vastu śubhākāreṇa vā nimittaṃ bhavati rāgotpattitaḥ / pratighākāreṇa vā dveṣotpattitaḥ / avidyākāreṇa vā mohotpattitaḥ / tacca rāgadveṣamohanimittamayathābhutamārambaṇaṃ kurvatāmayoniśomanasikāraścittaṃ paryādadāti / teṣāmayoniśomanasikāraparyavasthitacetasāṃ rāgadveṣamohānāmanyatakleśasamudācāro bhavati / te tatonidānaṃ kāyena vācā manasā rāgajamapi karmābhisaṃskurvanti / dveṣajamapi mohajamapi karmābhisaṃskurvanti / karmataśca punarjanmānubandha eva bhavati / evameṣāṃ bālānāmanuśayavatāṃ / nimittagrāhiṇāmārambaṇacaritānāmayoniśomanasikārasamudācārāt kleśasamudayaḥ / kleśamudāyāt karmasamudayaḥ / karmasamudayājjanmasamudayo bhavati / sa punareṣa sarvākārakleśakarmajanmasaṃkleśo bālānāmekasya dhātoryathābhūtamajñānādadarśanācca pravartate /
body.translated_text: The obstruction (<s>vibandha</s>), moreover, is the arising of passion (<s>rāga</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), and delusion (<s>moha</s>) preceded by mental engagement with unreal objects and signs, due to the influence of latent dispositions (<s>anuśaya</s>) and manifest afflictions (<s>paryutthāna</s>). For, due to latent dispositions, for the foolish, an unreal object whose nature is otherwise becomes a sign in a pleasant aspect, leading to the arising of passion; or in a repulsive aspect, leading to the arising of hatred; or in an aspect of ignorance, leading to the arising of delusion. And for those who make that sign of passion, hatred, and delusion an unreal object [of cognition], unwise mental engagement (<s>ayoniśomanasikāra</s>) seizes the mind. For those whose minds are overcome by unwise mental engagement, the manifest occurrence of one or another affliction — passion, hatred, or delusion — arises. From that cause, with body, speech, and mind, they construct <s>karma</s> born of passion, <s>karma</s> born of hatred, and <s>karma</s> born of delusion. And from <s>karma</s>, the continuation of rebirth indeed occurs. Thus, for these foolish ones who have latent dispositions, who grasp at signs, who pursue objects, from the occurrence of unwise mental engagement there is the arising of afflictions; from the arising of afflictions, the arising of <s>karma</s>; from the arising of <s>karma</s>, the arising of birth. And this entire defilement (<s>saṃkleśa</s>) of afflictions, <s>karma</s>, and birth in every aspect arises for the foolish from not knowing and not seeing one single element (<s>dhātu</s>) as it truly is.

body.text: sa ca tathā draṣṭavyo yathā parigaveṣayanna tasya kiṃcinnimittamārambaṇaṃ vā paśyati / sa yadā na nimittaṃ nārambaṇaṃ vā paśyati tadā bhūtaṃ paśyati / evamete dharmāstathāgatenābhisaṃbuddhāḥ samatayā samā iti / ya evamasataśca nimittārambaṇasyādarśanāt sataśca yathābhūtasya paramārthasatyasya darśanāt tadubhayoranutkṣepāprakṣepasamatājñānena sarvadharmasamatābhisaṃbodhaḥ so 'sya sarvākārasya tattvadarśanavibandhasya pratipakṣo veditavyo yasyodayāditarasyātyantamasaṃgatirasamavadhānaṃ pravartate / sa khalveṣa dharmakāyaprāptiheturavikalpajñānadarśanabhāvanāmārgo vistareṇa yathāsūtraṃ prajñāpāramitānusāreṇānugantavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: And he should be seen in such a way that, upon investigating, he sees neither any cause nor any object-support for it. When he sees neither cause nor object-support, then he sees reality. Thus these <s>dharmas</s> have been fully awakened to by the <s>Tathāgata</s> as equal through equality. He who, through the non-seeing of the unreal cause and object-support, and through the seeing of what is real — the ultimate truth as it truly is — through the knowledge of equality that neither affirms nor negates both: that complete awakening to the equality of all <s>dharmas</s> should be understood as the antidote to the totality of bondage to the seeing of reality, upon whose arising the other ceases entirely and finds no ground. This path of cultivating non-conceptual knowledge-vision (<s>avikalpajñānadarśana</s>), which is the cause for attaining the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, should be understood in detail according to the sūtra, following the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>.

body.text: ato mahāyānadharmaratnādavaivartikabodhisattvagaṇaratnaprabhāvaneti tadanantaraṃ tadadhikṛtya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: Therefore, from the Jewel of the <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s>, [we proceed to] the elucidation of the Jewel of the Assembly of Irreversible <s>Bodhisattvas</s> (<s>avaivartikabodhisattvagaṇaratna</s>). Subsequently, regarding that, the verse:

body.text: ye samyak pratividhya sarvajagato nairātmyakoṭiṃ śivāṃ
body.translated_text: Those who, having thoroughly penetrated the auspicious limit of selflessness (<s>nairātmyakoṭi</s>) of the entire world,

children.translated_text: through seeing the non-inherent nature of the defilements (<s>kleśa</s>) due to the natural luminosity (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvaratā</s>) of that mind,
with unobstructed understanding, see Buddhahood (<s>saṃbuddhatā</s>) pervading everywhere —
to those whose vision is the knowledge of the infinite domain of the purity of beings, homage! [13]

body.text: anena kiṃ darśitam /
body.translated_text: What is shown by this?

children.translated_text: Through the purity of inner knowledge-vision, both as to quality (<s>yathāvat</s>) and extent (<s>yāvat</s>),
the assembly (<s>gaṇa</s>) of the wise, irreversible ones, is endowed with unsurpassed qualities. [14]

body.text: anena samāsato 'vaivartikabodhisattvagaṇaratnasya dvābhyāmākārābhyāṃ yathāvadbhāvikatayā yāvadbhāvikatayā ca lokottarajñānadarśanaviśuddhito 'nuttaraguṇānvitatvamudbhāvitam /
body.translated_text: By this, in summary, it is shown that the Jewel of the Assembly of Irreversible <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is pervaded by unsurpassed qualities through the purity of supramundane knowledge-vision, in both its qualitative aspect (<s>yathāvadbhāvikatā</s>) and quantitative aspect (<s>yāvadbhāvikatā</s>).

children.translated_text: The qualitative aspect, through comprehension of the true nature (<s>dharmatā</s>) that pacifies that world,
through the natural purity [of mind], and through seeing the primordial exhaustion of the defilements. [15]

body.text: tatra yathāvadbhāvikatā kṛtsnasya pudgaladharmākhyasya jagato yathāvannairātmyakoṭerava gamādveditavyā / sa cāyamavagamo 'tyantādiśāntasvabhāvatayā pudgaladharmāvināśayogena samāsato dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmutpadyate / prakṛtiprabhāsvaratādarśanācca cittasyādikṣayanirodhadarśanācca tadupakleśasya / tatra yā cittasya
body.translated_text: Here, the qualitative aspect (<s>yathāvadbhāvikatā</s>) should be understood through the comprehension of the limit of selflessness of the entire world, designated as the selflessness of persons and <s>dharmas</s>, as it truly is. And this comprehension arises, in summary, from two causes — through the nature of being primordially and utterly pacified in essence, and through the non-destruction of persons and <s>dharmas</s>: from seeing the natural luminosity (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvaratā</s>) of mind, and from seeing the primordial exhaustion and cessation of its adventitious defilements. Here, [regarding] the

body.text: prakṛtiprabhāsvaratā yaśca tadupakleśa ityetad dvayamanāsravai dhātau kuśalākuśalayościttayorekecaratvād dvitīyacittānabhisaṃdhānayogena paramaduṣprativedhyam / ata āha / kṣaṇikuṃ bhagavan kuśalaṃ cittam / na kleśaiḥ saṃkliśyate / kṣaṇikamakuśalaṃ cittam / na saṃkliṣṭameva taccittaṃ kleśaiḥ / na bhagavan kleśāstaccittaṃ spṛśanti / kathamatra bhagavannasparśanadharmi cittaṃ tamaḥkliṣṭaṃ bhavati / asti ca bhagavannupakleśaḥ / astyupakliṣṭaṃ cittam / atha ca punarbhagavan prakṛtipariśuddhasya cittasyopakleśārtho duṣprativedhyaḥ / iti vistareṇa yathāvadbhāvikatāmārabhya duṣpratividhārthanirdeśo yathāsūtramanugantavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: natural luminosity of mind and its adventitious defilements — this pair is exceedingly difficult to penetrate in the undefiled element (<s>anāsravadhātu</s>), because wholesome and unwholesome minds operate as one, and thus by the method of not apprehending a second mind. Therefore [the Sūtra] says: 'Momentary, Blessed One, is a wholesome mind — it is not defiled by defilements. Momentary is an unwholesome mind — that mind itself is not defiled by defilements. Blessed One, the defilements do not touch that mind. How then, Blessed One, is the mind, whose nature is to be untouched, defiled by darkness? There is, Blessed One, adventitious defilement. There is an adventitiously defiled mind. And yet, Blessed One, the meaning of adventitious defilement of the naturally pure mind is difficult to penetrate.' Thus, in detail, the exposition of the difficult-to-penetrate meaning beginning with the qualitative aspect should be understood according to the sūtra.

children.translated_text: The quantitative aspect (<s>yāvadbhāvikatā</s>), through understanding that reaches the limit of all knowables,
is from seeing the existence of the nature of omniscience (<s>sarvajñadharmatā</s>) in all sentient beings. [16]

body.text: tatra yāvadbhāvikatā sarvajñeyavastuparyantagatayā lokottarayā prajñayā sarvasattveṣvantaśastiryagyonigateṣvapi tathāgatagarbhāstitvadarśanādveditavyā / tacca darśanaṃ bodhisattvasya prathamāyāmeva bodhisattvabhūmāvutpadyate sarvatragāthane dharmadhātuprativedhāt /
body.translated_text: Here, the quantitative aspect should be understood from seeing the existence of the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> (Buddha-nature) in all sentient beings — even including those in the animal realm — through supramundane wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) that has reached the limit of all knowable objects. And that vision arises for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> at the very first <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage (<s>bhūmi</s>), from the penetration of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> pervading everywhere.

body.text: ityevaṃ yo 'vabodhastatpratyātmajñānadarśanam /
body.translated_text: Thus, that awakening, which is inner personal knowledge-vision (<s>pratyātmajñānadarśana</s>),

body.text: tacchuddhiramale dhātāvasaṅgāpratighā tataḥ // 17 //
body.translated_text: that purity, in the stainless element (<s>amaladhātu</s>), free from attachment and obstruction — [arises] from that. [17]

body.text: ityevamanena prakāreṇa yathāvadbhāvikatayā ca yāvadbhāvikatayā ca yo lokottaramārgāvabodhastadāryāṇāṃ pratyātmamananyasādhāraṇaṃ lokottarajñānadarśanamabhipretam / tacca samāsato dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmitaprādeśikajñānadarśanamupanidhāya suviśuddhirityucyate / katamābhyāṃ dvābhyām / asaṅgatvādapratihatatvācca / tatra yathāvadbhāvikatayā sattvadhātuprakṛtiviśuddhaviṣayatvādasaṅgam yāvadbhāvikatayānantejñeyavastuviṣayatvādapratihatam /
body.translated_text: Thus, in this manner, the awakening of the supramundane path through both the qualitative and quantitative aspects — that supramundane knowledge-vision, personal and not shared with others, of the Noble Ones (<s>Āryas</s>) — is what is intended. And that, in summary, is called 'thoroughly pure' for two reasons, in comparison with limited knowledge-vision. Which two? Because it is unobstructed (<s>asaṅga</s>) and unimpeded (<s>apratihata</s>). Here, in terms of the qualitative aspect, it is unobstructed because its domain is the natural purity of the element of sentient beings; in terms of the quantitative aspect, it is unimpeded because its domain is the infinite knowable objects.

children.translated_text: Through the purity of knowledge-vision, being unsurpassed compared to the <s>Buddha</s>'s knowledge,
the Noble Ones, [being] irreversible, become the refuge of all embodied beings. [18]

body.text: itīyaṃ jñānadarśanaśuddhiravinivartanīyabhūmisamārūḍhānāṃ bodhisattvānāmanuttarāyāstathāgatajñānadarśanaviśuddherupaniṣadgatatvādanuttarā veditavyā tadanyebhyo vā dāna śīlādibhyo bodhisattvaguṇebhyo madyogādavinivartanīyā bodhisattvāḥ śaraṇa bhūtā bhavanti sarvasattvānāmiti /
body.translated_text: Thus this purity of knowledge-vision of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have ascended to the irreversible stage should be understood as unsurpassed, because it is proximate to the unsurpassed purity of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge-vision, or because, due to its meditative intensity, irreversible <s>Bodhisattvas</s> become a refuge for all sentient beings beyond [what is achieved by] other <s>Bodhisattva</s> qualities such as generosity and moral discipline.

body.text: śrāvakasaṃgharatnāgrahaṇaṃ bodhisattvagaṇaratnānantaraṃ tatpūjānarhatvāt / na hi jātu paṇḍitā bodhisattvaśrāvakaguṇāntarajñā mahābodhivipulapuṇyajñānasaṃbhārāpūryamāṇajñānakaruṇāmaṇḍalamaprameyasattvadhātugaṇasaṃtānāvabhāsapratyupasthitamanuttaratathāgatapūrṇacandra gamanānukūlamārgapratipannaṃ
body.translated_text: The Jewel of the <s>Śrāvaka Saṃgha</s> is not taken up after the Jewel of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> Assembly, because it is not worthy of such honor. For the wise who know the difference between <s>Bodhisattva</s> and <s>Śrāvaka</s> qualities would never, abandoning the <s>Bodhisattva</s> — who is like a new moon, set upon a path conducive to attaining the full moon of unsurpassed <s>Tathāgatahood</s>, whose maṇḍala of knowledge and compassion is being filled by the vast accumulations of merit and wisdom for great awakening, and who stands ready to illuminate the streams of immeasurable assemblies of sentient beings —

body.text: bodhisattvanavacandramutsṛjya prādeśikajñānaniṣṭhāgatamapi tārārūpavat svasaṃtānāvabhāsapratyupasthitaṃ śrāvakaṃ namasyanti / parahitakriyāśayaviśuddheḥ saṃniśrayaguṇenaiva hi prathamacittotpādiko 'pi bodhisattvo niranukrośamananyapoṣigaṇyamanāsravaśīlasaṃvaraviśuddhiniṣṭhāgatamāryaśrāvakamabhibhavati / prāgeva tadanyairdaśavaśitādibhirbodhisattvaguṇaiḥ / vakṣyati hi /
body.translated_text: pay homage to a <s>Śrāvaka</s> who, even though having reached the culmination of limited knowledge, is like a star, standing ready to illuminate only his own stream. For through the quality of the support alone — that is, the purity of the intention for benefiting others — even a <s>Bodhisattva</s> at the first generation of the thought [of awakening] surpasses a Noble <s>Śrāvaka</s> who has reached the culmination of the purity of the untainted moral discipline that is compassionless, incapable of nourishing others, and isolated. How much more so through other <s>Bodhisattva</s> qualities such as the ten masteries (<s>daśavaśitā</s>). For it will be said:

children.translated_text: He who maintains moral discipline for his own benefit alone, devoid of compassion for beings of bad conduct,
the self-centered one, pure through the wealth of morality — the Noble Ones do not call him one of pure moral conduct.
He who, having adopted morality, makes it a source of sustenance for others, like fire, wind, water, and earth,

children.text: kāruṇyamutpādya paraṃ pareṣu sa śīlavāṃstatpratirūpako 'nya iti //
children.translated_text: generating supreme compassion for others — he is the moral one; the other is merely his semblance.

body.text: tatra kenārthena kimadhikṛtya bhagavatā śaraṇatrayaṃ prajñaptam //
body.translated_text: Now, for what purpose and regarding what has the Blessed One established the Three Refuges?

children.translated_text: With reference to the Teacher, the Teaching, and the Disciples, addressing those of the three vehicles,
and those devoted to the three types of reverence, the Three Refuges have been established. [19]

body.text: buddhaḥ śaraṇamagryatvād dvipadānāmiti śāstṛguṇodbhāvanārthena buddhabhāvāyopagatān bodhisattvān pudgalān buddhe ca paramakārakriyādhimuktānadhikṛtya deśitaṃ prajñaptam /
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Buddha</s> is the supreme refuge among bipeds' — this has been taught and established with reference to persons who have set out for Buddhahood, namely <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, and those devoted to the highest reverence for the <s>Buddha</s>, for the purpose of elucidating the qualities of the Teacher.

body.text: dharmaḥ śaraṇamagryatvādvirāgāṇāmiti śāstṛḥ śāsana guṇodbhāvanārthena svayaṃ pratītya gambhīradharmānubodhāyopagatān pratyekabuddhayānikān pudgalān dharme ca paramakārakriyādhimuktānadhikṛtya deśitaṃ prajñaptam /
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Dharma</s> is the supreme refuge among those free from passion' — this has been taught and established with reference to persons who have set out for the awakening of the profound <s>Dharma</s> by themselves, namely those of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, and those devoted to the highest reverence for the <s>Dharma</s>, for the purpose of elucidating the qualities of the Teacher's Teaching.

body.text: saṃghaḥ śaraṇamagryatvādgaṇānāmiti śāstuḥ śāsane supratipannaśiṣyaguṇodbhāvanārthena parataḥ śravaghoṣasyānugamāyopagatān śrāvakayānikān pudgalān saṃghe ca paramakārākriyādhimuktānadhikṛtya deśitaṃ prajñaptam / ityanena samāsatastrividhenārthena ṣaṭ pudgalānadhikṛtya prabhedayo bhagavatā saṃvṛtipadasthānena sattvānāmanupūrvanayāvatārārthamimāni trīṇi śaraṇāni deśitāni prajñaptāni /
body.translated_text: 'The <s>Saṃgha</s> is the supreme refuge among assemblies' — this has been taught and established with reference to persons who have set out for following the spoken proclamation from another, namely those of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle, and those devoted to the highest reverence for the <s>Saṃgha</s>, for the purpose of elucidating the qualities of the well-practiced Disciples of the Teacher. Thus, in summary, through these three purposes, with reference to six types of persons, the Blessed One has taught and established these Three Refuges on the conventional level, for the purpose of gradually introducing sentient beings.

children.translated_text: Because of being abandonable, because of being deceptive in nature, because of non-existence, and because of being accompanied by fear,
the <s>Dharma</s> in both forms and the Noble <s>Saṃgha</s> are not ultimately the supreme refuge. [20]

body.text: dvividho dharmaḥ / deśanādharmo 'dhigamadharmaśca / tatra deśanādharmaḥ sūtrādideśanāyā nāmapadavyañjanakāyasaṃgṛhītaḥ / sa ca mārgābhisamayaparyavasānatvāt kolopama ityuktaḥ / adhigamadharmo hetuphalabhedena dvividhaḥ / yaduta mārgasatyaṃ nirodhasatyaṃ
body.translated_text: The <s>Dharma</s> is twofold: the <s>Dharma</s> of teaching and the <s>Dharma</s> of realization. The <s>Dharma</s> of teaching is comprised of the bodies of names, words, and syllables of the teachings such as the <s>sūtras</s>. And it has been called 'like a raft' because its culmination is the realization of the Path. The <s>Dharma</s> of realization is twofold, distinguished as cause and effect: namely, the Truth of the Path (<s>mārgasatya</s>) and the Truth of Cessation (<s>nirodhasatya</s>),

body.text: ca / yena yadadhigamyata iti kṛtvā / tatra mārgaḥ saṃskṛtalakṣaṇaparyāpannaḥ / yat saṃskṛtalakṣaṇaparyāpannaṃ tan mṛṣāmoṣadharmi / yan mṛṣāmoṣadharmi tadasatyam / yadasatyaṃ tadanityam / yadanityaṃ tadśaraṇam / yaśca tena mārgeṇa nirodho 'dhigataḥ so 'pi śrāvakanayena pradīpocchedavat kleśaduḥkhābhāvamātraprabhāvitaḥ / na cābhāvaḥ śaraṇamaśaraṇaṃ vā bhavitumarhati /
body.translated_text: since that by which that is realized [constitutes this division]. Here, the Path partakes of the characteristic of the conditioned. Whatever partakes of the conditioned characteristic is deceptive and false in nature. Whatever is deceptive is untrue. Whatever is untrue is impermanent. Whatever is impermanent is not a [true] refuge. And the cessation that is realized by that Path is also, according to the <s>Śrāvaka</s> method, characterized as merely the absence of defilements and suffering, like the extinguishing of a lamp. And non-existence cannot properly be either a refuge or a non-refuge.

body.text: saṃgha iti traiyānikasya gaṇasyaitadadhivacanam / sa ca nityaṃ sabhayastathāgataśaraṇagato niḥsaraṇaparyeṣī śaikṣaḥ sakaraṇīyaḥ pratipannakaścānuttarāyāṃ samyaksaṃbodhāviti / kathaṃ samayaḥ / yasmādarhatāmapi kṣīṇapunarbhavānāmaprahīṇatvādvāsaṃnāyāḥ satatasamitaṃ sarvāsaṃskāreṣu tīvrā bhayasaṃjñā pratyupasthitā bhavati syādyathāpi nāmotkṣiptāsike vadhakapuruṣe tasmātte 'pi nātyantasukhaniḥsaraṇamadhigatāḥ / na hi śaraṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ paryeṣate / yathaivā śaraṇāḥ sattvā yena tena bhayena bhītāstatastato niḥsaraṇaṃ paryeṣante tadvadarhatāmapyasti tadbhayaṃ yataste bhayādbhītāstathāgatameva śaraṇamupagacchanti / yaścaivaṃ sabhayatvāccharaṇamupagacchatyavaśyaṃ bhayānniḥsaraṇaṃ sa paryeṣyate / niḥsaraṇaparyeṣitvācca bhayanidānaprahāṇamadhikṛtya śaikṣo bhavati sakaraṇīyaḥ / śaikṣatvāt
body.translated_text: '<s>Saṃgha</s>' is the designation for the assembly of the three vehicles. And it is always accompanied by fear, having taken refuge in the <s>Tathāgata</s>, seeking escape, being a learner (<s>śaikṣa</s>), having work yet to be done, and being one who is practicing toward unsurpassed perfect awakening. How is it accompanied by fear? Because even for <s>Arhats</s>, those for whom rebirth is exhausted, since the latent dispositions have not been abandoned, there constantly arises an intense perception of fear regarding all conditioned things, as though a man stood with an upraised sword ready to kill. Therefore, even they have not attained ultimate happiness and escape. For a refuge does not seek refuge. Just as beings without refuge, frightened by this or that fear, seek escape from it — so too even for <s>Arhats</s> there exists that fear, frightened by which they take refuge in the <s>Tathāgata</s> alone. And one who thus, because of fear, takes refuge will necessarily seek escape from fear. Because of seeking escape, with reference to abandoning the cause of fear, one becomes a learner with work yet to be done. Because of being a learner,

body.text: pratipannako bhavatyabhayamāryabhasthānamanuprāptuṃ yadutānuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhim / tasmātso 'pi tadaṅgaśaraṇatvānnātyantaṃ śaraṇam / evamime dve śaraṇe paryantakāle śaraṇe ityucyete /
body.translated_text: one becomes a practitioner seeking to attain the fearless Noble state, namely unsurpassed perfect awakening. Therefore, even that [<s>Saṃgha</s>], being a refuge only in a partial sense, is not ultimately a refuge. Thus these two refuges are called 'refuges with a limit.'

children.translated_text: The sole refuge of the world is Buddhahood in the ultimate sense,
because the Sage has the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, and because the Assembly has that as its culmination. [21]

body.text: anena tu pūrvoktena vidhinānutpādānirodhaprabhāvitasya munervyavadānasatyadvayavirāgadharmakāyatvād dharmakāyaviśuddhiniṣṭhādhigamaparyavasānatvācca traiyānikasya gaṇasya pāramārthikamevātrāṇe 'śaraṇe loke 'parāntakoṭisamamakṣayaśaraṇaṃ nityaśaraṇaṃ dhruvaśaraṇaṃ yaduta tathāgatā arhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ / eva ca nityadhruvaśivaśāśvataikaśaraṇanirdeśo vistareṇāryaśrīmālāsūtrānusāreṇānugantavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: But by the previously stated method, because the Sage — characterized by non-arising and non-cessation — has a <s>Dharmakāya</s> free from the dual truth of purity and passion, and because the assembly of the three vehicles has as its culmination the attainment of the purity of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, the ultimate, imperishable, eternal, permanent, and stable refuge in this world without protection and without refuge — equal to the final limit [of time] — is none other than the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones. And this exposition of the single refuge that is permanent, stable, auspicious, and eternal should be understood in detail following the Noble <s>Śrīmālā Sūtra</s>.

children.translated_text: Because of their rare arising, because of their stainlessness, because of their power,
because of being ornaments of the world, because of their supremacy, and because of their changelessness — [22]

body.text: samāsataḥ ṣaḍvidhena ratnasādharmyeṇaitāni buddhadharmasaṃghākhyāni trīṇi ratnānyucyante / yaduta durlabhotpādabhāvasādharmyeṇa bahubhirapi kalpaparivarteranavāptakuśalamūlānāṃ tatsamavadhānāpratilambhāt / vaimalyasādharmyeṇa sarvācāramalavigatatvāt / prabhāvasādharmyeṇa ṣaḍabhijñādyacintyaprabhāvaguṇayogāt / lokālaṃkārasādharmyeṇa sarvajagadāśayaśobhānimittatvāt / ratnaprativarṇikāgryasādharmyeṇa lokottaratvāt / stutinindādyavikārasādharmyeṇāsaṃskṛtasvabhāvatvāditi /
body.translated_text: In brief, through sixfold similarity to gems, these three jewels called <s>Buddha</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Saṅgha</s> are spoken of. Namely: through the similarity of rare arising—because those who have not obtained roots of virtue (<s>kuśalamūla</s>) even over many aeon-cycles do not attain their encounter; through the similarity of stainlessness—because they are free from all defilements of conduct; through the similarity of power—because they possess the qualities of inconceivable powers such as the six superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>) and so forth; through the similarity of being an ornament of the world—because they are the cause of the beauty of the aspirations of all beings; through the similarity of being the foremost among counterfeits of gems—because they are supramundane; and through the similarity of being unaltered by praise and blame and such—because they are of unconditioned nature.

body.text: ratnatrayanirdeśānantaraṃ yasmin satyeva laukikalokottaraviṃśuddhiyoniratnatrayamutpadyate tadadhikṛtya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: After the exposition of the three jewels, regarding that upon the presence of which the jewel-triad arises as the source of mundane and supramundane purification, there is a verse:

children.text: samalā tathatātha nirmalā vimalāḥ buddhaguṇā jinakriyā /
children.translated_text: The <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) with defilements, then the stainless [suchness], the immaculate <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, and the activity of the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror)—
these are the domain of those who see the ultimate truth, because they are the source of the noble jewel-triad. // 23 //

body.text: anena kiṃ paridīpitam /
body.translated_text: What is illuminated by this?

children.translated_text: The <s>gotra</s> (lineage) of this jewel-triad is the domain of the all-seeing ones;
it is fourfold, and it is inconceivable for four reasons, in order. // 24 //

body.text: tatra samalā tathatā yo dhāturavinirmuktakleśakośastathāgatagarbha ityucyate / nirmalā tathatā sa eva buddhabhūmāvāśrayaparivṛttilakṣaṇo yastathāgatadharmakāye ityucyate / vimalabuddhaguṇā ye tasminnevāśrayaparivṛttilakṣaṇe tathāgatadharmakāye lokottarā daśabalādayo buddhadharmāḥ / jinakriyā teṣāmeva daśabalādīnāṃ buddhadharmāṇāṃ pratisvamanuttaraṃ karma yadaniṣṭhitamaviratamapratipraśrabdhaṃ bodhisattvavyākaraṇakathāṃ nopacchinatti / tāni punarimāni catvāri sthānāni yathāsaṃkhyameva caturbhiḥ kāraṇairacintyatvāt sarvajñaviṣayā ityucyante / katamaiścaturbhiḥ /
body.translated_text: There, the <s>tathatā</s> with defilements—the <s>dhātu</s> (element) not yet freed from the sheath of afflictions—is called <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> (embryo of the Tathāgata). The stainless <s>tathatā</s>—that very same [element], on the <s>Buddha</s>-stage, characterized by the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>)—is called the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>dharmakāya</s> (truth-body). The immaculate <s>Buddha</s>-qualities are those supramundane <s>Buddha</s>-qualities such as the ten powers (<s>daśabala</s>) and so forth, in that very <s>dharmakāya</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> characterized by the transformation of the basis. The activity of the <s>Jina</s> is the unsurpassed individual action of those very <s>Buddha</s>-qualities such as the ten powers—action that is unfinished, unceasing, and unrelaxing, and that does not cut off the discourse of prediction for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. These four topics are said to be the domain of the omniscient because they are inconceivable for four respective reasons. What are the four?

children.translated_text: Because of the conjunction of purity and defilement, because of purification without defilement,
because of having inseparable qualities, and because of being without effort and without conceptualization. // 25 //

body.text: tatra samalā tathatā yugapadekakālaṃ viśuddhā ca saṃkliṣṭā cetyacintyametat sthānaṃ gambhīradharmanayādhimuktānāmapi pratyekabuddhānāmagocaraviṣatvāt / yata
body.translated_text: There, the <s>tathatā</s> with defilements is simultaneously, at one time, both pure and defiled—this is an inconceivable topic, because even for <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> who have faith in the profound way of <s>Dharma</s>, it is beyond their domain. Because

body.text: āha / dvāvimau devi dharmau duṣprativedhyau / prakṛtipariśuddhicittaṃ duṣprativedhyam / tasyaiva cittasyopakliṣṭatā duṣprativedhyā / anayordevi dharmayoḥ śrotā tvaṃ vā bhaverathavā mahādharmasamanvāgatā bodhisattvāḥ / śeṣāṇāṃ devi sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāṃ tathāgataśraddhāgamanīyā vevaito dharmāviti /
body.translated_text: he said: 'O <s>Devī</s>, these two <s>dharmas</s> are difficult to penetrate: the mind that is naturally pure (<s>prakṛtipariśuddhacitta</s>) is difficult to penetrate, and the defilement of that very mind is difficult to penetrate. O <s>Devī</s>, the listener of these two <s>dharmas</s> may be you yourself or <s>Bodhisattvas</s> endowed with the great <s>Dharma</s>. For all the remaining <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, O <s>Devī</s>, these two <s>dharmas</s> are to be approached through faith in the <s>Tathāgata</s>.'

body.text: tatra nirmalā tathatā pūrvamalāsaṃkliṣṭā paścādviśuddhetyacintyametat sthānam / yat āha / prakṛtiprabhāsvaraṃ cittam / tattathaiva jñānam / tata ucyate / ekakṣaṇalakṣaṇasamāyuktayā prajñayā samyaksaṃbodhirabhisaṃbuddheti /
body.translated_text: There, the stainless <s>tathatā</s>—previously not defiled by defilements, subsequently purified—this is an inconceivable topic. Because he said: 'The mind is naturally luminous (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvara</s>).' That is precisely <s>jñāna</s> (knowledge). Therefore it is said: 'With <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) endowed with the characteristic of a single moment, perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) is fully awakened.'

body.text: tatra vimalā buddhaguṇāḥ paurvāparyeṇaikāntasaṃkliṣṭāyāmapi pṛthagjanabhūmāvavinirbhāgadharmatayā nirviśiṣṭā vidyanta ityacintyametat sthānam / yat āha /
body.translated_text: There, the immaculate <s>Buddha</s>-qualities exist even on the ordinary person's stage (<s>pṛthagjanabhūmi</s>), which is thoroughly defiled from first to last, as inseparable qualities without distinction—this is an inconceivable topic. Because he said:

body.text: na sa kaścitsattvaḥ sattvanikāye saṃvidyate yatra tathāgatajñānaṃ na sakalamanupraviṣṭam / api tu saṃjñāgrāhatastathāgatajñānaṃ na prajñāyate / saṃjñāgrāhavigamāt punaḥ sarvajñajñānaṃ svayaṃbhūjñānamasaṅgataḥ prabhavati / tadyathāpi nāma bho jinaputra trisāhasramahāsahasralokadhātupramāṇaṃ mahāpustaṃ bhavet / tasmin khalu punarmahāpuste trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātuḥ sakalasamāpta ālikhito bhavet / mahāpṛthivīpramāṇena mahāpṛthivī / dvisāhasralokadhātupramāṇena dvisāhasralokadhātuḥ / sāhasralokadhātupramāṇena sāhasralokadhātuḥ / cāturdvīpikapramāṇena cāturdvīpikāḥ / mahāsamudrapramāṇena mahāsamudrāḥ / jambūdvīpapramāṇena jambūdvīpāḥ / pūrvavidehadvīpapramāṇena pūrvavidehadvīpāḥ / godāvarīdvīpapramāṇena godāvarīdvīpāḥ / uttarakurudvīpapramāṇenottarakurudvīpāḥ / sūmerupramāṇena sumeravaḥ /
body.translated_text: 'There is no being in the multitude of beings in whom the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge has not fully entered. But due to the grasping of concepts, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge is not recognized. When the grasping of concepts is removed, the all-knowing knowledge, the self-born knowledge, arises from non-attachment. Just as, O son of the <s>Jina</s>, there might be a great book the size of the trichiliocosm (<s>trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātu</s>). In that great book, the trichiliocosm would be fully depicted: the great earth the size of the great earth, the dichiliocosm the size of the dichiliocosm, the chiliocosm the size of the chiliocosm, the four-continent systems the size of the four-continent systems, the great oceans the size of the great oceans, <s>Jambudvīpa</s> the size of <s>Jambudvīpa</s>, <s>Pūrvavideha</s> the size of <s>Pūrvavideha</s>, <s>Godāvarī</s> the size of <s>Godāvarī</s>, <s>Uttarakuru</s> the size of <s>Uttarakuru</s>, <s>Sumeru</s> the size of <s>Sumeru</s>,

body.text: bhūmyavacaradevavimānapramāṇena bhūmyavacaradevavimānāni / kāmāvacaradevavimānapramāṇena kāmāvacaradevavimānāni / rūpāvacaradevavimānapramāṇena rūpāvacaradevavimānāni / tacca mahāpustaṃ trisāhasramahāsāhasralokadhātvāyāmavistarapramāṇaṃ bhavet / tatkhālu punarmahāpustamekasmin paramāṇurajasi prakṣiptaṃ bhavet / yathā caikaparamāṇurajasi tanmahāpustaṃ prakṣiptaṃ bhavet tathānyeṣu sarvaparamāṇurajaḥsu tatpramāṇānyeva mahāpustānyabhyantarapraviṣṭāni bhaveyuḥ / atha kaścideva puruṣa utpadyate paṇḍito nipuṇo vyakto medhāvī tatropagamikayā mīmāṃsayā samanvāgataḥ divyaṃ cāsya cakṣuḥ samantapariśuddhaṃ prabhāsvaraṃ bhavet / sa divyena cakṣuṣā vyavalokayati / idaṃ mahāpustamevaṃbhūtamihaiva parītte paramāṇurajasyanitiṣṭhataṃ / na kasyacidapi sattvasyopakāritbhūtaṃ bhavati / tasyaivaṃ syāt / yannvahaṃ mahāvīryabalasthāmnā etatparamāṇurajo bhittvā etanmahāpustaṃ sarvajagadupajīvyaṃ kuryām / sa mahāvīryabalasthāma saṃjanayitvā sūkṣmeṇa vajreṇa tatparamāṇurajo bhittvā yathābhiprāyaṃ tanmahāpustaṃ sarvajagadupajīvyaṃ kuryāt / yathā caikasmāt tathāśeṣebhyaḥ paramāṇubhyastathaiva kuryāt / evameva bho jinaputra tathāgatajñānamapramāṇajñānaṃ sarvasattvopajīvyajñānaṃ sarvasattvacittasaṃtāneṣu sakalamanupraviṣṭam / sarvāṇi ca tāni sattvacittasaṃtānānyapi tathāgatajñānapramāṇāni / atha ca punaḥ saṃjñāgrāhavinivaddhā
body.translated_text: the palaces of the earth-dwelling gods the size of the palaces of the earth-dwelling gods, the palaces of the desire-realm gods the size of the palaces of the desire-realm gods, the palaces of the form-realm gods the size of the palaces of the form-realm gods. And that great book would be the length and breadth of the trichiliocosm. Now that great book would be placed within a single atom. And just as that great book is placed in one atom, so too in all other atoms, books of exactly the same size would be entered within. Then a certain man might arise—wise, skillful, clear-sighted, intelligent, endowed with the capacity for investigation—and his divine eye would be completely purified and luminous. With that divine eye he would examine and [say]: "This great book of such a kind abides right here within this minute atom. It is of no benefit to any being." The thought would occur to him: "Let me, with great heroic strength and power, split open this atom and make this great book available for the benefit of the entire world." Having generated great heroic strength and power, with a subtle <s>vajra</s> he would split open that atom and, as intended, make that great book available for the benefit of the entire world. And just as from one [atom], so from all remaining atoms he would do likewise. Even so, O son of the <s>Jina</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge—immeasurable knowledge, knowledge to be relied upon by all beings—has fully entered the mind-streams of all beings. And all those mind-streams of beings are of the same measure as the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge. But bound by the grasping of concepts,

body.text: bālā na jānanti na prajānanti nānubhavanti na sākṣātkurvanti tathāgatajñānam / tatastathāgato 'saṅgeṇa tathāgatajñānena sarvadharmadhātusattvabhavanāni vyavalokyācāryasaṃjñī bhavati / aho bata ime sattvā yathāvat tathāgatajñānaṃ na prajānanti / tathāgatajñānānupraviṣṭāśca / yannvahameṣā sattvānāmāryeṇa mārgopadeśena sarvasaṃjñākṛtabandhanāpanayanaṃ kuryā yathā svayamevāryamārgabalādhānena mahatīṃ saṃjñāgranthiṃ vinivartya tathāgatajñānaṃ pratyabhijānīran / tathāgatasamatāṃ cānuprāpnuyaḥ / te tathāgatamārgopadeśena sarvasaṃjñākṛtabandhanāni vyapanayanti / apanīteṣu ca sarvasaṃjñākṛtabandhaneṣu tat tathāgatajñānama pramāṇaṃ bhavati sarvajagadupajīvyamiti /
body.translated_text: the foolish do not know, do not understand, do not experience, do not directly realize the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge. Then the <s>Tathāgata</s>, with unattached <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge, surveying all the realms of beings in the <s>dharmadhātu</s>, conceives the thought of a teacher: "Alas! These beings do not understand the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge as it truly is, even though they are permeated by the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge. Let me, through the instruction of the noble path, bring about the removal of all bonds created by concepts for these beings, so that through the power of the noble path itself, having removed the great knot of concept-grasping, they may recognize the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge and attain equality with the <s>Tathāgata</s>." Through the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s instruction of the path, they remove all bonds created by concepts. And when all bonds created by concepts have been removed, that <s>Tathāgata</s>-knowledge becomes immeasurable and available for the benefit of the entire world.'
