body.text: tatra jinakriyā yugapatsarvatra sarvakālamanābhogenāvikalpato yathāśayeṣu yathāvainayikeṣu sattveṣvakṣūṇamanuguṇaṃ pravartata ityacintyametat sthānam / yata āha / saṃkṣepamātrakeṇāvatāraṇārthaṃ sattvānāmapramāṇamapi tathāgatakarma pramāṇato nirdiṣṭam / api tu kulaputra yattathāgatasya bhūtaṃ tathāgatakarma tadapramāṇamacintyamavijñeyaṃ sarvalokena / anudāharaṇamakṣaraiḥ / duḥsaṃpādaṃ parebhyaḥ / adhiṣṭhitaṃ sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu / samatānugataṃ sarvabuddhaiḥ / samatikrāntaṃ sarvābhogakriyābhyaḥ / nirvikalpamākāśasamatayā / nirnītākāraṇaṃ dharmadhātukriyayā / iti vistareṇa yāvadviśuddhavaiḍūryamaṇiduṣṭāntaṃ kṛtvā nirdiśati / tadanena kulaputra paryāyeṇaivaṃ veditavyamacintyaṃ tathāgatakarma samatānugataṃ ca sarvato 'navadyaṃ ca triratnavaṃśanupacchettṛ ca / yatrācintye tathāgatakarmaṇi pratiṣṭhitastathāgata ākāśasvabhāvatāṃ ca kāyasya na vijahāti
body.translated_text: There, the activity of the <s>Jina</s>—simultaneously, everywhere, at all times, without effort, without conceptualization, in accordance with the dispositions and trainability of beings, it operates without diminution and in accord—this is an inconceivable topic. Because he said: 'For the purpose of introducing beings, even the immeasurable <s>Tathāgata</s>-activity has been taught in a measured way, in mere summary. But, O son of good family, the actual <s>Tathāgata</s>-activity of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is immeasurable, inconceivable, unknowable by all the world, unillustrable by words, difficult for others to attain, established in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields, followed by equality with all <s>Buddhas</s>, transcending all effortful activities, without conceptualization through equality with space, with its manner removed through the activity of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>,' and so on in detail, up to the illustration with the simile of the pure <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gem. 'By this method, O son of good family, one should understand that the <s>Tathāgata</s>-activity is inconceivable, followed by equality [with all Buddhas], faultless in all respects, and does not interrupt the lineage of the Three Jewels. And in this inconceivable <s>Tathāgata</s>-activity, the <s>Tathāgata</s>, while established [therein], does not abandon the space-like nature of [his] body,'

body.text: sarvabuddhakṣetreṣu ca darśanaṃ dadāti / anabhilāpyadharmatāṃ ca vāco na vijahāti yathārutavijñaptyā ca sattvebhyo dharmaṃ deśayati / sarvacittārambaṇavigataśca sarvasattvacittacaritāśayāṃśca prajānātiti /
body.translated_text: 'and gives visions in all <s>Buddha</s>-fields; does not abandon the inexpressible nature of speech, and teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings through communication as heard; is free from all mental objects, and yet knows the conduct of minds and the dispositions of all beings.'

children.translated_text: <s>Bodhi</s> (awakening), the limbs of awakening (<s>bodhyaṅga</s>), and the act of awakening (<s>bodhana</s>)—in order,
one term is the cause, three are the conditions for its purification. // 26 //

body.text: eṣāṃ khalvapi caturṇāmarthapadānāṃ sarvajñeyasaṃgrahamupādāya prathamaṃ boddhavyapadaṃ draṣṭavyam / tadanubodho bodhiriti dvitīyaṃ bodhipadam / bodheraṅgabhūtā buddhaguṇā iti tritīyaṃ bodhyaṅgapadam / bodhyaṅgaireva bodhanaṃ pareṣāmiti caturtha bodhanāpadam / itīmāni catvāri padānyadhikṛtya hetupratyayabhāvena ratnatrayagotravyavasthānaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: Of these four meaning-terms, in terms of encompassing all that is to be known, the first is to be seen as the term 'that which is to be awakened to' (<s>boddhavya</s>). The awakening to that is <s>bodhi</s>—the second term. The <s>Buddha</s>-qualities that are the limbs of awakening—the third term, <s>bodhyaṅga</s>. The awakening of others through those very limbs of awakening—the fourth term, <s>bodhana</s>. With reference to these four terms, the establishment of the <s>gotra</s> (lineage) of the Three Jewels is to be understood in terms of cause and condition.

body.text: tatraiṣāṃ caturṇāṃ padānāṃ prathamaṃ lokottaradharmavijatvāt pratyātmayoniśomanasikārasaṃniśrayeṇa tadviśuddhimupādāya triratnotpattiheturanugantavyaḥ / ityevamekaṃ padaṃ hetuḥ / kathaṃ trīṇi pratyayaḥ / tathāgato 'nuttarāṃ samyaksaṃbodhimabhisaṃbudhya daśabalādibhirbuddhadharmerdvātriśadākāraṃ tathāgatakarma kurvan parato ghoṣasaṃniśrayeṇa tadviśuddhimupādāya triratnotpattipratyayo 'nugantavyaḥ / ityevaṃ trīṇi pratyayaḥ / ataḥ parameṣāmeva caturṇā padānāmanupūrvamavaśiṣṭena granthena vistaravibhāganirdeśo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, the first of these four terms, because it is the seed of supramundane <s>dharmas</s>, is to be understood as the cause of the arising of the Three Jewels, through its purification by relying on individual, thorough mental attention (<s>yoniśomanasikāra</s>). Thus one term is the cause. How are three the conditions? The <s>Tathāgata</s>, having fully awakened to unsurpassed perfect awakening, performing the thirty-two aspects of <s>Tathāgata</s>-activity with <s>Buddha</s>-qualities such as the ten powers, is to be understood as the condition for the arising of the Three Jewels, through its purification by relying on the voice of another. Thus three are the conditions. Hereafter, the detailed and classified exposition of these very four terms, in sequence, is to be understood through the remaining text.

body.text: tatra samalāṃ tathatāmadhikṛtya yaduktaṃ sarvasattvāstathāgatagarbhā iti tat kenārthena /
body.translated_text: There, with reference to the <s>tathatā</s> with defilements, the statement 'All beings are <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>'—in what sense [is this said]?

body.text: buddhajñānāntargamāt sattvarāśestannairmalyasyādvayatvāt prakṛtyā /
body.translated_text: Because the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s knowledge has entered all beings, because that stainlessness is non-dual by nature,

body.text: bauddhe gotre tatphalasyopacārāduktāḥ sarve dehino buddhagarbhāḥ // 27 //
body.translated_text: and because the fruit [of Buddhahood] is metaphorically attributed to the <s>Buddha</s>-<s>gotra</s> (lineage)—all embodied beings are said to be <s>buddhagarbha</s> (possessing the Buddha-embryo). // 27 //

children.translated_text: Because the body of the perfectly awakened one pervades [all], because <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) is undifferentiated,
and because of the <s>gotra</s> (lineage), all embodied beings are always <s>buddhagarbha</s>. // 28 //

body.text: samāsatastrividhenārthena sadā sarvasattvāstathāgatagarbhā ityuktaṃ bhagavatā / yaduta sarvasattveṣu tathāgatadharmakāyaparispharaṇārthena tathāgatatathatāvyatibhedārthena tathāgatagotrasaṃbhavārthena ca / eṣāṃ punastrayāṇāmarthapadānāmutaratra tathāgatagarbhasūtrānusāreṇa nirdeśo bhaviṣyati / pūrvataraṃ tu yenārthena sarvatrāviśeṣeṇa pravacane sarvākāraṃ tadarthasūcanaṃ bhavati tadapyādhikṛtya nirdekṣyāmi / uddānam /
body.translated_text: In brief, the <s>Bhagavān</s> has said 'All beings are always <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>' in three senses: namely, in the sense that the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>dharmakāya</s> pervades all beings, in the sense that the <s>tathatā</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> is undifferentiated [in all], and in the sense that the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> arises from the <s>Tathāgata</s>-<s>gotra</s>. The exposition of these three meaning-terms will follow later in accordance with the <s>Tathāgatagarbhasūtra</s>. But first, I shall also address that sense in which, everywhere without distinction in the teachings, there is the indication of that meaning in all its aspects, with reference to that. Summary:

children.translated_text: In nature, cause, fruit, action, union, manifestation, stages, and in all-pervasiveness,
in eternal unchangeability, in qualities, and in non-difference—the convergence of meaning regarding the ultimate element (<s>paramārthadhātu</s>) is to be known. // 29 //

body.text: samāsato daśavidhamarthamabhisaṃdhāya paramatattvajñānāviṣayasya tathāgatadhātorvyavasthānamanugantavyam / daśavidho 'rthaḥ katamaḥ / tadyathā svabhāvārtho hetvarthaḥ phalārthaḥ karmārtho yogārtho vṛtyartho 'vasthāprabhedārthaḥ sarvatragārtho 'vikārārtho 'bhedārthaśca / tatra svabhāvarthaṃ hetvartha cārabhya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: In brief, having intended a tenfold meaning, the establishment of the <s>Tathāgatadhātu</s>, which is beyond the domain of knowledge of ultimate reality, is to be understood. What is the tenfold meaning? Namely: the meaning of nature (<s>svabhāva</s>), the meaning of cause (<s>hetu</s>), the meaning of fruit (<s>phala</s>), the meaning of action (<s>karma</s>), the meaning of union (<s>yoga</s>), the meaning of manifestation (<s>vṛtti</s>), the meaning of the division of stages (<s>avasthāprabheda</s>), the meaning of all-pervasiveness (<s>sarvatraga</s>), the meaning of unchangeability (<s>avikāra</s>), and the meaning of non-difference (<s>abheda</s>). Regarding the meaning of nature and the meaning of cause, a verse:

children.translated_text: Always naturally undefiled, like a pure jewel, sky, and water,
[it] accords with faith in the <s>Dharma</s> (<s>dharmādhimukti</s>), superior wisdom (<s>adhiprajñā</s>), <s>samādhi</s>, and compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>). // 30 //

body.text: tatra pūrveṇaṃ ślokārthena kiṃ darśayati /
body.translated_text: There, what does the meaning of the preceding verse show?

children.translated_text: By the nature of power, unchangeability, and tenderness,
in these [three], the similarity with the qualities of the wish-fulfilling gem, space, and water [is to be known]. // 31 //

body.text: ya ete trayo 'tra pūrvamuddiṣṭā eṣu triṣu yathāsaṃkhyameva svalakṣaṇaṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇaṃ cārabhya tathāgatadhātościntāmaṇinabhovāriviśuddhiguṇasādharmyaṃ veditavyam / tatra tathāgatadharmakāye tāvaccintitārthasamuddhayādi prabhāvasvabhāvatāṃ svalakṣaṇamārabhya cintāmaṇiratnasādharmyaṃ veditavyam / tathatāyāmananyathābhāvasvabhāvatāṃ svalakṣaṇamārabhyākāśasādharmyaṃ veditavyam / tathāgatagotre sattvakaruṇāsnigdhasvabhāvatāṃ svalakṣaṇamārabhya vārisādharmya veditavyam / sarveṣāṃ cātra sadātyantaprakṛtyanupakliṣṭatāṃ prakṛtipariśuddhiṃ sāmānyalakṣaṇāmārabhya tadeva cintāmaṇinabhovāriviśuddhiguṇasādharmyaṃ veditavyam /
body.translated_text: Those three that were previously indicated here—in these three, in corresponding order, with reference to their specific and general characteristics, the similarity of the <s>Tathāgatadhātu</s> with the purity-qualities of the wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>), space (<s>nabhas</s>), and water (<s>vāri</s>) is to be understood. There, regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s> first, with reference to the specific characteristic of having the nature of power (<s>prabhāva</s>) such as the accomplishment of desired aims, the similarity with the wish-fulfilling gem is to be understood. Regarding <s>tathatā</s> (suchness), with reference to the specific characteristic of having the nature of unchangeability (<s>ananyathābhāva</s>), the similarity with space is to be understood. Regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>gotra</s> (lineage), with reference to the specific characteristic of having the nature of tenderness (<s>snigdhabhāva</s>) through compassion for beings, the similarity with water is to be understood. And for all of them here, with reference to the general characteristic of being always and utterly naturally undefiled—natural purity (<s>prakṛtipariśuddhi</s>)—that very similarity with the purity-qualities of the wish-fulfilling gem, space, and water is to be understood.

body.text: tatra pareṇa ślokārdhena kiṃ darśitam /
body.translated_text: There, what has been shown by the following half-verse?

children.translated_text: The fourfold obstruction [consists of]: hostility toward the <s>Dharma</s>, the view of self,
fear of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, and indifference toward the welfare of beings. // 32 //
Of <s>icchantikas</s>, <s>tīrthikas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and the self-born [<s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>],
the qualities beginning with faith (<s>adhimukti</s>) are the four causes of purification. // 33 //

body.text: samāsata ime trividhāḥ sattvāḥ sattvarāśau saṃvidyante / bhavābhilāṣiṇo vibhavābhilāṣiṇastadubhayānabhilāṣiṇaśca / tatra bhavābhilāṣiṇo dvividhā veditavyāḥ /
body.translated_text: In brief, these three types of beings are found in the mass of beings: those desiring existence (<s>bhavābhilāṣin</s>), those desiring non-existence (<s>vibhavābhilāṣin</s>), and those desiring neither of the two. There, those desiring existence are to be known as twofold.

body.text: mokṣamārgapratihatāśa aparinirvāṇagotrakāḥ sattvā ye saṃsāramevecchanti na nirvāṇaṃ tanniyatipatitāścehadhārmikā eva / tadekatyā mahāyānadharmavidviṣo yānadhikṛtyataduktaṃ bhagavatā / nāhaṃ teṣāṃ śāstā na te mama śrāvakāḥ / tānahaṃ śāriputra tamasastamo 'ntaramandhakārān mahāndhakāragāminastamobhūyiṣṭhā iti vadāmi /
body.translated_text: Those beings who are obstructed from the path of liberation, of the lineage that will not attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s> (<s>aparinirvāṇagotra</s>), who desire only <s>saṃsāra</s> and not <s>nirvāṇa</s>—they have fallen into fixity and are indeed followers of this [Buddhist] <s>Dharma</s>. Some among them are haters of the <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s>; with reference to their vehicle, the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'I am not their teacher, and they are not my disciples.' 'I say of them, <s>Śāriputra</s>, that from darkness they go to further darkness, from blindness to great blindness—they are deeply immersed in darkness.'

body.text: tatra vibhavābhilāṣiṇo dvividhāḥ / anupāyapatitā upāyapatitāśca / tatrānupāyapatitāḥ api trividhāḥ / itobāhyā bahunānāprakārāścakaparibrājakanigranthiputraprabhṛtayo 'nyatīrthyāḥ / ihadhārmikāśca tatsabhāgacaritā eva śrāddhā api durgṛhītagrāhiṇaḥ / te ca punaḥ katame / yaduta pudgaladṛṣṭayaśca paramārthānadhimuktā yān prati bhagavatā śūnyatānadhimukto nirviśiṣṭo bhavati tīrthikairityuktam / śūnyatādṛṣṭayaścābhimānikā yeṣāmiha tadvimokṣamukhe 'pi śūnyatāyāṃ mādyamānānāṃ śūnyataiva dṛṣṭirbhavati yānadhikṛtyāha / varaṃ khalu kāśyapa sumerumātrā pudgaladṛṣṭirna tvevābhimānikasya śūnyatādṛṣṭiriti / tatropāyapatitā api dvividhāḥ / śrāvakayānīyāśca samyaktvaniyāmamavakrāntāḥ pratyekabuddhayānīyāśca /
body.translated_text: There, those desiring non-existence are twofold: those fallen into wrong means (<s>anupāyapatita</s>) and those fallen into [correct] means (<s>upāyapatita</s>). There, those fallen into wrong means are also threefold: external to this [teaching], the many various non-Buddhist <s>tīrthikas</s> such as wandering ascetics (<s>parivrājakas</s>), <s>Nirgrantha</s>-sons, and so forth; and those who follow this <s>Dharma</s> yet conduct themselves similarly [to the outsiders]—even those with faith who grasp wrongly. And who are they? Namely, those with the view of a person (<s>pudgaladṛṣṭi</s>) who lack faith in the ultimate, regarding whom the <s>Bhagavān</s> said: 'One without faith in emptiness is no different from a <s>tīrthika</s>.' And the conceited ones with views of emptiness, for whom, even in this gate of liberation through emptiness, being intoxicated, emptiness itself becomes a [wrong] view—regarding which he said: 'Indeed, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, a view of a person as large as [Mount] <s>Sumeru</s> is better than the view of emptiness held by a conceited one.' There, those fallen into [correct] means are also twofold: those of the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle who have entered the certainty of rightness (<s>samyaktvaniyāma</s>), and those of the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle.

body.text: tadubhayānābhilāṣiṇaḥ punarmahāyānasaṃprasthitāḥ paramatīkṣṇendriyāḥ sattvā ye nāpi saṃsāramicchanti yathecchantikā nānupāyapatitāstīrthikādivan nāpyupāyapatitāḥ śrāvakapratyekabuddhavat / api tu saṃsāranirvāṇasamatāpatti mārgapratipannāste bhavantyapratiṣṭhitanirvāṇāśayā nirupakliṣṭasaṃsāragataprayogā dṛḍhakaruṇādhyāśayapratiṣṭhitamūlapariśuddhā iti /
body.translated_text: Those desiring neither of the two, moreover, are beings who have set forth on the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, of supremely sharp faculties, who do not desire <s>saṃsāra</s> as do <s>icchantikas</s>, who have not fallen into wrong means like the <s>tīrthikas</s> and others, nor fallen into [limited] means like <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>; but rather, having entered the path of the attainment of the equality of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, they have the intention of non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>), their practice while going through <s>saṃsāra</s> is undefiled, and they are established in root-purity through the firm superior intention of compassion.

body.text: tatra ye sattvā bhavābhilāṣiṇa icchantikāstanniyatipatitā ihadhārmikā evocyante mithyātvaniyataḥ sattvarāśiriti / ye vibhavābhilāṣiṇo 'pyanupāyapatitā ucyante 'niyataḥ sattvarāśiriti / ye vibhavābhilāṣiṇa upāyapatitāstadubhayānabhilāṣiṇaśca samatāptimārgapratipannāsta ucyatte samyaktvaniyataḥ sattvarāśiriti / tatra mahāyānasaṃprasthitān sattvānanāvaraṇagāminaḥ sthāpayitvā ya ito 'nye sattvāstadyathā / icchantikāstīrthyāḥ śrāvakāḥ pratyekabuddhāśca / teṣāmimāni catvāryāvaraṇāni tathāgatadhātoranadhigamāyāsākṣātkriyāyaisaṃvartante / katamāni ca catvāri / tadyathā mahāyānadharmapratigha icchantikānāmāvaraṇa yasya pratipakṣo mahāyānadharmādhimuktibhāvanā bodhisattvānām / dharmeṣvātmadarśanamanyatīrthānāmāvaraṇaṃ yasya pratipakṣaḥ prajñāpāramitābhāvanā bodhisattvānām / saṃsāre duḥkhasaṃjñā duḥkhabhīrutva śrāvakayānikānāmavaraṇaṃ yasya pratipakṣo gaganagañjādisamādhibhāvanā bodhisattvānām / sattvārthavimukhatā sattvārthanirapekṣatā pratyekabuddhayānikānāmāvaraṇaṃ yasya pratipakṣo mahākaruṇābhāvanā bodhisattvānāmiti /
body.translated_text: There, those beings who desire existence, the <s>icchantikas</s> who have fallen into fixity, who are indeed followers of this <s>Dharma</s>—they are called the 'mass of beings fixed in wrongness' (<s>mithyātvaniyata sattvarāśi</s>). Those desiring non-existence who have fallen into wrong means are called the 'unfixed mass of beings' (<s>aniyata sattvarāśi</s>). Those desiring non-existence who have fallen into [correct] means, and those desiring neither of the two who have entered the path of the attainment of equality—they are called the 'mass of beings fixed in rightness' (<s>samyaktvaniyata sattvarāśi</s>). There, setting aside the beings who have set forth on the <s>Mahāyāna</s> as those proceeding without obstruction, the other beings are as follows: <s>icchantikas</s>, <s>tīrthikas</s>, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. For them, these four obstructions operate to prevent the realization and direct experience of the <s>Tathāgatadhātu</s>. And what are the four? Namely: hostility toward the <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s> (<s>mahāyānadharmapratigha</s>) is the obstruction of <s>icchantikas</s>, whose antidote is the cultivation of faith in the <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s> by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. The view of self in <s>dharmas</s> is the obstruction of non-Buddhist <s>tīrthikas</s>, whose antidote is the cultivation of the Perfection of Wisdom (<s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>) by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. The perception of suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s> and fear of suffering is the obstruction of those following the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle, whose antidote is the cultivation of <s>samādhis</s> such as the <s>Gaganagañja</s> by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. Turning away from the welfare of beings and indifference toward the welfare of beings is the obstruction of those following the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicle, whose antidote is the cultivation of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>) by <s>Bodhisattvas</s>.

body.text: etaccaturvidhamāvaraṇameṣāṃ caturvidhānāṃ sattvānāṃ yasya pratipakṣānimāṃścaturo 'dhimuktyādīn bhāvayitvā bodhisattvā niruttarārthadharmakāyaviśuddhiparamatāmadhigacchantyebhiśca viśuddhisamudāgamakāraṇaiścaturbhiranugatā dharmarājaputrā bhavanti tathāgatakule / kathamiti /
body.translated_text: This fourfold obstruction of these four types of beings—having cultivated the four [qualities] beginning with faith (<s>adhimukti</s>) as antidotes to them, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> attain the supreme purification of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> of unsurpassed meaning. And endowed with these four causes for the attainment of purification, they become sons of the <s>Dharma</s>-king in the family of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. How so?

body.text: bījaṃ yeṣāmagrayānādhimuktirmātā prajñā buddhadharmaprasūtyai /
body.translated_text: For them, the seed is faith in the supreme vehicle (<s>agrayānādhimukti</s>); the mother is wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), for giving birth to <s>Buddha</s>-qualities;

body.text: garbhasthānaṃ dhyānasaukhyaṃ kṛpoktā dhātrī putrāste 'nujātā munīnām // 34 //
body.translated_text: the womb-abode is the bliss of meditation (<s>dhyānasukha</s>); compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>) is said to be the nurse—they are the sons born after the sages. // 34 //

body.text: tatra phalārtha karmārtha cārabhya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: Regarding the meaning of fruit and the meaning of action, a verse:

children.translated_text: The perfection of the qualities of purity, self, bliss, and permanence is the fruit;
revulsion from suffering, the wish for attainment, aspiration, and resolve are the actions [that produce it]. // 35 //

body.text: tatra pūrveṇa ślokārdhena kiṃ darśitam /
body.translated_text: There, what has been shown by the preceding half-verse?

children.translated_text: The fruit of these [causes], in brief, in the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, through the reversal
of the fourfold inversion, is produced as the antidote [to them]. // 36 //

body.text: ya ete 'dhimuktyādayaścatvāro dharmāstathāgatadhātorviśuddhihetava eṣāṃ yathāsaṃkhyameva samāsataścaturvidhaviparyāsaviparyayapratipakṣeṇa caturākārā tathāgatadharmakāyaguṇapāramitā phalaṃ draṣṭavyam / tatra yā rūpādike vastunyanitye nityamiti saṃjñā / duḥkhe sukhamiti / anātmanyātmeti / aśubhe śubhamiti saṃjñā / ayamucyate caturvidho viparyāsaḥ / etadviparyayeṇa caturvidha evāviparyāso veditavyaḥ / katamaścaturvidhaḥ / yā tasminneva rūpādike vastunyanityasaṃjñā / duḥkhasaṃjñā / anātmasaṃjñā / aśubhasaṃjñā / ayamucyate caturvidhaviparyāsaviparyayaḥ / sa khalveṣa nityādilakṣaṇaṃ tathāgatadharmakāyamadhikṛtyeha viparyāso 'bhipreto yasya pratipakṣeṇa caturākārā tathāgatadharmakāyaguṇapāramitā vyavasthāpitā / tadyathā nityapāramitā sukhapāramitātmapāramitā subhapāramiteti / eṣa ca grantho vistareṇa yathāsūtramanugantavyaḥ / viparyastā bhagavan sattvā upātteṣu pañcasūpādānaskandheṣu / te bhavantyanitye nityasaṃjñinaḥ / duḥkhe sukhasaṃjñinaḥ / anātmanyātmasaṃjñinaḥ / aśubhe subhasaṃjñinaḥ / sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhā api bhagavan śūnyatājñānenādṛṣṭapūrve sarvajñajñānaviṣaye tathāgatadharmakāye
body.translated_text: Those four qualities beginning with faith (<s>adhimukti</s>) that are the causes of purification of the <s>Tathāgatadhātu</s>—for them, in corresponding order, in brief, through the antidote that is the reversal of the fourfold inversion, the fourfold perfection of qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s> is to be seen as the fruit. There, the perception of 'permanent' regarding a thing such as form that is impermanent; 'blissful' regarding what is suffering; 'self' regarding what is without self; 'pure' regarding what is impure—this is called the fourfold inversion (<s>caturvidha viparyāsa</s>). By the reversal of this, the fourfold non-inversion is to be understood. What is the fourfold [non-inversion]? The perception of impermanence, the perception of suffering, the perception of non-self, and the perception of impurity regarding that very thing such as form—this is called the reversal of the fourfold inversion. However, here what is intended as the inversion is with reference to the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s> characterized by permanence and so forth; as the antidote to which the fourfold perfection of qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s> has been established—namely: the perfection of permanence (<s>nityapāramitā</s>), the perfection of bliss (<s>sukhapāramitā</s>), the perfection of self (<s>ātmapāramitā</s>), and the perfection of purity (<s>śubhapāramitā</s>). And this topic is to be understood in detail as in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Beings are inverted, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, with regard to the five aggregates of clinging (<s>upādānaskandha</s>) that they have taken up. They perceive permanence in what is impermanent, bliss in what is suffering, self in what is without self, and purity in what is impure. Even all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, are inverted regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s>, which is the domain of omniscient knowledge (<s>sarvajñajñāna</s>), never before seen through the knowledge of emptiness (<s>śūnyatājñāna</s>).'

body.text: viparyastāḥ / ye bhagavan sattvāḥ syurbhagavataḥ putrā aurasā nityasaṃjñina ātmasaṃjñinaḥ sukhasaṃjñinaḥ śubhasaṃjñinaste bhagavan sattvāḥ syuraviparyastāḥ / syuste bhagavan samyagdarśinaḥ / tat kasmāddhetoḥ / tathāgatadharmakāya eva bhagavan nityapāramitā sukhapāramitā ātmapāramitā śubhapāramitā / ye bhagavan sattvāstathāgatadharmakāyamevaṃ paśyanti te samyak paśyanti / ye samyaka paśyanti te bhagavataḥ putrā aurasā iti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: 'Those beings, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, who are the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s own sons (<s>aurasa putra</s>), who perceive permanence, self, bliss, and purity—those beings, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, would be non-inverted. They would be correct seers, O <s>Bhagavān</s>. For what reason? The <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s> alone, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, is the perfection of permanence, the perfection of bliss, the perfection of self, the perfection of purity. Those beings, O <s>Bhagavān</s>, who see the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s> in this way—they see correctly. Those who see correctly are the <s>Bhagavān</s>'s own sons'—and so on in detail.

body.text: āsāṃ punaścatasṛṇāṃ tathāgatadharmakāyaguṇapāramitāyāṃ hetvānupūrvyā pratilomakramo veditavyaḥ / tatra mahāyānadharmapratihatānāmicchantikānāmaśucisaṃsārābhirativiparyayeṇa bodhisattvānāṃ mahāyānadharmādhimuktibhāvanāyāḥ śubhapāramitādhigamaḥ phalaṃ draṣṭavyam / pañcasūpādānaskandheṣvātmadarśināmanyatīrthyānāmasadātmagrahābhirativiparyayeṇa prajñāpāramitābhāvanāyāḥ paramātmapāramitādhigamaḥ phalaṃ draṣṭavyam / sarve hyanyatīrthyā rūpādikamatatsvabhāvaṃ vastvātmetyupagatāḥ / taccaiṣāṃ vastu yathāgrahamātmalakṣaṇena visaṃvāditvāt sarvakālamanātmā / tathāgataḥ punaryathābhūtajñānena sarvadharmanairātmyaparapā ramabhiprāptaḥ / taccāsya nairātmyamanātmalakṣaṇena yathādarśanamavisaṃvāditvāt sarvakālamātmābhipreto nairātmyaṃmevātmani kṛtvā / yathoktaṃ sthito 'sthānayogeneti / saṃsāraduḥkhabhīrūṇāṃ śrāvakayānikānāṃ
body.translated_text: Furthermore, regarding these four perfections of qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s>, the reverse order in terms of the sequence of causes is to be understood. There, through the reversal of the delight in impure <s>saṃsāra</s> of the <s>icchantikas</s> who are hostile to the <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s>, the attainment of the perfection of purity (<s>śubhapāramitā</s>) through the cultivation of faith in the <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s> by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is to be seen as the fruit. Through the reversal of the delight in grasping a false self among the five aggregates of clinging by non-Buddhist <s>tīrthikas</s> who perceive self [in them], the attainment of the supreme perfection of self (<s>paramātmapāramitā</s>) through the cultivation of the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> by <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is to be seen as the fruit. For all non-Buddhist <s>tīrthikas</s> have apprehended things such as form, which are not of that nature, as self. And since those things, as they grasp them, are discordant with the characteristic of self, they are at all times without self. The <s>Tathāgata</s>, on the other hand, through knowledge of things as they truly are (<s>yathābhūtajñāna</s>), has reached the ultimate perfection of the selflessness of all <s>dharmas</s>. And since that selflessness, being concordant with the characteristic of non-self as truly seen, is at all times [truly] self—having made selflessness itself into self. As stated: 'Established by the method of non-establishment.' Of those following the <s>Śrāvaka</s> vehicle who fear the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

body.text: saṃsāraduḥkhopaśamamātrābhirativiparyayeṇa gaganagañjādisamādhibhavanāyāḥ sarvalaukikalokottarasukhapāramitādhigamaḥ phalaṃ draṣṭavyam / sattvārthanirapekṣāṇāṃ pratyekabuddhayānīyānāyamasaṃsargavihārābhirativiṣaparyayeṇa mahākaruṇābhāvanāyāḥ satatasamitamā saṃsārāt sattvārthaphaligodhapariśuddhatvān nityapāramitādhigamaḥ phalaṃ draṣṭavyam / ityetāsāṃ catasṛṇāmadhimuktiprajñāsamādhikaruṇābhāvanānāṃ yathāsaṃkhyameva caturākāraṃ tathāgatadharmakāye śubhātmasukhanityatvaguṇāpāramitākhyaṃ phalaṃ nirvartyate bodhisattvānām / ābhiśca tathāgato dharmadhātuparama ākāśadhātuparyavasāno 'parāntakoṭīniṣṭha ityucyate / mahāyānaparamadharmādhimuktibhāvanāyā hi tathāgato 'tyantaśubhadharmadhātuparamatādhigamāddharmadhātuparamaḥ saṃvṛttaḥ / prajñāpāramitābhāvanayākāśopamasattvabhājanalokanairātmyaniṣṭhāgamanād gaganagañjādisamādhibhāvanayā ca sarvatra paramadharmeśvaryavibhutvasaṃdarśanādākāśadhātuparyavasānaḥ / mahākaruṇābhāvanayā sarvasattveṣvaparyantakālakāruṇikatāmupādāyāparāntakoṭiniṣṭha iti /
body.translated_text: by the reversal of the attachment to the mere cessation of the suffering of <s>saṃsāra</s>, the attainment of the <s>sukhapāramitā</s> (perfection of bliss) — both mundane and supramundane — should be seen as the fruit of the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> such as <s>Gaganagañja</s> and others. By the reversal of the attachment to the solitary dwelling of disengagement of the <s>Pratyekabuddhayāna</s> adherents, who are indifferent to the welfare of beings, the attainment of the <s>nityapāramitā</s> (perfection of permanence) — because of purity in continuously and constantly bearing fruit for the welfare of beings throughout <s>saṃsāra</s> — should be seen as the fruit of the cultivation of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>). Thus, from these four cultivations — of faith (<s>adhimukti</s>), wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>), concentration (<s>samādhi</s>), and compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) — in corresponding order, the fourfold fruit called the quality-perfections of purity (<s>śubha</s>), self (<s>ātman</s>), bliss (<s>sukha</s>), and permanence (<s>nityatva</s>) is brought about in the <s>Dharmakāya</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s> for <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. And through these, the <s>Tathāgata</s> is said to be 'supreme in the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>,' 'reaching to the limit of the <s>Ākāśadhātu</s>,' and 'abiding to the final point of the future.' For through the cultivation of faith in the supreme <s>Dharma</s> of the <s>Mahāyāna</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has become supreme in the <s>Dharmadhātu</s> through the attainment of supremacy in the utterly pure <s>Dharmadhātu</s>. Through the cultivation of <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s>, by reaching the ultimate [realization of] the selflessness of the space-like world of beings and the receptacle-world, and through the cultivation of <s>samādhi</s> such as <s>Gaganagañja</s>, by the display everywhere of sovereignty and mastery over the supreme <s>Dharma</s>, he reaches to the limit of the <s>Ākāśadhātu</s>. Through the cultivation of great compassion, by virtue of his boundless compassionateness toward all beings throughout unlimited time, he abides to the final point of the future.

body.text: āsāṃ punaścatasṛṇāṃ tathāgatadharmakāyaguṇapāramitānāmadhigamāyānāsravadhātusthitānāmapyarhatāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ vaśitāprāptānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāmime catvāraḥ paripanthā bhavanti / tadyathā pratyayalakṣaṇaṃ hetulakṣaṇaṃ saṃbhavalakṣaṇaṃ vibhavalakṣaṇamiti / tatra pratyayalakṣaṇamavidyāvāsabhūmiravidyeva saṃskārāṇām / hetulakṣaṇamavidyāvāsabhūmipratyayameva saṃskāravadanāsravaṃ karma / saṃbhavalakṣaṇamavidyāvāsabhūmipratyayānāsravakarmahetukī ca trividhā manomayātmabhāvanirvṛttiścaturupādānapratyayā
body.translated_text: Now, for the attainment of these four quality-perfections of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s>, there are four obstacles even for <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained mastery, though they abide in the undefiled element (<s>anāsravadhātu</s>). These are: that which has the character of a condition (<s>pratyayalakṣaṇa</s>), that which has the character of a cause (<s>hetulakṣaṇa</s>), that which has the character of arising (<s>saṃbhavalakṣaṇa</s>), and that which has the character of dissolution (<s>vibhavalakṣaṇa</s>). Among these, the condition-characteristic is the ground of the latent impressions of ignorance (<s>avidyāvāsabhūmi</s>), which is ignorance itself as [the condition] of [the remaining] formations (<s>saṃskāras</s>). The cause-characteristic is the undefiled action (<s>anāsravakarma</s>), which, like a formation conditioned by ignorance, is conditioned by the ground of the latent impressions of ignorance. The arising-characteristic is the threefold arising of a mind-made body (<s>manomayātmabhāva</s>), caused by undefiled action conditioned by the ground of latent impressions of ignorance, and conditioned by the four types of clinging

body.text: sāsravakarmahetukīva tribhavābhinirvṛttiḥ / vibhavalakṣaṇaṃ trividhamanomayātmabhāvanirvṛttipratyayā jātipratyayamiva jarāmaraṇamacintyā pāriṇāmikī cyutiriti /
body.translated_text: — just as threefold existence-arising is caused by defiled action. The dissolution-characteristic is the inconceivable transformative death (<s>pāriṇāmikī cyuti</s>), conditioned by the arising of the threefold mind-made body — just as death-and-aging is conditioned by birth.

body.text: tatra sarvopakleśasaṃniśrayabhūtāyā avidyāvāsabhūmeraprahīṇātvādarhantaḥ pratyekabuddhā vaśitāprāptāśca bodhisattvāḥ sarvakleśamaladaurgandhyavāsanāpakarṣaparyantaśubhapāramitāṃ nādhigacchanti / tāmeva cāvi dyāvāsabhūmiṃ pratītya sūkṣmanimittaprapañcasamudācārayogādatyantamanabhisaṃskāramātmapāramitāṃ nādhigacchanti / tāṃ cāvidyāvāsabhūmimavidyāvāsabhūmipratyayaṃ ca sūkṣmanimittaprapañcasamudācārasamutthāpitamanāsravaṃ karma pratītya manomayaskandhasamudayāt tannirodhamatyantasukhapāramitāṃ nādhigacchanti / yāvacca nirayaśeṣakleśakarmajanmasaṃkleśanirodhasamudbhūtaṃ tathāgatadhātuṃ na sākṣātkurvanti tāvadacintyapāriṇāmikyāścyu teravigamādatyantānanyathābhāvāṃ nityapāramitāṃ nādhigacchanti / tatra kleśasaṃkleśavadavidyāvāsabhūmiḥ / karmasaṃkleśavadanāsravakarmābhisaṃskāraḥ / janmasaṃkleśavat trividhā manomayātmabhāvanirvṛttiracintyapāriṇāmikī ca cyutiriti /
body.translated_text: Here, because the ground of latent impressions of ignorance (<s>avidyāvāsabhūmi</s>), which is the basis of all secondary defilements, has not been abandoned, <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained mastery do not attain the <s>śubhapāramitā</s> (perfection of purity), which is the ultimate removal of the stench of the defilements' stain and latent impressions. And depending on that very ground of latent impressions of ignorance, due to the operation of subtle conceptual proliferation, they do not attain the <s>ātmapāramitā</s> (perfection of self), which is the utter freedom from all mental construction. And depending on that ground of latent impressions of ignorance and on the undefiled action generated by the operation of subtle conceptual proliferation conditioned by it, due to the arising of the mind-made aggregates (<s>manomayaskandha</s>), they do not attain the <s>sukhapāramitā</s> (perfection of bliss), which is the cessation of those [aggregates] and their cause. And as long as they do not directly realize the <s>Tathāgatadhātu</s> (Buddha-element), which arises from the cessation of all defilement by afflictions, action, and birth — including their residues — so long do they not attain the <s>nityapāramitā</s> (perfection of permanence), which is the utter changelessness of never becoming otherwise, due to the non-departure of the inconceivable transformative death. Here, the ground of latent impressions of ignorance corresponds to defilement by afflictions (<s>kleśasaṃkleśa</s>); the formation of undefiled action corresponds to defilement by action (<s>karmasaṃkleśa</s>); the threefold arising of the mind-made body and the inconceivable transformative death correspond to defilement by birth (<s>janmasaṃkleśa</s>).

body.text: eṣa ca grantho vistareṇa yathāsūtramanugantavyaḥ / syādyathāpi nāma bhagavannupādānapratyayāḥ sāsravakarmahetukāstrayo bhavāḥ saṃbhavanti / evameva bhagavannavidyāvāsabhūmipratyayā
body.translated_text: This passage should be understood in detail according to the sūtra: 'Just as, Blessed One, the three existences arise caused by defiled action and conditioned by clinging, so too, Blessed One,

body.text: anāsravakarmahetukā arhatāṃ pratyekabuddhānāṃ vaśitāprāptānāṃ ca bodhisattvānāṃ manomayāstrayaḥ kāyāḥ saṃbhavanti / āsu bhagavan tisṛṣu bhūmipveṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ manomayānāṃ kāyānāṃ saṃbhavāyānāsravasya ca karmaṇo 'bhinirvṛttaye pratyayobhavatyavidyāvāsabhūmiriti vistaraḥ / yata eteṣu triṣu manomayeṣvarhatpratyekabuddhabodhisattvakāyeṣu subhātmasukhanityatvaguṇapāramitā na saṃvidyante tasmāt tathāgatadharmakāya eva nityapāramitā sukhapāramitātmapāramitā śubhapāramitetyukatam /
body.translated_text: caused by undefiled action and conditioned by the ground of latent impressions of ignorance, the three mind-made bodies of <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have attained mastery arise. In these three planes, Blessed One, the ground of latent impressions of ignorance serves as the condition for the arising of these three mind-made bodies and for the production of undefiled action' — and so forth in detail. Since in these three mind-made bodies of <s>Arhats</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, the quality-perfections of purity, self, bliss, and permanence are not found, therefore it is said that the <s>nityapāramitā</s>, <s>sukhapāramitā</s>, <s>ātmapāramitā</s>, and <s>śubhapāramitā</s> exist only in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s>.

body.text: sa hi prakṛtiśuddhatvādvāsanāpagamācchuciḥ

children.translated_text: it is the supreme self (<s>paramātman</s>) through the pacification of the proliferation of [both] self and selflessness. [37]

body.translated_text: For it is pure because of its natural purity and the removal of latent impressions,

children.translated_text: It is bliss through the cessation of the mind-made aggregates and their cause,
it is permanent through the penetrative realization of the equality of <s>saṃsāra</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>. [38]

body.text: samasato dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ tathāgatadharmakāye śubhapāramitā veditavyā / prakṛtipariśuddhyā sāmānyalakṣaṇena / vaimalyapariśuddhyā viśeṣalakṣaṇena / dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmātmapāramitā veditavyā / tīrthikāntavivarjanatayā cātmaprapañcavigamācchrāvakāntavivarjanatayā ca nairātmyaprapañcavigamāt / dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ sukhapāramitāṃ veditavyā / sarvākāraduḥkhasamudayaprahāṇataśca vāsanānusaṃdhisamudghātāt sarvākāraduḥkhanirodhasākṣātkaraṇataśca manomayaskandhanirodhasākṣātkāraṇāt / dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāṃ nityapāramitā veditavyā / anityasaṃsārānapakarṣaṇāta ścocchedāntā patanān nityanirvāṇasamāropaṇataśca śāśvatāntāpatanāt / yathoktam / anītyāḥ saṃskārā iti ced bhagavan paśyeta sāsya syāducchedadṛṣṭiḥ /
body.translated_text: In summary, the <s>śubhapāramitā</s> (perfection of purity) should be understood in the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s> for two reasons: through natural purity (<s>prakṛtipariśuddhi</s>) as the general characteristic, and through purity from stains (<s>vaimalyapariśuddhi</s>) as the specific characteristic. The <s>ātmapāramitā</s> (perfection of self) should be understood for two reasons: by avoiding the extreme of the non-Buddhists through the elimination of the proliferation of self, and by avoiding the extreme of the <s>Śrāvakas</s> through the elimination of the proliferation of selflessness. The <s>sukhapāramitā</s> (perfection of bliss) should be understood for two reasons: through the abandonment of all forms of the origin of suffering, namely the eradication of the continuity of latent impressions, and through the direct realization of all forms of the cessation of suffering, namely the direct realization of the cessation of the mind-made aggregates. The <s>nityapāramitā</s> (perfection of permanence) should be understood for two reasons: through not falling into the extreme of annihilation (<s>ucchedānta</s>) by not being repelled from impermanent <s>saṃsāra</s>, and through not falling into the extreme of eternalism (<s>śāśvatānta</s>) by not superimposing permanent <s>nirvāṇa</s>. As it is said: 'If, Blessed One, one were to see that formations are impermanent, that would be an annihilationist view.

body.text: sāsya syānna samyagdṛṣṭiḥ / nityaṃ nirvāṇamiti ced bhagavan paśyeta sāsya syācchāśvatadṛṣṭiḥ / sāsya syānna samyagdṛṣṭiriti /
body.translated_text: That would not be right view. If, Blessed One, one were to see that <s>nirvāṇa</s> is permanent, that would be an eternalist view. That would not be right view.'

body.text: tadanena dharmadhātunayamukhena paramārthataḥ saṃsāra eva nirvāṇamityuktam / ubhayathāvikalpanāpratiṣṭhitanirvāṇasākṣātkaraṇataḥ / api khalu dvābhyāṃ kāraṇābhyāmaviśeṣeṇa sarvasattvānāmāsannadūrībhāvavigamādapratiṣṭhitapadaprāptimātraparidīpanā bhavati / katamābhyāṃ dvābhyām / iha bodhisattvo 'viśeṣeṇa sarvasattvānāṃ nāsannībhavati prajñayāśeṣatṛṣṇānuśayaprahāṇāt / na dūrībhavati mahākaruṇayā tadaparityāgāditi / ayamupāyo 'pratiṣṭhitasvabhāvāyāḥ samyaksaṃbodheranuprāptaye / prajñayā hi bodhisattvo 'śeṣatṛṣṇānuśayaprahāṇādātmahitāya nirvāṇagatādhyāśayaḥ saṃsāre na pratiṣṭhate 'parinirvāṇagotravat / mahākaruṇayā duḥkhitasattvāparityāgāt parihītāya saṃsāragataprayogo nirvāṇe na pratiṣṭhate śamaikayānagotravat / evamidaṃ dharmadvayamanuttarāyā bodhermūlaṃ pratiṣṭhānamiti /
body.translated_text: By this method of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, it is said that in the ultimate sense, <s>saṃsāra</s> itself is <s>nirvāṇa</s> — through the direct realization of non-abiding <s>nirvāṇa</s> (<s>apratiṣṭhitanirvāṇa</s>) that is free from conceptual construction in both ways. Moreover, through two reasons, there is an indication of the attainment of the non-abiding state through the removal of proximity and distance with respect to all beings without distinction. Which two? Here, a <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not become close to any beings without distinction, through the abandonment of all residual traces of craving by means of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>); and does not become distant, through not abandoning them by means of great compassion (<s>mahākaruṇā</s>). This is the means for attaining perfect awakening (<s>samyaksaṃbodhi</s>) whose nature is non-abiding. For through wisdom, a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having abandoned all residual traces of craving for his own benefit, with his aspiration directed toward <s>nirvāṇa</s>, does not abide in <s>saṃsāra</s> — unlike those of the <s>aparinirvāṇagotra</s> (lineage of non-final-nirvāṇa). Through great compassion, by not abandoning suffering beings, with his endeavor directed toward <s>saṃsāra</s> for the benefit of others, he does not abide in <s>nirvāṇa</s> — unlike those of the <s>śamaikayānagotra</s> (lineage of the single vehicle of quiescence). Thus this pair of <s>dharmas</s> is the root and foundation of unsurpassed awakening.

children.text: chittvā snehaṃ prajñayātmanyaśeṣaṃ sattvasnehān naiti śāntiṃ kṛpāvān /
children.translated_text: Having cut through all attachment to self by means of wisdom, the compassionate one does not attain quiescence due to his love for beings;

children.text: niḥśrityaivaṃ dhīkṛpe bodhyupāyau nopaityāryaḥ saṃvṛtiṃ nirvṛtiṃ vā // 39 //
children.translated_text: thus, relying upon these two means of awakening — wisdom and compassion — the Noble One enters neither worldly existence nor final cessation. [39]

body.text: tatra purvādhikṛtaṃ karmārthamārabhya pareṇa ślokārdhena kiṃ darśitam /
body.translated_text: Here, with regard to the previously introduced topic of the purpose of action, what is shown by the latter half-verse?

children.translated_text: If the <s>Buddhadhātu</s> (Buddha-element) did not exist, there would be no weariness with suffering,

children.text: necchā na prārthanā nāpi prāṇidhirnivṛtau bhavet // 40 //
children.translated_text: nor would there be desire, aspiration, or resolve for <s>nirvāṇa</s>. [40]

body.text: tathā coktam / tathāgatagarbhaścedbhagavanna syānna syādduḥkhe 'pi nirvinna nirvāṇa icchā vā prārthanā vā praṇidhirveti / tatra samāsato buddhadhātuviśuddhigotraṃ mithyātvaniyatānāmapi sattvānāṃ dvividhakāryapratyupasthāpanaṃ bhavati / saṃsāre ca duḥkhadoṣadarśananiḥśrayeṇa nirvidamutpādayati / nirvāṇe sukhanuśaṃsadarśananiḥśrayeṇa cchandaṃ janayati / icchāṃ prārthanāṃ praṇidhimiti / icchābhilaṣitārthaprāptāvasaṃkocaḥ / prārthanābhilaṣitārthaprāptyupāyaparimārgaṇā / praṇidhiryābhilaṣitārthe cetanā cittābhisaṃskāraḥ /
body.translated_text: And so it has been said: 'If, Blessed One, there were no <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s>, there would be neither weariness with suffering, nor desire for <s>nirvāṇa</s>, nor aspiration, nor resolve.' Here, in summary, the <s>Buddhadhātu</s>'s purification-lineage (<s>viśuddhigotra</s>) brings about a twofold effect even for beings who are fixed in wrong views (<s>mithyātvaniyata</s>): through the perception of the faults of suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s>, it generates weariness (<s>nirveda</s>); through the perception of the benefits of bliss in <s>nirvāṇa</s>, it generates desire, aspiration, and resolve. Desire (<s>icchā</s>) is non-hesitation upon obtaining the desired object. Aspiration (<s>prārthanā</s>) is the search for the means to obtain the desired object. Resolve (<s>praṇidhi</s>) is the volition, the mental formation, directed toward the desired object.

children.translated_text: The perception of the faults of suffering in [worldly] existence, and the perception of the qualities of bliss in <s>nirvāṇa</s> —
these occur when the lineage (<s>gotra</s>) exists; they are not found in those without lineage. [41]

body.text: yadapi tat saṃsāre ca duḥkhadoṣadarśanaṃ bhavati nirvāṇe ca sukhānuśaṃsadarśanametadapi śuklāṃśasya pudgalasya gotre sati bhavati nāhetukaṃ nāpratyayamiti / yadi hi tadgotramantareṇa syādahetukamapratyayaṃ pāpasamucchedayogena tadicchāntikānāmapyaparinirvāṇagotrāṇāṃ syāt / na ca bhavati tāvadyāvadāgantukamalaviśuddhigotraṃ trayāṇāmanyatamadharmādhimuktiṃ na sa mudānayati satpuruṣasaṃsargādicatuḥśuklasamavadhānayogena /
body.translated_text: That perception of the faults of suffering in <s>saṃsāra</s> and the perception of the benefits of bliss in <s>nirvāṇa</s> — these too occur for a person of the pure portion (<s>śuklāṃśa</s>) only when the lineage exists; they are not without cause or without condition. For if it were without cause and condition, independent of that lineage, then by the method of eliminating evil, it would also exist for those of the <s>icchāntika</s> disposition — those of the lineage of non-final-nirvāṇa. But it does not occur so long as the lineage of purification from adventitious defilements has not brought forth faith in the <s>Dharma</s> of any one of the three [vehicles], through the conjunction of the four wholesome conditions such as association with good persons.

body.text: yatra hyāha / tatra paścādantaśo mithyātvaniyatasaṃtānānāmapi sattvānāṃ kāyeṣu tathāgatasūryamaṇḍalaraśmayo nipatanti * * * anāgatahetusaṃjananatayā
body.translated_text: For there [the sūtra] states: 'And thereafter, in the bodies even of beings fixed in wrong views as their last [birth], the rays of the sun-maṇḍala of the <s>Tathāgata</s> fall * * * and nurture with wholesome <s>dharmas</s> for the purpose of generating future causes

body.text: saṃvardhayanti ca kuśalairdharmeriti / yatpunaridamuktamicchantiko 'tyantamaparinirvāṇadharmeti tan mahāyānadharmapratigha icchantikatve heturiti mahāyānadharmapratighanivartanārthamuktaṃ kālāntarābhiprāyeṇa / na khalu kaścitprakṛtiviśuddhagotrasaṃbhavādatyantāviśuddhidharmā bhavitumarhasi / yasmādaviśeṣeṇa punarbhagavatā sarvasattveṣu viśuddhibhavyatāṃ saṃdhāyoktam /
body.translated_text: .' But as for the statement 'an <s>icchāntika</s> is one whose nature is to never attain <s>parinirvāṇa</s>' — since aversion to the <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s> is the cause of the <s>icchāntika</s> state, this was said with the intention of a future time, for the purpose of turning away from aversion to the <s>Mahāyāna Dharma</s>. Certainly no one, because of being born from the naturally pure lineage, can be one whose nature is to be utterly impure forever. For the Blessed One, having declared the capacity for purification in all beings without distinction, said:

children.translated_text: Though beginningless, it has an end; naturally pure, endowed with permanent <s>dharmas</s>,

children.text: anādikośairbahirvṛto na dṛśyate suvarṇabimbaṃ paricchāditaṃ yathā //
children.translated_text: though covered from without by beginningless sheaths, it is not seen — like a golden image covered over.

body.text: tatra yogārthamārabhya ślokaḥ / mahodadhirivāmeyaguṇaratnākṣayākaraḥ /

children.translated_text: by nature endowed with inseparable qualities, like a lamp. [42]

body.translated_text: Here, with regard to the topic of practice, a verse: Like a great ocean, an inexhaustible mine of immeasurable qualities — like jewels,

body.text: tatra pūrveṇa ślokārthena ki darśitam /
body.translated_text: Here, what is shown by the first half-verse?

children.translated_text: Through the inclusion of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, the Conqueror's knowledge, and compassion within the [<s>Tathāgata</s>-] element,
the similarity of this noble [element] to an ocean of jewel-vessels and water has been shown. [43]

body.text: trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ yathāsaṃkhyameva trividhena mahāsamudrasādharmyeṇa tathāgatadhātorhetusamanvāgamamadhikṛtya yogārtho veditavyaḥ / katamāni trīṇi sthānāni / tadyathā dharmakāyaviśuddhihetuḥ / buddhajñānasamudāgamahetuḥ / tathāgatamahākaruṇāvṛttiheturiti /
body.translated_text: The topic of practice with regard to the <s>Tathāgatadhātu</s> should be understood through the threefold similarity with the great ocean, in corresponding order to three grounds, with reference to the cause for the endowment [of the <s>Tathāgatadhātu</s>]. Which three grounds? Namely: the cause for the purity of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, the cause for the attainment of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge, and the cause for the operation of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s great compassion.

body.text: tatra dharmakāyaviśuddhiheturmahāyānādhimuktibhāvanā draṣṭavyā / buddhajñānasamudāgamahetuḥ prajñāsamādhimukhabhavanā / tathāgatamahākaruṇāpravṛttiheturbodhisattvakaruṇābhāvaneti / tatra mahāyānādhimuktibhāvanāyā bhājanasādharmyaṃ tasyāmaparimeyākṣayaprajñāsamādhiratnakaruṇāvārisamavasaraṇāt / prajñāsamādhimukhabhāvanāyā ratnāsādharmyaṃ tasya nirvikalpatvādacintyaprabhāvaguṇayogācca / bodhisattvakaruṇābhāvanāyā vārisādharmyaṃ tasyāḥ sarvajagati paramasnigdhabhāvaikarasalakṣaṇaprayogāditi / eṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ dharmāṇāmanena trividhena hetunā tatsaṃbaddhaḥsamanvāgamo yoga ityucyate /
body.translated_text: There, the cause of the purification of the <s>Dharmakāya</s> is to be seen as the cultivation of devotion to the <s>Mahāyāna</s>. The cause of the attainment of <s>Buddha</s>-knowledge is the cultivation having <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) and <s>samādhi</s> (concentration) as its gateways. The cause of the operation of <s>Tathāgata</s>'s great compassion is the cultivation of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-compassion. There, the similarity of the cultivation of <s>Mahāyāna</s> devotion to a vessel [is] because immeasurable and inexhaustible treasures of <s>prajñā</s>, <s>samādhi</s>, and the waters of compassion come together in it. The similarity of the cultivation having <s>prajñā</s> and <s>samādhi</s> as its gateways to a jewel [is] because of its non-discriminating nature and its endowment with qualities of inconceivable power. The similarity of the cultivation of <s>Bodhisattva</s>-compassion to water [is] because of its application with the characteristic of being of a single flavor of supreme tenderness toward all the world. The conjunction with these three <s>dharmas</s> through this threefold cause is called '<s>yoga</s>' (connection).

body.text: tatrāpareṇa ślokārdhena kiṃ darśayati /
body.translated_text: There, what is shown by the remaining half-verse?

children.translated_text: Through the non-differentiation of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) [as it appears] in superknowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>), knowledge, and stainlessness,
the similarity of a lamp's light, heat, and color [is established] for the stainless basis (<s>vimalāśraya</s>). ||44||

body.text: trayāṇāṃ sthānānāṃ yathāsaṃkhyameva trividhena dīpasādharmyeṇa tathāgatadhātoḥ phalasamanvāgamamadhikṛtya yogārtho veditavyaḥ / katamani trīṇi sthānāni / tadyathā / abhijñā āsravakṣayajñānamāsravakṣayaśceti / tatra pañcānāmabhijñānāṃ jvālāsādharmyaṃ tāsāmarthānubhavajñānavipakṣāndhakāravidhamanapratyupasthānalakṣaṇatvāt / āsravakṣayajñānasyoṣṇasādharmya tasya niravaśeṣakarmakleśendhanadahanapratyupasthānalakṣaṇatvāt / āśrayaparivṛtterāsravakṣayasya varṇasādharmya tasyātyantavimalaviśuddhaprabhāsvaralakṣaṇatvāt /
body.translated_text: With reference to the fruit-connection (<s>phalasamanvāgama</s>) of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element, the meaning of '<s>yoga</s>' is to be understood through the threefold similarity to a lamp with respect to three categories in numerical correspondence. What are the three categories? Namely: superknowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>), the knowledge of the destruction of defilements (<s>āsravakṣayajñāna</s>), and the destruction of defilements (<s>āsravakṣaya</s>) itself. There, the similarity of the five superknowledges to a flame [is] because their characteristic is the dispelling of the darkness that is the opponent of knowledge and the experience of [their respective] objects. The similarity of the knowledge of the destruction of defilements to heat [is] because its characteristic is the burning of all the fuel of <s>karma</s> and afflictions without remainder. The similarity of the transformation of the basis — the destruction of defilements — to color [is] because its characteristic is being utterly stainless, pure, and luminous.

body.text: tatra vimalaḥ kleśāvaraṇaprahāṇāt / viśuddho jñeyāvaraṇaprahāṇāt / prabhāsvarastadubhayāgantukatāprakṛtitaḥ / ityeṣāṃ samāsataḥ saptānāmabhijñājñānaprahāṇasaṃgṛhītānāmaśaikṣasāntānikānāṃ dharmāṇāmanāsravadhātāvanyonyamavinirbhagatvamapṛthagbhāvo dharmadhātusamanvāgamo yoga ityucyate / eṣa ca yogārthamārabhya pradīpadṛṣṭānto vistareṇa yathāsūtramanugantavyaḥ / tadyathā śāriputra pradīpaḥ / avinirbhagadharmā / avinirmuktaguṇaḥ / yaduta ālokoṣṇavarṇatābhiḥ / maṇirvālokavarṇasaṃsthānaiḥ / evameva śāriputra tathagatanirdiṣṭo dharmakāyo 'vinirbhāgadharmāvinirmuktajñānaguṇo yaduta gaṅgānadīvālikāvyativṛttaistathāgatadharmairiti /
body.translated_text: There, 'stainless' (<s>vimala</s>) is because of the abandonment of the afflictive obstruction (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>). 'Pure' (<s>viśuddha</s>) is because of the abandonment of the cognitive obstruction (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>). 'Luminous' (<s>prabhāsvara</s>) is because both [obstructions] are adventitious by nature. Thus, in brief, the mutual inseparability and non-differentiation of these seven <s>dharmas</s> — comprised of superknowledge, knowledge, and abandonment — which belong to the continuum of a non-learner (<s>aśaikṣa</s>), in the undefiled element (<s>anāsravadhātu</s>), is called the connection with the <s>dharmadhātu</s> (<s>dharmadhātusamanvāgama</s>), [i.e.,] '<s>yoga</s>.' And this lamp-illustration with reference to the meaning of '<s>yoga</s>' is to be followed in detail as [stated] in the <s>sūtra</s>: 'Just as, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, a lamp has inseparable <s>dharmas</s> and undetached qualities — namely, its light, heat, and color. Or a gem [has inseparable] light, color, and shape. Even so, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>Dharmakāya</s> taught by the <s>Tathāgata</s> has inseparable <s>dharmas</s> and undetached qualities of knowledge, namely, <s>Tathāgata</s>-qualities that exceed the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river.'

body.text: tatra vṛttyarthamārabhya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, with reference to the meaning of function (<s>vṛtti</s>), there is a verse:

children.translated_text: Through the non-differentiation of <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) in ordinary beings, noble ones, and fully awakened ones,
this <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> in beings has been taught by those who see the truth. ||45||
What is shown by this?
Ordinary beings are inverted; those who have seen the truths are [free from] inversion;
<s>Tathāgatas</s> are correctly non-inverted and free from conceptual proliferation (<s>niṣprapañca</s>). ||46||

body.text: yadidaṃ tathāgatadhātoḥ sarvadharmatathatāviśuddhisāmānyalakṣaṇamupadiṣṭaṃ prajñāpāramitādiṣu nirvikalpajñānamukhāvavādamārabhya bodhisattvānāmasmin samāsatastrayāṇāṃ pudgalānāṃ pṛthagjanasyātattvadarśina āryasya tattvadarśino viśuddhiniṣṭhāgatasya tathāgatasya tridhā bhinnā pravṛttirveditavyā / yaduta viparyastāviparyastā
body.translated_text: That general characteristic of <s>tathatā</s>-purification of all <s>dharmas</s> belonging to the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element, which has been taught in the <s>Prajñāpāramitā</s> and other [sūtras] beginning with the instructions having non-discriminating knowledge as their gateway — with reference to the <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, in brief, for three types of persons — the ordinary being who does not see the truth, the noble one who sees the truth, and the <s>Tathāgata</s> who has reached the culmination of purity — the function is to be understood as threefold: namely, inverted, non-inverted,

body.text: samyagaviparyastā niṣprapañcā ca yathākramam / tatra viparyastā saṃjñācittadṛṣṭiviparyāsād vālānām / aviparyastā viparyayeṇa tatprahāṇādāryāṇām / samyagaviparyastā niṣprapañcā ca savāsanakleśajñeyāvaraṇasamudghātāt samyaksambuddhānām /
body.translated_text: correctly non-inverted, and free from conceptual proliferation, respectively. There, 'inverted' [refers to] the foolish, because of the inversion of perception, thought, and views. 'Non-inverted' [refers to] the noble ones, because of the abandonment of those [inversions] through their reversal. 'Correctly non-inverted and free from conceptual proliferation' [refers to] the perfectly awakened ones, because of the eradication of the obstructions of affliction and cognition together with their latent impressions (<s>vāsana</s>).

body.text: ataḥ parametameva vṛttyarthamārabhya tadanye catvāro 'rthāḥ prabhedanirdeśādeva veditavyāḥ / tatraiṣāṃ trayāṇāṃ pudgalānāmavasthāprabhedārthamārabhya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: From this point onward, with reference to this very meaning of function, the remaining four meanings are to be understood through the classified exposition. There, with reference to the meaning of the classification of stages for these three types of persons, there is a verse:

children.translated_text: Impure, impure-and-pure, and perfectly pure, in order —
[the element] is called '<s>sattvadhātu</s>' (element of beings), '<s>Bodhisattva</s>,' and '<s>Tathāgata</s>.' ||47||

body.text: anena kiṃ darśitam /
body.translated_text: What is shown by this?

children.translated_text: Through these six meanings — nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) and the rest — in brief,
the element (<s>dhātu</s>) in three stages is known by three names. ||48||

body.text: iti ye kecidanāsravadhātunirdeśā nānādharmaparyāyamukheṣu bhagavatā vistareṇa nirdiṣṭāḥ sarveta ebhireva samāsataḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ svabhāvahetuphalakarmayogavṛttyarthaḥ saṃgṛhītāstisṛṣvavasthāsu yathākramaṃ trināmanirdeśato nirdiṣṭā veditavyāḥ / yadutāśuddhāvasthāyāṃ sattvadhāturiti / aśuddhaśuddhāvasthāyāṃ bodhisattva iti / suviśuddhāvasthāyāṃ tathāgata iti / yathoktaṃ bhagavatā / ayameva śāriputra dharmakāyo 'paryantakleśakośakoṭigūḍhaḥ / saṃsārastrotasā uhmamāno 'navarāgrasaṃsāragaticyutyupapattiṣu saṃcaran sattvadhāturityucyate / sa eva śāriputra dharmakāyaḥ saṃsārastrotoduḥkhanirviṣṇo viraktaḥ sarvakāmaviṣayebhyo daśapāramitāntargataiścaturaśītyā
body.translated_text: Thus, whatever expositions of the undefiled element (<s>anāsravadhātu</s>) have been taught in detail by the Blessed One through the gateways of various <s>dharma</s>-methods — all of these are to be understood as encompassed by these six meanings in brief — nature, cause, fruit, function, connection, and operation — and as taught through the designation of three names in three stages respectively. Namely: in the impure stage, it is called '<s>sattvadhātu</s>' (element of beings); in the impure-and-pure stage, '<s>Bodhisattva</s>'; in the perfectly pure stage, '<s>Tathāgata</s>.' As the Blessed One has said: 'This very <s>Dharmakāya</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, hidden within the sheath of the boundless mass of afflictions, carried along by the stream of <s>saṃsāra</s>, wandering in the beginningless and endless destinations of <s>saṃsāra</s> — births, deaths, and rebirths — is called "<s>sattvadhātu</s>." That very <s>Dharmakāya</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, wearied by the suffering of the stream of <s>saṃsāra</s>, disenchanted with all objects of desire, practicing the conduct toward awakening through eighty-four

body.text: dharmaskandhasahasrairbodhāya caryā caran bodhisattva ityucyate / sa eva punaḥ śāriputra dharmakāyaḥ sarvakleśakośaparimuktaḥ sarvaduḥkhatikrāntaḥ sarvopakleśamalāpagataḥ śuddho viśuddhaḥ paramapariśuddhadharmatāyāṃ sthitaḥ sarvasattvālokanīyāṃ bhūmimārūḍhaḥ sarvasyāṃ jñeyabhūmāvadvitīyaṃ pauruṣaṃ sthāma prāpto 'nāvaraṇadharmāpratihatasarvadharmaiśvaryabalatāmadhigatastathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddha ityucyate /
body.translated_text: thousand collections of <s>dharma</s>-groups included within the ten <s>pāramitās</s> — is called "<s>Bodhisattva</s>." That very <s>Dharmakāya</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, liberated from the sheath of all afflictions, having transcended all suffering, freed from the stain of all secondary defilements, pure, utterly pure, established in the supreme purity of <s>dharmatā</s>, having ascended to the stage that is the object of vision for all beings, having attained unrivaled masculine strength in the entire domain of the knowable, having reached the sovereignty and power over all <s>dharmas</s> without obstruction — is called "<s>Tathāgata</s>, <s>Arhat</s>, Perfectly Awakened One."'

body.text: tāsteva tisṛṣvavasthāsu tathāgatadhātoḥ sarvatragārthamārabhya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: With reference to the meaning of the all-pervasiveness of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element in those very three stages, there is a verse:

children.translated_text: Just as space, being all-pervading and of non-discriminating nature,
so too, the element of the natural stainlessness of the mind (<s>cittaprakṛtivaimalya</s>) pervades everywhere. ||49||
What is shown by this?
Its general characteristic pervades those [stages characterized by] faults, qualities, and the culmination [of qualities],
just as space [pervades] things of inferior, middling, and superior [form]. ||50||

body.text: yāsau pṛthagjanāryasaṃbuddhānāmavikalpacittaprakṛtiḥ sā tisṛṣvavasthāsu yathākramaṃ doṣeṣvapi guṇeṣvapi guṇaviśuddhiniṣṭhāyāmapi sāmānyalakṣaṇatvādākāśamiva mṛdrajatasuvarṇabhājaneṣvanugatānupraviṣṭā samā nirviśiṣṭā prāptā sarvakālam / ata evāvasthānirdeśānantaramāha / tasmācchāriputra nānyaḥ sattvadhāturnānyo dharmakāyaḥ / sattvadhātureva dharmakāyaḥ / dharmakāya eva sattvadhātuḥ / advayametadarthena / vyañjanamātrabheda iti
body.translated_text: That non-discriminating natural state of the mind (<s>avikalpacittaprakṛti</s>) of ordinary beings, noble ones, and fully awakened ones — in the three stages respectively, whether in faults, in qualities, or in the culmination of the purification of qualities — because of being a general characteristic, like space in vessels of clay, silver, and gold, it has pervaded and entered equally, without distinction, and is attained at all times. For this very reason, immediately after the exposition of the stages, he says: 'Therefore, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, the <s>sattvadhātu</s> is not one thing and the <s>Dharmakāya</s> another. The <s>sattvadhātu</s> itself is the <s>Dharmakāya</s>; the <s>Dharmakāya</s> itself is the <s>sattvadhātu</s>. These two are non-dual in meaning; there is merely a verbal difference.'

body.text: etāsteva tisṛṣvavasthāsu tathāgatadhātoḥ sarvatragasyāpi tatsaṃkleśavyavadānābhyāmavikārārthamārabhya caturdaśa ślokāḥ / ayaṃ ca teṣāṃ piṇḍārtho veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: With reference to the meaning of the unchangeability of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element — even though it pervades everywhere — in those very three stages through defilement and purification, there are fourteen verses. And the summarized meaning of these is to be understood as follows:

children.translated_text: Because of the connection with faults being adventitious, and because of the connection with qualities being innate,
its <s>dharmatā</s> (essential nature) is unchangeable, the same before and after. ||51||

body.text: dvādaśabhirekena ca ślokena yathākramamaśuddhāvasthāyāmaśuddhaśuddhāvasthāyāṃ ca kleśopakleśadoṣayorāgantukayogāṃccaturdaśamena ślokena suviśuddhāvasthāyāṃ gaṅgānadīvālukāvyativṛttairavinirbhāgairamuktaśiracintyairbuddhaguṇaiḥ prakṛtiyogādākāśadhātoriva paurvāparyeṇa tathāgatadhātoratyantāvikāradharmatā paridīpitā / tatrāśuddhāvasthāyāmavikārārthamārabhya katame dvādaśa ślokāḥ
body.translated_text: By twelve [verses] and one verse, the adventitious connection of the faults of afflictions and secondary afflictions in the impure stage and the impure-and-pure stage respectively [is shown]; and by the fourteenth verse, in the perfectly pure stage, because of the innate connection with <s>Buddha</s>-qualities that exceed the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, that are inseparable, unshakeable, and inconceivable — the utterly unchangeable <s>dharmatā</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element is illuminated, as of the space-element, in its earlier and later [states]. There, with reference to the meaning of unchangeability in the impure stage, what are the twelve verses?

children.translated_text: Just as space, being all-pervading and subtle, is not tainted,
so too, this [element], established in all beings, is not tainted. ||52||
Just as in all world-systems, space is the locus of both arising and perishing,
so too, in the unconditioned element, [there is] the perishing and arising of the sense-faculties. ||53||
Just as space has never been burned by fires,
so too, the fires of death, disease, and old age do not burn this [element]. ||54||
Earth rests upon water, water upon wind, wind rests upon space;
space does not rest upon the elements of wind, water, or earth. ||55||
Similarly, the aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), elements (<s>dhātus</s>), and sense-faculties (<s>indriyas</s>) rest upon <s>karma</s> and afflictions;
<s>Karma</s> and afflictions always rest upon unwise mental engagement (<s>ayoniśomanasikāra</s>). ||56||
Unwise mental engagement rests upon the purity of the mind;
but the natural state of the mind does not rest upon any <s>dharma</s>. ||57||
The aggregates (<s>skandhas</s>), sense-bases (<s>āyatanas</s>), and elements (<s>dhātus</s>) are to be known as like the earth-element;
<s>Karma</s> and afflictions of embodied beings are to be known as like the water-element. ||58||

body.text: ayoniśomanaskāro vijñeyo vāyudhātuvat /
body.translated_text: Unwise mental engagement is to be known as like the wind-element;

body.text: tadamūlāpratiṣṭhānā prakṛtirvyomadhātuvat // 59 //
body.translated_text: the natural state [of the mind], rootless and without foundation, is like the space-element. ||59||

children.translated_text: Unwise mental engagement is the activity [that arises] from the defilement of the natural state of the mind;
from unwise mental engagement arise afflictions and <s>karma</s>. ||60||
Born from the waters of <s>karma</s> and afflictions, the aggregates, sense-bases, and elements
arise and cease, just as those [world-systems undergo] evolution and dissolution. ||61||

children.text: na hetuḥ pratyayo nāpi na sāmagrī na codayaḥ /
children.translated_text: There is no cause, no condition, no assemblage, no arising,
no cessation, and no persistence for the natural state of the mind — like the space-element. ||62||

children.text: cittasya yāsau prakṛtiḥ prabhāsvarā na jātu sā dyauriva yāti vikriyām /
children.translated_text: That natural state of the mind which is luminous (<s>prabhāsvara</s>) never undergoes transformation, like the sky;
but it is defiled by adventitious stains of passion and such — [defilements] born of unreal conceptualization. ||63||

body.text:
kathamanenākāśadṛṣṭāntena tathāgatadhātoraśuddhāvasthāyāmavikāradharmatā paridīpitā /
taducyate /
body.translated_text: How is the unchangeable <s>dharmatā</s> of the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element in the impure stage illuminated by this space-illustration? It is said:

body.text: nābhinirvartayatyenaṃ karmakleśāmbusaṃcayaḥ

children.translated_text: nor does the blazing fire of death, disease, and old age burn it. ||64||

body.translated_text: The accumulation of the waters of <s>karma</s> and afflictions does not produce this [element],

body.text: yadvadayoniśomanaskāravātamaṇḍalasaṃbhūta karmakleśodakarāśiṃ pratītya skandhadhātvāyatanalokanirvṛttyā cittaprakṛtivyomadhātorvivarto na bhavati / tadvadayoniśomanaskārakarmakleśavāyvapskandhapratiṣṭhitasya skandhadhātvāyatanalokasyāstaṃgamāya mṛtyuvyādhijarāgniskandhasamudayādapi tadasaṃvarto veditavyaḥ / ityevamaśuddhāvasthāyāṃ bhājanalokavadaśeṣakleśakarmajanmasaṃkleśasamudayāstagamaṃ'pyākāśavadasaṃskṛtasya tathāgatadhātoranutpādānirodhādatyantamavikāradharmatā paridīpitā / eṣa ca prakṛtiviśuddhimukhaṃ dharmālokamukhamārabhyākāśadṛṣṭānto vistareṇa yathāsūtramanugantavyaḥ / kavirmārṣā kleśāḥ / āloko viśuddhiḥ / durbalāḥ kleśāḥ / balavatī vipaśyanā / āgantukāḥ kleśāḥ / mūlaviśuddhā prakṛtiḥ / parikalpāḥ kleśāḥ / aparikalpā prakṛtiḥ / tadyathā mārṣā iyaṃ mahāpṛthivyapsu pratiṣṭhitā / āpo vāyau pratiṣṭhitāḥ / vāyurākāśe pratiṣṭhitaḥ / apratiṣṭhitaṃ cākāśama / evameṣāṃ caturṇā dhātūnāṃ pṛthivīdhātorabdhātorvāyudhātorākāśadhātureva balī yo dṛḍho 'calo 'nupacayo 'napacayo 'nutpanno 'niruddhaḥ sthitaḥ svarasayogena / tatra ya ete trayo dhātavasta utpādabhaṅgayuktā anavasthitā acirasthāyinaḥ / dṛśyata eṣāṃ vikāro na punarākāśadhātoḥ kaścidvikāraḥ / evameva
body.translated_text: Just as through the arising of the world of aggregates, elements, and sense-bases in dependence upon the mass of water that is <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> (afflictions), born from the wind-circle of <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> (improper mental attention), there is no creation of the space-element that is the nature of mind (<s>cittaprakṛtivyomadhātu</s>)—so too, for the destruction of the world of aggregates, elements, and sense-bases established upon the wind, water, and aggregate of <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>, <s>karma</s>, and <s>kleśas</s>, even from the conflagration of the fire-aggregate of death, disease, and old age, its non-destruction should be understood. Thus, in the impure state, just as with the vessel-world, even despite the arising and cessation of all defilements of affliction, <s>karma</s>, and birth, the utterly changeless nature of the <s>tathāgatadhātu</s>—which, like space, is unconditioned, without arising or cessation—has been illuminated. And this space-simile, beginning from the aspect of natural purity and the aspect of the light of <s>Dharma</s>, is to be understood in detail according to the sūtra: 'Darkness, O <s>Mārṣa</s>, is the afflictions. Light is purity. The afflictions are weak. <s>Vipaśyanā</s> (insight) is powerful. The afflictions are adventitious. The nature is fundamentally pure. The afflictions are imagined. The nature is unimagined. Just as, O <s>Mārṣa</s>, this great earth is established upon water; water is established upon wind; wind is established upon space; but space is unestablished. Thus, among these four elements—earth, water, wind—the space-element alone is powerful, firm, immovable, without increase, without decrease, unborn, unceased, abiding by its own nature. Among those, these three elements are subject to arising and destruction, unstable, not long-lasting. Their change is seen, but no change whatsoever of the space-element is seen. In the same way,

body.text: skandhadhātvāyatanāni karmakleśapratiṣṭhitāni / karmakleśā ayoniśomanaskārapratiṣṭhitāḥ / ayoniśomanaskāraḥ prakṛtipariśuddhipratiṣṭhitaḥ / tata ucyate prakṛtiprabhāsvaraṃ cittamāgantukairupakleśairupakliśyata iti / tatra paścādyo 'yoniśomanaskāro ye ca karmakleśā yāni ca skandhadhātvāyatanāni sarva ete dharmā hetupratyayasaṃgṛhītā utpadyante hetupratyayavisāmagrayā nirudhyante / yā punaḥ sā prakṛtistasyā na heturna pratyayo na sāmagrī notpādo na nirodhaḥ / tatra yathākāśadhātustathā prakṛtiḥ / yathā vāyudhātustathāyoniśomanasikāraḥ / yathābdhātustathā karmakleśāḥ / yathā pṛthivīdhātustathā skandhadhātvāyatanāni / tata ucyante sarvadharmā asāramūlā apratiṣṭhānamūlāḥ śuddhamūlā amūlamūlā iti /
body.translated_text: the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases are established upon <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>; <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s> are established upon <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> (improper mental attention); <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> is established upon natural purity. Therefore it is said: "The mind is naturally luminous (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvara</s>); it is defiled by adventitious defilements." Among these, the subsequent <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>, <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>, and aggregates, elements, and sense-bases—all these dharmas arise as comprised by causes and conditions, and cease through the dissipation of causes and conditions. But that nature itself—it has no cause, no condition, no assemblage, no arising, no cessation. There, as is the space-element, so is the nature; as is the wind-element, so is <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>; as is the water-element, so are <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>; as is the earth-element, so are the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases. Therefore it is said: 'All dharmas have an essenceless root, a foundationless root, a pure root, a rootless root.'

body.text: uktamaśuddhāvasthāyāmavikāralakṣaṇamārabhya prakṛterākāśadhātusādharmya tadāśritasyāyoniśomanasikārasya karmakleśānāṃ ca hetulakṣaṇamārabhya vāyudhātusādharmyamabdhātusādharmya ca tatprabhavasya skandhadhātvāyatanasya vipākalakṣaṇamārabhya pṛthivīdhātusādharmyam / tadvibhavakāraṇasya tu mṛtyuvyādhijarāgnerupasargalakṣaṇamārabhya tejodhātusādharmya noktamiti taducyate /
body.translated_text: Thus has been stated: in the impure state, with reference to the changelessness-characteristic of the nature, its similarity to the space-element; with reference to the cause-characteristic of <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s> dependent upon it and of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>, the similarity to the wind-element and the water-element; and with reference to the ripening-characteristic of the aggregates, elements, and sense-bases that arise from those, the similarity to the earth-element. But the similarity to the fire-element—regarding the calamity-characteristic of the fire of death, disease, and old age that causes their dissolution—has not been stated. Therefore it is stated:

children.translated_text: The three fires—the fire at the end of an age, the fire of hell, and the ordinary fire—in order,
are the three similes for the fires of death, disease, and old age. (65)

body.text: tribhiḥ kāraṇairyathākramaṃ mṛtyuvyādhijarāṇāmagnisādharmya veditavyam / ṣaḍāyatananirmamīkaraṇato vicitrakāraṇānubhavanataḥ saṃskāraparipākopanayanataḥ / ebhirapi mṛtyuvyādhijarāgnibhiravikāratvamārabhya tathāgatadhātoraśuddhāvasthāyāmidamuktam / lokavyavahāra epa bhagavan mṛta iti vā jāta iti
body.translated_text: The similarity of death, disease, and old age to fire should be understood through three reasons, in order: because of the destruction of the six sense-bases, because of causing the experience of various painful causes, and because of leading to the ripening of the <s>saṃskāras</s> (formations). Even with reference to these fires of death, disease, and old age, the changelessness of the <s>tathāgatadhātu</s> in the impure state has been stated: 'This is merely a worldly convention, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, to say "one has died" or "one has been born."'

body.text: vā / mṛta iti bhagavannindriyoparodha eṣaḥ / jāta iti bhagavan navānāmindriyāṇāṃ prādurbhāva eṣa / na kṣunarbhagavaṃstathāgatagarbho jāyate vā jīryati vā mriyate vā cyavate votpadyate vā ! tatkasmāddheto / saṃskṛtalakṣaṇaviṣayavyativṛtto bhagavaṃstathāgatagarbho nityo dhruvaḥ śivaḥ śāśvata iti /
body.translated_text: '"Died," O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the cessation of the faculties. "Born," O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the appearance of new faculties. But, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> is not born, does not age, does not die, does not pass away, and does not arise! Why is that? Because, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> has transcended the domain of conditioned characteristics; it is permanent, stable, auspicious, and eternal.'

body.text: tatrāśuddhaśuddhāvasthāyāmavikārārthamārabhya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: Regarding the impure-and-pure state, with reference to the meaning of changelessness, a verse:

children.translated_text: Free from creation, destruction, disease, and old age—having understood the nature of this very [element] as not otherwise,
even after death from the calamities of birth and the rest, the wise ones, out of the arising of compassion, embrace [rebirth] in the world. (66)

body.text: anena kiṃ darśayati /
body.translated_text: What does this show?

children.translated_text: The root of the suffering of death, disease, and old age has been extracted by the Noble Ones;
Birth arises from the power of <s>karma</s> and <s>kleśas</s>; in their absence, that [birth] does not exist for them. (67)

body.text: asya khalu mṛtyuvyādhijarāduḥkhavahreraśuddhāvasthāyāmayoniśomanasikārakarmakleśapūrvikā jātirindhanamivopādānaṃ bhavati / yasya manomayātmabhāvapratilabdheṣu bodhisattveṣu śuddhāśuddhāvasthāyāmatyantamanābhāsagamanāditarasyātyantamanujjvalanaṃ prajñāyate /
body.translated_text: Indeed, for this [tathāgatadhātu] that carries the suffering of death, disease, and old age, in the impure state, birth preceded by <s>ayoniśomanaskāra</s>, <s>karma</s>, and <s>kleśas</s> serves as fuel, as it were. For <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have obtained mind-made bodies (<s>manomayātmabhāva</s>), in the impure-pure state, because [the fuel] has utterly ceased to approach them, the utter non-blazing of the other [fire] is discerned.

body.text: janmamṛtyujarāvyādhīn darśayanti kṛpātmakāḥ /
body.translated_text: Those whose nature is compassion display birth, death, old age, and disease;

body.text: jātyādivi nivṛttāśca yathābhūtasya darśanāt // 68 //
body.translated_text: but they have ceased from birth and the rest, because of their vision of reality as it truly is. (68)
