body.text: kuśalamūlasaṃyojanāddhi bodhisattvoḥ saṃcintyopapattivaśitāsaṃniḥśrayeṇa karuṇayā traidhātuke saṃśliṣyante / jātimapyupadarśayanti jarāmapi vyādhimapi maraṇamapyupadarśayanti / na ca teṣāmime jātyādayo dharmāḥ saṃvidyante / yathāpi tadasyaiva dhātoryathābhūtamajātyanutpattidarśanāt / sā punariyaṃ bodhisattvavasthā vistareṇa yathāsūtramanugantavyā / yadāha / katame ca te saṃsārapravartakāḥ kuśalamūlasaṃprayuktāḥ kleśāḥ / yaduta puṇyasaṃbhāraparyeṣṭyatṛptatā / saṃcintyabhavopapattiparigrahaḥ / buddhasamavadhānaprārthanā / sattvaparipākāparikhedaḥ / saddharmaparigrahodyogaḥ / sattvakiṃkaraṇīyotsukatā / dharmarāgānuśayānutsargaḥ / pāramitāsaṃyojanānāmaparityāgaḥ / ityete sāgaramate kuśalamūlasaṃprayuktāḥ kleśā yairbodhisattvāḥ saṃśliṣyante / na khalu kleśadoṣairlipyante / āha punaḥ / yadā bhagavan kuśalamūlāni tatkena kāraṇena kleśā ityucyante / āha / tathā hi sāgaramate ebhirevaṃrūpaiḥ kleśairbodhisattvāstraidhātuke śliṣyante / kleśasaṃbhūtaṃ ca traidhātukam / tatra bodhisattvā upāyakauśalena ca kuśalamūlavalānvādhānena ca saṃcintya traidhātuke śliṣyante / tenocyante kuśalamūlasaṃprayuktāḥ kleśā iti / yāvadeva traidhātuke śleṣatayā na punaścittopakleśatayā /
body.translated_text: For through the conjunction with wholesome roots, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, by means of the mastery of deliberately-willed rebirth (<s>saṃcintyopapattivaśitā</s>) and supported by compassion, attach themselves to the triple world. They display birth, old age, disease, and death. But these dharmas of birth and the rest do not actually exist for them—because of their vision of the true non-arising and non-origination of this very <s>dhātu</s>. And this <s>Bodhisattva</s>-state is to be understood in detail according to the sūtra. As it says: 'And what are those afflictions connected with wholesome roots that cause the continuation of <s>saṃsāra</s>? Namely: insatiability in seeking the accumulation of merit; the deliberate embracing of existence and rebirth; aspiration for encounter with the <s>Buddha</s>; unwearying patience in the maturation of beings; zeal for the effort of embracing the true <s>Dharma</s>; eagerness for service to beings; non-abandonment of the latent tendency of passion for the <s>Dharma</s>; non-relinquishment of the conjunction with the <s>Pāramitās</s> (perfections). These, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, are the afflictions connected with wholesome roots, by which <s>Bodhisattvas</s> attach themselves [to the world]. But they are not defiled by the faults of afflictions.' And he further said: 'If, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, they are wholesome roots, for what reason are they called afflictions?' He replied: 'Because, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, through afflictions of this kind, <s>Bodhisattvas</s> attach themselves to the triple world. And the triple world is born from afflictions. There, <s>Bodhisattvas</s>, through skill in means and the power of wholesome roots, deliberately attach themselves to the triple world. Therefore they are called afflictions connected with wholesome roots—only insofar as they cause attachment to the triple world, but not insofar as they defile the mind.'

body.text: syādyathāpi nāma sāgaramate śreṣṭhino gṛhapatereka putraka iṣṭaḥ kāntaḥ priyo manāpo 'prakṛtikūlo darśanena sa ca dārako bālabhāvena nṛtyanneva mīḍhakūpe prapateta / atha te tasya dārakasya mātṛjñātayaḥ paśyeyustaṃ dārakaṃ mīḍhakūpe prapatitam / dṛṣṭvā ca gambhīraṃ niśvaseyuḥ śoceyuḥ parideveran / na punastaṃ mīḍhakūpamavaruhya
body.translated_text: 'Just as, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, the beloved, dear, and cherished only son of a wealthy merchant householder, pleasant to behold, while playing in childishness might fall into a cesspit. Then the boy's maternal relatives, seeing the boy fallen into the cesspit, would sigh deeply, grieve, and lament, but would not descend into that cesspit

body.text: taṃ dārakamadhyālamberan / atha tasya dārakasya pitā taṃ pradeśamāgacchet / sa paśyetaikaputrakaṃ mīḍhakūpe prapatitaṃ dṛṣṭvā ca śīghraśīghraṃ tvaramāṇarūpa ekaputrakādhyāśayapremānunoto 'jugupsamānastaṃ mīḍhakūpamavaruhyaikaputrakamabhyutkṣipet / iti hi sāgaramate upamaiṣā kṛtā yāvadevārthasya vijñaptaye / kaḥ prabandho draṣṭavyaḥ / mīḍhakūpa iti sāgaramate traidhātukasyaitadadhivacanam / ekaputraka iti sattvānāmetadadhivacanam / sarvasattveṣu hi bodhisattvasyaikaputrasaṃjñā pratyupasthitā bhavati / mātṛjñātaya iti śrāvakapratyekabuddhayānīyānāṃ pudgalānāmetadadhivacanaṃ ye saṃsāraprapatitān sattvān dṛṣṭvā śocanti paridevante na punaḥ śamarthā bhavantyabhyutkṣeptum / śreṣṭhī gṛhapatiriti bodhisattvasyaitadadhivacanaṃ yaḥ śucirvimalo nirmalacitto 'saṃskṛtadharmapratyakṣagataḥ saṃcintya traidhātuke pratisaṃdadhāti sattvaparipākārtham / seyaṃ sāgaramate bodhisattvasya mahākaruṇā yadatyantaparimuktaḥ sarvabandhanebhyaḥ punareva bhavopapattimupādadāti / upāyakauśalyaprajñāparigṛhītaśca saṃkleśairna lipyate / sarva kleśabandhaprahāṇāya ca sattvebhyo dharma deśayatīti / tadanena sūtrapadanirdeśena parahītakriyārtha vaśino bodhisattvasya saṃcintyabhavopapattau kuśalamūlakaruṇāvalābhyāmupaśleṣādupāyaprajñābalābhyāṃ ca tadasaṃkleśādaśuddhaśuddhāvasthā paridīpitā /
body.translated_text: to pull up the boy. Then the boy's father would come to that place. Seeing the only son fallen into the cesspit, quickly hastening, impelled by the love of resolve for his only son, without disgust he would descend into that cesspit and pull up the only son.' And this simile, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, was given just for the purpose of conveying the meaning. What connection should be seen? 'Cesspit,' O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, is a designation for the triple world. 'Only son' is a designation for beings—for the <s>Bodhisattva</s> has the perception of an only son present toward all beings. 'Maternal relatives' is a designation for persons following the <s>Śrāvaka</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddha</s> vehicles, who upon seeing beings fallen into <s>saṃsāra</s>, grieve and lament but are unable to pull them up. 'Wealthy merchant householder' is a designation for the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, who is pure, stainless, of spotless mind, who has directly realized the unconditioned dharmas, and who deliberately reconnects to the triple world for the purpose of maturing beings. This, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, is the great compassion of the <s>Bodhisattva</s>: that though utterly liberated from all bonds, he again takes up existence and rebirth. And guarded by skill in means and wisdom, he is not defiled by defilements. And he teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to beings for the abandonment of all bonds of afflictions.' Thus, by this sūtra-passage, the impure-pure state is illuminated: for a <s>Bodhisattva</s> who is master [of rebirth] for the purpose of benefiting others, through attachment to deliberate existence-rebirth by the power of wholesome roots and compassion, and through non-defilement therein by the power of means and wisdom.

body.text: tatra yadā bodhisattvo yathābhūtājātyanutpattidarśanamāgamya tathāgatadhatorimāṃ bodhisattvadharmatāmanuprāpnoti tathā vistareṇa yathāsūtramanugantavyam / yadāha / paśya sāgaramate dharmāṇāmasāratāmakārakatāṃ nirātmatāṃ niḥsattvatāṃ
body.translated_text: There, when a <s>Bodhisattva</s>, having arrived at the vision of the true non-arising and non-origination [of all dharmas], attains this <s>Bodhisattva</s>-<s>dharmatā</s> (nature) of the <s>tathāgatadhātu</s>—this is to be understood in detail according to the sūtra. As it says: 'See, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, the essencelessness, non-agency, selflessness, beinglessness,

body.text: nirjīvatāṃ niḥpudgalatāmasvāmikatām / yatra hi nāma yatheṣyante tathā viṭhapyante viṭhapitāśca samānā na cetayanti na prakalpayanti / imāṃ sāgaramate dharmaviṭhapanāmadhimucya bodhisattvo na kasmiṃściddharme parikhedamutpādayati / tasyaiva jñānadarśanaṃ śuci śuddhaṃ bhavati / nātra kaścidupakāro vāpakāro vā kriyata iti / evaṃ ca dharmāṇāṃ dharmatāṃ yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / evaṃ ca mahākaruṇāsaṃnāhaṃ na tyajati / syādyathāpi nāma sāgaramata'nargha viḍūryamaṇiratnaṃ svavadāpitaṃ supariśuddhaṃ suvimalaṃ kardamaparikṣiptaṃ varṣasahasramavatiṣṭheta / tadvarṣasahasrātyayena tataḥ kardamādabhyutkṣipya loḍyeta payavadāyeta / tatsudhautaṃ pariśodhitaṃ paryavadāpitaṃ samānaṃ tameva śuddhavimalamaṇiratnasvabhāvaṃ na jahyāt / evameva sāgaramate bodhisattvaḥ sattvānāṃ prakṛtiprabhāsvaratāṃ cittasya prajānāti / tāṃ punarāgantuko pakleśopakliṣṭāṃ paśyati / tatra bodhisattvasyaivaṃ bhavati / naite kleśāḥ sattvānāṃ cittaprakṛtiprabhāsvaratāyāṃ praviṣṭāḥ / āgantukā ete kleśā abhūtaparikalpasamutthitāḥ / śaknuyāmahaṃ punareṣāṃ sattvānāmāgantukleśāpanayanāya dharma deśayitumiti / evamasya nāvalīyanācittamutpadyate / tasya bhūyasyā mātrayā sarvasattvānāmantike pramokṣacittotpāda utpadyate / evaṃ cāsya bhavati / naiteṣāṃ kleśānāṃ kiṃcidvalaṃ sthāma vā / abalā durbalā ete kleśāḥ / naiteṣāṃ kiṃcidbhūtapratiṣṭhānam / abhūtaparikalpita
body.translated_text: lifelessness, personlessness, and ownerlessness of dharmas! Where they are established as desired, once established, they do not think and do not conceptualize.' Having accepted, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, this establishment of dharmas (<s>dharmaviṭhapanā</s>), the <s>Bodhisattva</s> does not generate weariness toward any dharma. His knowledge and vision become pure and clean. No benefit or harm is done here. Thus he truly knows the <s>dharmatā</s> (true nature) of all dharmas. And he does not abandon the armor of great compassion. 'Just as, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, a priceless <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli) gem, self-purified, thoroughly pure, and perfectly stainless, were to remain immersed in mud for a thousand years—after the passage of a thousand years, it would be extracted from that mud, washed, and cleansed. Once washed, purified, and cleansed, it would not lose its very nature as a pure and stainless gem. In the same way, O <s>Sāgaramati</s>, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> knows the naturally luminous nature (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvaratā</s>) of beings' minds. And he perceives it as defiled by adventitious defilements. There, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> thinks thus: "These afflictions have not entered the naturally luminous nature of beings' minds. These afflictions are adventitious, arisen from false conceptualization (<s>abhūtaparikalpa</s>). Could I teach the <s>Dharma</s> to these beings for the removal of their adventitious afflictions?" Thus a mind of non-timidity arises in him. And to a greater degree, toward all beings, the thought of liberation arises in him. And he thinks thus: "These afflictions have no strength or power whatsoever. These afflictions are powerless and weak. They have no real foundation. They are falsely imagined,

body.text: ete kleśāḥ / te yathābhūtayoniśomanasikāranirīkṣitā na kupyanti / te 'smābhistathā pratyavekṣitavyā yathā na bhūyaḥ śliṣyeyuḥ / aśleṣo hi kleśānāṃ sādhurna punaḥ śleṣaḥ / yadyahaṃ kleśānāṃ ślipyeya tatkathaṃ kleśabandhanabaddhānāṃ sattvānāṃ kleśabandhanaprahāṇaya dharma deśayeyam / hanta vayaṃ kleśānāṃ ca na śliṣyāmahe kleśabandhanaprahāṇāya ca sattvebhyo dharma śayiṣyāmaḥ / ye punaste saṃsāraprabandhakāḥ kuśalanasaṃprayuktāḥ kleśāsteṣvasmābhiḥ sattvaparipākāya śleṣṭavyamiti /
body.translated_text: These are the afflictions. When examined through thorough mental attention in accordance with reality (<s>yathābhūtayoniśomanasikāra</s>), they do not arise. They are to be observed by us in such a way that they do not cling again. For the non-clinging of afflictions is good, not their clinging. If I were to cling to afflictions, how could I teach the <s>Dharma</s> for the abandonment of the bonds of afflictions to beings bound by the bonds of afflictions? Come, we shall not cling to afflictions, and we shall teach the <s>Dharma</s> to beings for the abandonment of the bonds of afflictions. But those afflictions that perpetuate <s>saṃsāra</s> and are associated with the wholesome—to those we must cling for the maturation of beings.

body.text: saṃsāraḥ punariha traidhātukapratibimbakamanāsravadhātau manomayaṃ kāyatrayamabhipretam / taddhyanāsravakuśalamūlābhisaṃskṛtatvāt saṃsāraḥ / sāsravakarmakleśānabhisaṃskṛtatvānnirvāṇamapi tat / yadadhikṛtyāha / tasmādbhagavannasti saṃskṛto 'pyasaṃskṛto 'pi saṃsāraḥ / asti saṃskṛtamapyasaṃskṛtamapi nirvāṇamiti / tatra saṃskṛtā saṃskṛtasaṃsṛṣṭacittacaitasikasamudācārayogādiyamaśuddhaśuddhāvasthetyucyate / sā punarāsravakṣayābhijñābhimukhyasaṅgaprajñāpāramitabhāvanayā mahākaruṇābhāvanayā ca sarvasattvadhātuparitrāṇāya tadasākṣātkaraṇādābhimukhyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau prādhānyena vyavasthāpyate /
body.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s> here means the three mind-made bodies (<s>manomayakāyatraya</s>) that are reflections of the three realms in the undefiled element. Because they are conditioned by undefiled roots of virtue, it is <s>saṃsāra</s>; because they are not conditioned by defiled <s>karma</s> and afflictions, it is also <s>nirvāṇa</s>. With reference to which he said: 'Therefore, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, there is <s>saṃsāra</s> that is both conditioned and unconditioned; there is <s>nirvāṇa</s> that is both conditioned and unconditioned.' There, the conditioned [aspect]—because of the conjunction with the functioning of conditioned mind and mental factors mixed with the conditioned—this is called the impure-pure state. And this is established principally at the <s>Abhimukhī</s> (Facing Forward) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, through the cultivation of the <s>prajñāpāramitā</s> of non-attachment directed toward the superknowledge of the destruction of defilements, and through the cultivation of great compassion for the protection of all the realm of beings, [arising] from the non-direct-realization of that [destruction of defilements].

body.text: yathoktamātravakṣayajñānamārabhya nagarodāharaṇam / evameva kulaputra bodhisattvo manatā yatnena mahata vīryeṇa dṛḍhayādhyāśayapratipattyā pañcābhijñā utpādayati / tasya dhyānābhijñaparikarmakṛtacittasyāsravakṣayo 'bhimukhībhavati / sa mahākaruṇācittotpādena sarvasattvaparitrāṇāyāsravakṣayajñāne parijayaṃ kṛtvā punarapi
body.translated_text: As stated, beginning with the knowledge of the destruction of defilements, the illustration of the city [is given]: 'Even so, O son of good family, the <s>Bodhisattva</s>, with mindful effort, with great energy, with firm aspiration and practice, generates the five superknowledges (<s>abhijñā</s>). For the one whose mind has been prepared through <s>dhyāna</s> and superknowledge, the destruction of defilements becomes imminent. Having, through the generation of the mind of great compassion, gained mastery in the knowledge of the destruction of defilements for the protection of all beings, again'

body.text:
suparikarmakṛtacetāḥ ṣaṣṭhyāmasaṅgaprajñotpādādāsravakṣaye 'bhimukhībhavati / evamasyāmābhimukhyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmāvāsravakṣayasākṣātkaraṇavaśitvalābhino bodhisattvasya viśuddhāvasthā / paridīpitā / tasyaivamātmanā samyakpratipannasya parānapi cāsyāmeva samyakpratipattau sthāpayiṣyāmīti mahākaruṇayā vipratipannasattvaparitrāṇābhiprāyasya śamasukhānāsvādanatayā tadupāyakṛtaparijayasya saṃsārābhimukhasattvāpekṣayā nirvāṇavimukhasya bodhyaṅgaparipūraṇāya dhyānairvihṛtya punaḥ kāmadhātau saṃcintyopapattiparigrahaṇato yāvadāśu sattvānāmarthaṃ kartukāmasya vicitratiryagyonigatajātakaprabhedena pṛthagjanātmabhāvasaṃdarśanavibhutvalābhino 'viśuddhāvasthā paridīpitā /
aparaḥ ślokārthaḥ
body.translated_text: 'with a well-prepared mind, through the arising of non-attached <s>prajñā</s> on the sixth [stage], [the destruction of defilements] becomes imminent.' Thus, at this <s>Abhimukhī</s> <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage, the pure state of the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has attained mastery in directly realizing the destruction of defilements is illustrated. For that one who has thus practiced correctly himself, and who, with great compassion, intends to protect beings who have gone astray by establishing them too in this very correct practice—who, through not savoring the bliss of tranquility, has gained mastery in the means thereof, who, regarding beings inclined toward <s>saṃsāra</s>, turns away from <s>nirvāṇa</s>, and who, having dwelt in <s>dhyānas</s> for the fulfillment of the limbs of awakening, again deliberately takes birth in the desire realm—the impure state is illustrated, up to the one who, desiring to quickly accomplish the welfare of beings, attains the power to display various ordinary-being existences through the varieties of animal births and such. The other meaning of the verse:

children.translated_text: Having examined this <s>dharmatā</s> (nature of reality) [as] unchanging, the son of the <s>Jina</s>—
that which is seen by those blinded by ignorance in birth and so forth—that is wonderful. // 69 //
Therefore, when the kinsman of the world, [endowed with] supreme skillful means and compassion,
having attained the domain of the nobles, is seen in the domain of the childish— // 70 //
He has transcended the entire world, yet has not departed from the world;
he moves in the world for the sake of the world, unstained by worldly defilements. // 71 //
Just as a lotus born in water is not stained by water,
so too, though born in the world, he is not stained by worldly phenomena. // 72 //

body.text: nityojjvalitabuddhiśca kṛtyasaṃpādane 'gnivat /
body.translated_text: His intelligence is ever blazing, like fire in the accomplishment of duties;

body.text: śāntadhyānasamāpattipratipannaśca sarvadā // 73 //
body.translated_text: and he is always engaged in the attainments of peaceful <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation). // 73 //

children.translated_text: Due to the force of prior penetration and the departure of all conceptualizations,

children.text: na punaḥ kurute yatnaṃ paripākāya dehinām // 74 //
children.translated_text: he no longer makes effort for the maturation of embodied beings. // 74 //

children.text: yo yathā yena vaineyo manyate 'sau tathaiva tat /
children.translated_text: Whoever is to be trained, however, and by whatever [means]—he considers just so;
whether by teaching, by the two form-bodies (<s>rūpakāya</s>), by conduct, or by deportment. // 75 //
Without effort, for this one whose understanding is unimpeded, always,
in the world bounded by space, the welfare of beings proceeds. // 76 //
Having attained this state, the <s>Bodhisattva</s> attains equality with the <s>Tathāgatas</s>
in the worlds with respect to ferrying beings across. // 77 //
Yet the difference between an atom and the earth, a hoof-print and the ocean—
that is the difference between <s>Bodhisattvas</s> and the <s>Buddha</s>. // 78 //

body.text: eṣāṃ daśānāṃ ślokānāṃ yathākramaṃ navabhiḥ ślokaiḥ pramuditāyā bodhisattvabhūmeradhaśca saṃkleśaparamatāṃ daśamena ślokena dharmameghāyā bodhisattvabhūmerūrdhvaṃ viśuddhiparamatāmupanidhāya samāsataścaturṇāṃ bodhisattvānāṃ daśasu bodhisattvabhūmiṣu viśuddhiraviśuddhiśca parīdīpitā / catvāro bodhisattvāḥ prathamacittotpādikaḥ / caryāpratipannaḥ / avaivartikaḥ / ekajātipratibaddha iti / tatra prathamadvitīyābhyāṃ ślokābhyāmanādikālikamadṛṣṭapūrvaprathamalokottaradharmatāprativedhāta pramuditāyāṃ bhūmau prathamacittotpādikabodhisattvagaṇaviśuddhi lakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitam / tritīyacaturthābhyāṃ ślokābhyāmanupaliptacaryācaraṇādvimalāṃ
body.translated_text: Of these ten verses, by nine verses in order, having set forth the predominance of defilement below the <s>Pramuditā</s> (Joyful) <s>Bodhisattva</s> stage and by the tenth verse the predominance of purification above the <s>Dharmameghā</s> (Cloud of Dharma) stage, in brief the purification and non-purification of four [types of] <s>Bodhisattvas</s> on the ten <s>Bodhisattva</s> stages has been illustrated. The four <s>Bodhisattvas</s> are: the newly-generated-mind one, the practice-engaged one, the non-regressing one, and the one-birth-bound one. There, by the first and second verses, the characteristic of the purification of the group of newly-generated-mind <s>Bodhisattvas</s> on the <s>Pramuditā</s> stage is illustrated—due to the penetration of the unprecedented, first supramundane <s>dharmatā</s> since beginningless time.

body.text: bhūmimupādāya yāvadadūraṃgamāyāṃ bhūmau caryāpratipannabodhisattvaguṇaviśuddhilakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitam / pañcamena ślokena nirantaramahabodhisamudāgamaprayogasamādhiṣu vyavasthitatvādacalāyāṃ bhūmāvavaivartikabodhisattvaguṇaviśuddhilakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitam / ṣaṣṭhena saptamenāṣṭamena ca ślokena sakalasvaparārthasaṃpādanopāyaniṣṭhāgatasya buddhabhūmyekacaramajanmapratibaddhatvādanuttaraparamābhisaṃbodhiprāpterdharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmāvekajātipratibaddhabodhisattvaguṇaviśuddhilakṣaṇaṃ paridīpitam / navamena daśamena ca ślokena parārthamātmārtha cārabhya niṣṭhāgatabodhisattvatathāgatayorguṇaviśuddheraviśeṣo viśeṣaśca paridīpitaḥ /
body.translated_text: From the <s>Vimalā</s> (Stainless) stage onward, due to engaging in unstained conduct, up to the <s>Dūraṅgamā</s> (Far-Going) stage, the characteristic of quality-purification of practice-engaged <s>Bodhisattvas</s> is illustrated. By the fifth verse, because of being established in the meditative concentrations of uninterrupted endeavor toward great awakening, the characteristic of quality-purification of non-regressing <s>Bodhisattvas</s> on the <s>Acalā</s> (Immovable) stage is illustrated. By the sixth, seventh, and eighth verses, having reached the culmination of the means for accomplishing all benefits of self and others, because of being bound to the very last birth before the <s>Buddha</s>-stage, the characteristic of quality-purification of one-birth-bound <s>Bodhisattvas</s> on the <s>Dharmameghā</s> stage is illustrated—[those] who will attain unsurpassed perfect awakening. By the ninth and tenth verses, with reference to the benefit of others and of self, the non-difference and difference in quality-purification between the <s>Bodhisattva</s> who has reached the culmination and the <s>Tathāgata</s> is illustrated.

body.text: tatra suviśuddhā vasthāyāmavikārārthamārabhya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, regarding the meaning of unchangeability in the supremely pure state, a verse:

children.translated_text: Due to being conjoined with the qualities of unalterable nature and inexhaustible <s>dharma</s>, a refuge for the world, at the limit of the future,
always non-dual due to non-conceptualization, of indestructible nature yet of uncreated essence. // 79 //

body.text: anena kiṃ darśayati /
body.translated_text: What does this show?

children.text: na jāyate na mriyate bodhyate no na jīryate /
children.translated_text: He is not born, does not die, is not [newly] enlightened, and does not age;
this is due to permanence, stability, auspiciousness, and eternality. // 80 //
He is not born, due to permanence, through mind-made existences;
due to stability, he does not die through inconceivable transformation. // 81 //

body.text: vāsanāvyādhibhiḥ sūkṣmairbādhyate na śivatvataḥ /
body.translated_text: He is not afflicted by subtle habitual-tendency diseases, due to auspiciousness;

body.text: anāsravābhisaṃskāraiḥ śāśvatatvānna jīryate // 82 //
body.translated_text: due to eternality, he does not age through undefiled conditioned formations. // 82 //

body.text: sakha lveṣa tathāgatathāturbuddhabhūmāvatyantavimalaviśuddhaprabhāsvaratāyāṃ svaprakṛtau sthitaḥ pūrvāntamupādāya nityatvānna punarjāyate manomayairātmabhāvaiḥ / aparāntamupādāya dhruvatvānna punarmriyate 'cintyapāriṇāmikyā cyutyā / pūrvāparāntamupādāya śivatvānna punarvādhyate 'vidyāvāsabhūmiparigraheṇa / yaścaivamanarthāpatitaḥ sa śāśvatatvānna punarjīryatyanāsravakarmaphalapariṇāmena /
body.translated_text: Indeed, this <s>Tathāgata</s>-element, established in its own nature at the <s>Buddha</s>-stage of supremely stainless, pure, luminous [reality]—with reference to the past, due to permanence, he is not born again through mind-made existences; with reference to the future, due to stability, he does not die again through inconceivable transformative death; with reference to past and future together, due to auspiciousness, he is not afflicted again by grasping the ground of the habitual tendencies of ignorance; and one who has thus arrived at this state, due to eternality, does not age again through the ripening of the fruit of undefiled <s>karma</s>.

children.text: tatra dvābhyāmatha dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ yathākramam /
children.translated_text: There, by two and then by two, by two and by two, in order,
the meanings of permanence and so forth are to be understood through [pairs of] terms in the unconditioned state. // 83 //

body.text: tadeṣāmasaṃskṛtadhātau caturṇā nityadhruvaśivaśāśvapadānāṃ yathākramamekaikasya padasya dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāmuddeśanirdeśapadābhyāmarthapravibhāgo yathāsūtramanugantavyaḥ / yadāha / nityo 'yaṃ śāriputra dharmakāyo 'nanyatvadharmākṣayadharmatayā / dhruvo 'yaṃ śāriputradharmakāyo dhruvaśaraṇo 'parāntakoṭīsamatayā / śivo 'yaṃ śāriputra dharmakāyo 'dvayadharmāvikalpadharmatayā / śāśvato 'yaṃ śāriputra dharmakāyo 'vināśadharmākṛtrimadharmatayeti /
body.translated_text: Thus, in the unconditioned element, the detailed analysis of the meaning of each of these four terms—permanent, stable, auspicious, and eternal—is to be understood, in order, through two pairs of indicative and explanatory terms, in accordance with the <s>sūtra</s>. As he said: 'This <s>dharmakāya</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, is permanent, due to its nature of being unalterable and of inexhaustible <s>dharma</s>. This <s>dharmakāya</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, is stable, a stable refuge, due to its equality with the limit of the future. This <s>dharmakāya</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, is auspicious, due to its nature of non-dual <s>dharma</s> and non-conceptual <s>dharma</s>. This <s>dharmakāya</s>, O <s>Śāriputra</s>, is eternal, due to its nature of indestructible <s>dharma</s> and uncreated <s>dharma</s>.'

body.text: asyāmeva viśuddhāvasthāyāmatyantavyavadā naniṣṭhāgamanalakṣaṇasya tathāgatagarbhasyā saṃbhedārthamārabhya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: In this very pure state, regarding the meaning of the non-disintegration of the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> characterized by having reached the culmination of ultimate purification, a verse:

children.text: sa dharmakāyaḥ sa tathāgato yatastadāryasatyaṃ paramārthanirvṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: He is the <s>dharmakāya</s>, he is the <s>Tathāgata</s>, from whom comes that noble truth, the ultimate cessation (<s>nirvṛti</s>);
therefore, apart from Buddhahood, there is no cessation, due to the inseparability of qualities, like the sun's rays [from the sun]. // 84 //

body.text: tatra pūrvaślokārdhena ki darśayati /
body.translated_text: There, what does the first half of the verse show?

children.translated_text: The synonyms beginning with <s>dharmakāya</s> are to be understood, in brief,
as four in the undefiled element, through a fourfold division of meaning. // 85 //

body.text: samāsato 'nāsrave dhātau tathāgatagarbhe caturo 'rthānadhikṛtya catvāro nāmaparyāyā veditavyāḥ / catvāro 'rthāḥ katame /
body.translated_text: In brief, in the undefiled element, in the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>, four synonyms are to be understood with reference to four meanings. What are the four meanings?

children.translated_text: The inseparability of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, the arriving of that <s>gotra</s> (lineage) [at its fruit],
the nature of being non-deceptive and non-false, and primordial natural quiescence. // 86 //

body.text: buddhadharmāvinirbhāgārthaḥ / yamadhikṛtyoktam / aśūnyo bhagavaṃstathāgatagarbho gaṅgāanadīvālukāvyativṛttairavinirbhāgairamuktajñairacintyairbuddhadharmairiti / tadgotrasya prakṛteracintyaprakārasamudāgamārthaḥ / yamadhikṛtyoktam / ṣaḍāyatanaviśeṣaḥ sa tādṛśaḥ paraṃparāgato 'nādikāliko dharmatāpratilabdha iti / amṛṣāmopārthaḥ / yamadhikṛtyoktam / tatra paramārthasatyaṃ yadidamamoṣadharmi nirvāṇam / tatkasmāddhetoḥ / nityaṃ tadgotraṃ samadharmatayeti / atyantopaśamārthaḥ / yamadhikṛtyoktam / ādiparinirvṛta eva tathāgato 'rhan samyaksaṃbuddho 'nutpanno 'niruddha
body.translated_text: The meaning of the inseparability of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities—with reference to which it was said: 'The <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is not empty of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities that are inseparable, that exceed the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river, that are unfreed knowledge, inconceivable.' The meaning of the arriving of that <s>gotra</s> (nature) at its inconceivable mode of accomplishment—with reference to which it was said: 'That special configuration of the six sense-bases, such as it is, transmitted from generation to generation, beginningless in time, obtained by the nature of reality.' The meaning of being non-deceptive—with reference to which it was said: 'Therein, ultimate truth is that whose nature is non-deception, namely <s>nirvāṇa</s>. For what reason? Because that <s>gotra</s> is permanent by virtue of the equality of <s>dharma</s>.' The meaning of ultimate quiescence—with reference to which it was said: 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>, the <s>Arhat</s>, the perfectly awakened one is primordially in complete cessation, unborn, unarisen'

body.text: iti / eṣu caturṣvartheṣu yathāsaṃkhyāmima catvāro nāmaparyāyā bhavanti / tadyathā dharmakāyastathāgata paramārthasatyaṃ nirvāṇamiti / yata evamāha / tathāgatagarbha iti śāriputra dharmakāyasyaitadadhivacanamiti / nānyo bhagavaṃstathāgato 'nyo dharmakāyaḥ / dharmakāya eva bhagavaṃstathāgata iti / duḥkhanirodhanāmnā bhagavannevaṃguṇasamanvāgatastathāgatadharmakāyo deśita iti / nirvāṇadhāturiti bhagavaṃstathāgatadharmakāyasyaitadadhivacanamiti /
body.translated_text: In these four meanings, these four synonyms correspond in order: namely, <s>dharmakāya</s>, <s>Tathāgata</s>, ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>), and <s>nirvāṇa</s>. As he thus said: 'O <s>Śāriputra</s>, <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> is a designation for the <s>dharmakāya</s>.' 'The <s>Tathāgata</s>, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is not other than the <s>dharmakāya</s>. The <s>dharmakāya</s> itself, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is the <s>Tathāgata</s>.' 'O <s>Bhagavan</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>dharmakāya</s>, endowed with such qualities, has been taught under the name "cessation of suffering."' '<s>Nirvāṇadhātu</s>, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is a designation for the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>dharmakāya</s>.'

body.text: tatrāpareṇa ślokārdhena kiṃ darśayati /
body.translated_text: There, what does the latter half of the verse show?

children.translated_text: Awakening to all aspects, the uprooting of defilements together with their residual impressions,
Buddhahood and <s>nirvāṇa</s>—these two are non-dual in the ultimate sense. // 87 //

body.text: yata ete catvāro 'nāsravadhātuparyāyāstathāgatadhātāvekasminnabhinne 'rthe samavasaranti / ata eṣāmekārthatvādadvayadharmanayamukhena yacca sarvākārasarvadharmābhisaṃbodhādruddhatvamityuktaṃ yacca mahābhisaṃbodhāt savāsanamalaprahāṇānnirvāṇamityuktametadubhayamanāsrave dhātāvadvayamiti draṣṭavyamabhinnamacchinnam /
body.translated_text: Since these four synonyms of the undefiled element converge in a single, undivided meaning in the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element—therefore, because they have a single meaning, through the approach of the non-dual nature of <s>dharma</s>, that which is called 'Buddhahood' because of the awakening to all <s>dharmas</s> in all aspects, and that which is called '<s>nirvāṇa</s>' because of the abandonment of defilements together with residual impressions through great awakening—these two are to be seen as non-dual in the undefiled element, undivided and uncut.

children.translated_text: With qualities of all aspects, innumerable, inconceivable, and immaculate,

children.text: abhinnalakṣaṇo mokṣo yo mokṣaḥ sa tathāgata iti //
children.translated_text: liberation is of undifferentiated character; that which is liberation is the <s>Tathāgata</s>.

body.text: yaduktamarhatpratyekabuddhaparinirvāṇamadhikṛtya / nirvāṇamiti bhagavannupāya eṣa tathā gatānāmiti / anena dīrghādhvapariśrāntānāmaṭavīmadhye nagaranirmāṇavadavivartanopāya eṣa dharmaparameśvarāṇāṃ samyaksaṃbuddhānāmiti paridīpitam / nirvāṇādhigamād
body.translated_text: As stated with reference to the <s>parinirvāṇa</s> of <s>Arhats</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>: 'O Blessed One, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is a skillful means (<s>upāya</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>.' By this it is illuminated that this is a skillful means of non-regression [employed by] the sovereign lords of the <s>Dharma</s>, the perfectly awakened ones, like the creation of a phantom city for those wearied on a long journey through a wilderness. Through the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s>,

body.text:
bhagavaṃstathāgatā bhavantyarhantaḥ samyaksaṃbuddhāḥ sarvāprameyācintyaviśuddhiniṣṭhāgataguṇasamanvāgatā iti / anena caturākāraguṇaniṣpatsvasaṃbhinnalakṣaṇaṃ nirvāṇamadhigamya tadātmakāḥ samyaksaṃbuddhā bhavantīti / buddhatvanirvāṇayoravinirbhāgaguṇayogāduddhatvamantareṇa kasyacinnirvāṇādhigamo nāstīti paridīpitam /
tatra tathāgatānāmanāsrave dhātau sarvākāravaropetaśūnyatābhinirhārataścitrakaradṛṣṭāntena guṇasarvatā veditavyā /
body.translated_text: 'O Blessed One, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> become <s>Arhats</s>, Perfectly Awakened Ones, endowed with all immeasurable, inconceivable qualities that have reached the culmination of purity.' By this it is illuminated that, having attained <s>nirvāṇa</s> whose characteristic is inseparable from the accomplishment of qualities in four aspects, they become Perfectly Awakened Ones of that very nature — and that, because of the inseparable quality-nature of <s>Buddhahood</s> and <s>nirvāṇa</s>, there is no attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> for anyone apart from <s>Buddhahood</s>. There, the totality of qualities (<s>guṇasarvatā</s>) of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the undefiled element is to be understood through the painter illustration, by virtue of the production of <s>śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) endowed with all aspects of excellence.

children.translated_text: Just as there might be painters, each skilled in different [aspects],
each knowing whichever limb [he specializes in], which another could not master; ||88||
then a king, their sovereign, might give them a canvas with the command:
'All of you together must paint a portrait of me.' ||89||
Then, having agreed, they would set to work on the painting;
but one among those engaged [in the task] might go to another country. ||90||
With him gone to another country, the portrait, due to his absence,
would not be complete in all its limbs — thus the simile is made. ||91||
The painters of those forms are generosity (<s>dāna</s>), morality (<s>śīla</s>), patience (<s>kṣamā</s>), and so forth;
<s>Śūnyatā</s> (emptiness) endowed with all aspects of excellence is compared to the portrait. ||92||

body.text: tatraiṣāmeva dānādīnāmekaikasya buddhaviṣayāparyantaprakārabhedabhinnatvādaparimitatvaṃ veditavyam / saṃkhyāprabhāvābhyāmacintyatvam / mātsaryādivipakṣamalavāsanāpakarṣitatvādviśuddhiparamatvamiti / tatra sarvākāravaropetaśūnyatāsamādhimukhabhāvanayānutpattikadharmalābhādacalāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmāvavikalpāniśchidranirantarasvarasavāhimārgajñānasaṃniśrayeṇa
body.translated_text: There, the immeasurability of each one of these — generosity and the rest — is to be understood from the fact that each is differentiated by limitless varieties within the domain of the <s>Buddha</s>. Their inconceivability [is known] from their number and power. Their supreme purity [is known] from the removal of the stains and latent impressions of the opposing [forces] such as miserliness and the rest. There, through the cultivation of the <s>samādhi</s> gateway of <s>śūnyatā</s> endowed with all aspects of excellence, [one obtains] the attainment of the acceptance of the non-arising of <s>dharmas</s> (<s>anutpattikadharmakṣānti</s>). On the Immovable (<s>Acalā</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stage, relying upon the path-knowledge that is non-discriminating, unbroken, uninterrupted, and flows spontaneously,

body.text: tathāgatānāmanāsrave dhātau guṇasarvatā samudāgacchati / sādhumatyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmāvasaṃkhyeyasamādhidhāraṇīmukhasamudrairaparimāṇabuddhadharmaparigrahajñānasaniśrayeṇa guṇāprameyatā samudāgacchati / dharmameghāyāṃ bodhisattvabhūmau sarvatathāgatagṛhyasthānāviparokṣajñānasaṃniśrayeṇa guṇācintyatā samudāgacchati / tadanantaraṃ buddhabhūbhyadhigamāya sarvasavāsanakleśajñeyāvaraṇavimokṣajñānasaṃniśrayeṇa guṇaviśuddhiparamatā samudāgacchati / yat eṣu caturṣu bhūmijñānasaṃniśrayeṣvarhatpratyekabuddhā na saṃdṛśyante tasmātte dūrībhavanti caturākāraguṇapariniṣpattyasaṃbhinnalakṣaṇān nirvāṇadhātorityuktam /
body.translated_text: the totality of qualities of the <s>Tathāgatas</s> in the undefiled element arises. On the Good Intelligence (<s>Sādhumatī</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stage, relying upon the knowledge of comprehending immeasurable <s>Buddha</s>-qualities through the ocean of gateways of countless <s>samādhis</s> and <s>dhāraṇīs</s>, the immeasurability of qualities arises. On the Cloud of <s>Dharma</s> (<s>Dharmameghā</s>) <s>Bodhisattva</s>-stage, relying upon the knowledge that directly perceives all the secret domains of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, the inconceivability of qualities arises. Thereafter, for the attainment of the <s>Buddha</s>-stage, relying upon the knowledge of liberation from all obstructions of affliction and cognition together with their latent impressions, the supreme purity of qualities arises. Because <s>Arhats</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> are not seen in these four stage-knowledge-reliances, therefore they remain far from the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element whose characteristic is inseparable from the accomplishment of qualities in four aspects — so it is said.

children.translated_text: Through the radiance, diffusion, and purity of <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom), knowledge, and liberation,
and through their inseparability, the similarity to the light, rays, and disc of the sun [is established]. ||93||

body.text: yayā prajñayā yena jñānena yayā vimuktyā sa caturākāraguṇaniṣpattyasaṃbhinnalakṣaṇo nirvāṇadhātuḥ sūcyate tāsāṃ yathākramaṃ tribhirekena ca kāraṇena caturvidhamādityasādharmya paridīpitam / tatra buddhasāntānikyā lokottaranirvikalpāyāḥ paramajñeyatattvāndhakāravidhamanapratyupasthānatayā prajñāyā dīptisādharmyam / tatpṛṣṭhalabdhasya sarvajñajñānasya sarvākāraniravaśeṣajñeyavastupravṛttatayā raśmijālaspharaṇasādharmyam / tadubhayāśrayasya cittaprakṛtivimukteratyantavimalaprabhāsvaratayārkamaṇḍalaviśuddhisādharmyam / tisṛṇāmapi dharmadhātvasaṃbhedesvabhāvatayā tattrayāvinirbhāgasādharmyamiti /
body.translated_text: By which <s>prajñā</s>, by which knowledge, and by which liberation that <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element whose characteristic is inseparable from the accomplishment of qualities in four aspects is indicated — of those, respectively, the fourfold similarity to the sun is illuminated through three [points] and one [point]. There, the similarity of the <s>Buddha</s>'s supramundane, non-discriminating <s>prajñā</s> to radiance is because its characteristic is the dispelling of the darkness of ignorance regarding the supreme knowable reality. The similarity of the subsequently-obtained omniscient knowledge to the diffusion of a web of rays is because it extends to all knowable objects in every aspect without remainder. The similarity of the liberation of the natural state of the mind, which is the basis of both [prajñā and knowledge], to the purity of the sun's disc is because of its utterly stainless and luminous character. The similarity to the inseparability of those three is because of their nature being inseparable from the <s>dharmadhātu</s>.

body.text: ato 'nāgamya buddhatvaṃ nirvāṇaṃ nādhigamyate //
body.translated_text: Therefore, without attaining <s>Buddhahood</s>, <s>nirvāṇa</s> is not attained;

body.text: na hi śakyaḥ prabhāraśmī nirvṛjya prekṣituṃ raviḥ // 94 //
body.translated_text: for it is impossible to see the sun while separating [it from] its light and rays. ||94||

body.text: yata evamanādi sāṃnidhyasvabhāvaśubhadharmopahite dhātau tathāgatānāmavinirbhāgaguṇadharmatvamato na tathāgatatvamasaṅgāpratihataprajñājñānadarśanamanāgamya sarvāvaraṇavimuktilakṣaṇasya nirvāṇadhātoradhigamaḥ sākṣātkaraṇamupapadyate prabhāraśmyadarśina iva sūryamaṇḍaladarśanam / ata evamāha / na hi bhagavan hīnapraṇītadharmāṇāṃ nirvāṇādhigamaḥ / samadharmāṇāṃ bhagavan nirvāṇādhigamaḥ / samajñānānāṃ samavimuktīnāṃ samavimuktijñānadarśanānāṃ bhagavan nirvāṇādhigamaḥ / tasmādbhagavan nirvāṇadhāturekarasaḥ samarasa ityucyate / yaduta vidyāvimuktiraseneti /
body.translated_text: Since thus, in the element endowed with auspicious <s>dharmas</s> that are present from beginningless time by nature, the <s>Tathāgatas</s> have the nature of inseparable qualities — therefore, without attaining <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood, the unattached and unobstructed <s>prajñā</s>-knowledge-vision, the realization and direct experience of the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element characterized by liberation from all obstructions, is not possible — just as the seeing of the sun's disc is not possible for one who does not see its light and rays. Therefore he says thus: 'Indeed, O Blessed One, there is no attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> for those of inferior and superior <s>dharmas</s>. O Blessed One, the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> is for those of equal <s>dharmas</s>. O Blessed One, the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> is for those of equal knowledge, equal liberation, and equal liberation-knowledge-vision. Therefore, O Blessed One, the <s>nirvāṇa</s>-element is said to be of one flavor, of equal flavor — namely, the flavor of knowledge and liberation.'

children.translated_text: The establishment of the <s>Jinagarbha</s> (Buddha-embryo) — thus it has been stated in ten ways;
its being an embryo within the sheath of afflictions is further to be understood through illustrations. ||95||

body.text: ityetadaparāntakoṭisamadhruvadharmatāsaṃvidyamānatāmadhikṛtya daśavidhenārthena tathāgata garbhavyavasthānamuktam / punaranādisāṃnidhyāsaṃbaddha svabhāvakleśakośatāmanādisāṃnidhyasaṃbaddha svabhāvaśubhadharmatāṃ cādhikṛtya navabhirudāharaṇairaparyantakleśakośakoṭīgūḍhastathāgatagarbha iti yathāsūtramanugantavyam / navodāharaṇāni katamāni /
body.translated_text: Thus, with reference to the permanence and stable <s>dharmatā</s> coextensive with the final limit [of time], the establishment of the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> has been stated through ten kinds of meaning. Furthermore, with reference to its nature of being within the sheath of afflictions — connected from beginningless time — and its nature of auspicious <s>dharmas</s> — also connected from beginningless time — through nine illustrations, 'the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> hidden within the mass of the boundless sheath of afflictions' is to be followed as [stated] in the <s>sūtra</s>. What are the nine illustrations?

body.text: buddhaḥ kupadme madhu makṣikāsu tuṣesu sārāṇya śucau suvarṇam /
body.translated_text: A <s>Buddha</s> in a faded lotus, honey among bees, grain within husks, gold in filth,

body.text: nidhiḥ kṣitāvalpaphale 'ṅkurādi praklinnavastreṣu jinātmabhāvaḥ // 96 //
body.translated_text: a treasure beneath the earth, a sprout and such in a small fruit, a <s>Jina</s>'s form in tattered garments, ||96||

children.text: jaghanyanārījaṭhare nṛpatvaṃ yathā bhavenmṛtsu ca ratnabimbam /
children.translated_text: a universal monarch in the womb of a lowly woman, and a precious image in [a mold of] earth —

children.text: āgantukakleśamalāvṛteṣu sattveṣu tadvat sthita eṣa dhātuḥ // 97 //
children.translated_text: just so, this element abides in beings who are covered by the stain of adventitious afflictions. ||97||

body.text:
padmaprāṇituṣāśu cikṣitiphalatvakpūtivastrāvaras
trīduḥkhajvalanābhitaptapṛthivīdhātuprakāśā malāḥ / buddhakṣaudrasusārakāñcananidhinyagrodharatnākṛti-

children.translated_text: scorched by the three fires of suffering, and the earth-element. That supreme element is resplendent [and comparable to] a <s>Buddha</s>, honey, pure grain, gold, a treasure, a banyan tree, a jewel-image, the supreme lord of the continent, and a stainless jewel-image. ||98||

body.translated_text: The defilements are illuminated as [having the nature of] a lotus, bees, husks, filth, earth, a fruit-skin, a putrid garment, a woman

body.text: kutsitapadmakośasadṛśāḥ kleśāḥ / buddhavattathāgatadhāturiti /

children.translated_text: Just as a <s>Tathāgata</s>, radiant with a thousand marks, enveloped within the calyx of a discolored lotus,
would be seen by a person with stainless, divine vision, who would liberate him from the lotus-petal sheath; ||99||

body.translated_text: The afflictions are like a foul lotus-sheath; the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element is like the <s>Buddha</s> [within it].

body.text: vilokya tadvat sugataḥ svadharmatāmavīcisaṃstheṣvapi buddhacakṣuṣā / vimocayatyāvaraṇādanāvṛto 'parāntakoṭīsthitakaḥ kṛpātmakaḥ // 100 //
body.translated_text: just so, the <s>Sugata</s> (Well-Gone One), seeing with the <s>Buddha</s>-eye his own true nature even in those dwelling in <s>Avīci</s> (the lowest hell),

body.text: yadvat syādvijugupsitaṃ jalaruhaṃ saṃmiñji taṃ divyadṛk tadgarbhasthitamabhyudīkṣya sugataṃ patrāṇi saṃchedayet /
body.translated_text: being himself free from obstruction, compassionate in nature, abiding until the final limit [of time], liberates [beings] from their coverings. ||100||
Just as one with divine sight, seeing a <s>Sugata</s> dwelling within a loathsome, closed water-born [lotus], would cut its petals;

body.text: rāgadveṣamalādikośanivṛtaṃ saṃbuddhagarbhaṃ jagat
body.translated_text: so too, seeing that the world has the <s>Buddha</s>-embryo covered by the sheath of the stain of passion, hatred, and such,

body.text: kāruṇyādavalokya tannivaraṇaṃ nirhanti tadvanmuniḥ // 101 //
body.translated_text: the Sage, out of compassion, destroys that covering. ||101||

body.text: kṣudraprāṇākasadṛśāḥ kleśāḥ / kṣaudravattathāgatadhāturiti /
body.translated_text: The afflictions are like tiny creatures [bees]; the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element is like honey.

children.text: yathā madhu prāṇigaṇopagūḍhaṃ vilokya vidvān puruṣastadarthī /
children.translated_text: Just as a wise man, desiring honey, seeing it surrounded by a swarm of creatures [bees],
would skillfully bring about the removal of that swarm of creatures from all sides; ||102||
so too, the great Sage, seeing this element like honey, known to the omniscient eye,
brings about the ultimate non-attachment from those coverings that are like bees. ||103||
Just as honey, surrounded by millions and billions of creatures [bees] — a man
desiring honey, having destroyed those bees, would use the honey as he wishes;
so too, the undefiled knowledge, like honey, is in embodied beings,

children.text: kleśāḥ kṣudranibhā jinaḥ puruṣavat tadghātane kovidaḥ // 104 //
children.translated_text: the afflictions are like the tiny creatures, and the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror) is like the man, skilled in destroying them. ||104||

body.text: bahistuṣasadṛśāḥ kleśāḥ / antaḥsāravattathā gatadhāturiti /
body.translated_text: The afflictions are like outer husks; the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element is like the grain within.

children.text: dhānyeṣu sāraṃ tuṣasaṃprayuktaṃ nṛṇāṃ na ya[dva]tparibhogameti /
children.translated_text: Just as grain mixed with husks does not become fit for human consumption,
those who desire food and such free it from those husks; ||105||

body.text: sattveṣvapi kleśamalopasṛṣṭamevaṃ na tāvatkurute jinatvam /
body.translated_text: so too, [the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element] in beings, beset by the stain of afflictions, does not accomplish <s>Jina</s>-hood [for them],

body.text: saṃbuddhakāryaṃ tribhave na yāvadvimucyate kleśamalopasargāt // 106 //
body.translated_text: nor does it perform the activity of a fully awakened one in the three realms of existence so long as it is not freed from the affliction of the stain of defilements. ||106||

body.text:
yadvat kaṅgukaśālikodravayavavrīhiṣvamuktaṃ tuṣāt
sāraṃ khāḍyasusaṃskṛtaṃ na bhavati svādūpabhojyaṃ nṛṇām //
body.translated_text: Just as the grain of millet, rice, wild rice, or barley, not freed from the husk, is not fit for delicious, well-prepared, enjoyable food for humans;

body.text: tadvat kleśatuṣādaniḥsṛtavapuḥ sattveṣu dharmeśvaro

children.translated_text: does not bestow the flavor of the joy of <s>Dharma</s> upon people afflicted by the hunger of afflictions. ||107||

body.translated_text: so too, the Lord of <s>Dharma</s>, whose body has not emerged from the husk of afflictions, [dwelling] in beings,

body.text: aśucisaṃkāradhānasadṛśāḥ kleśāḥ / suvarṇavattathāgatadhāturiti /
body.translated_text: The afflictions are like an impure rubbish-heap; the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element is like gold [within it].

children.text: yathā suvarṇaṃ vrajato narasya cyutaṃ bhavetsaṃkarapūtidhāne /
children.translated_text: Just as gold belonging to a traveling man might fall into a foul rubbish-heap,
and it would remain there for many hundreds of years, being of imperishable nature; ||108||
a deity with pure, divine vision, seeing it there, would tell the man:
'Here is gold, the foremost excellent jewel — purify it and do what is to be done with the gem.' ||109||

body.text: dṛṣṭvā muniḥ sattvaguṇaṃ tathaiva kleśeṣvamekṣyapratimeṣu magnam /
body.translated_text: Just so, the Sage, seeing the quality [of Buddha-nature] in beings, sunk in afflictions that are immeasurable and beyond comparison,

body.text: tatkleśapaṅkavyavadānahetordharmāmbuvarṣaṃ vyasṛjat prajāsu // 110 //
body.translated_text: in order to purify [them from] the mire of those afflictions, rains down the waters of <s>Dharma</s> upon the world. ||110||

children.translated_text: Just as a deity, seeing gold fallen in a foul rubbish-heap,
would point it out to people — the most visible thing — for the purpose of purifying it from filth;
so too, the <s>Jina</s>, seeing the <s>Buddha</s>-jewel fallen in the great impurity of afflictions
in beings, teaches the <s>Dharma</s> for the purification of embodied beings. ||111||

body.text: pṛthivītalasadṛśāḥ kleśāḥ / ratnanidhāna vattathāgatadhāturiti /
body.translated_text: The afflictions are like the surface of the earth; the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element is like a treasure buried [beneath it].

children.text: yathā daridrasya narasya veśmanyantaḥ pṛthivyāṃ nidhirakṣayaḥ syāt /
children.translated_text: Just as beneath the house of a poor man, within the earth, there might be an inexhaustible treasure,

children.text: vidyānna cainaṃ sa naro na cāsminneṣo 'hamasmīti vadennidhistam // 112 //
children.translated_text: but the man would not know it, nor would the treasure say to him, 'I am here'; ||112||
so too, the inconceivable, inexhaustible jewel-treasury of stainless <s>Dharma</s>, though hidden within the mind,
not being realized, the world experiences manifold poverty and suffering ceaselessly. ||113||
Just as a treasure of gems, situated within the house of a poor man, would not say
'I am a treasure of gems' to the man — and so the man would not know;
so too, the treasure of <s>Dharma</s> is situated within the house of the mind, and beings are like the poor;
for the purpose of their attainment of that, the Sage arises in the world. ||114||

body.text: tvakkośasadṛśāḥ kleśāḥ / bījāṅkuravattathāgatadhāturiti /
body.translated_text: The afflictions are like a fruit-skin; the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element is like a seed-sprout [within it].

body.text: yathāmratālādiphale drumāṇāṃ bījāṅkuraḥ sannavināśadharmī /
body.translated_text: Just as the seed-sprout of trees such as mango or palm, being of imperishable nature,

body.text: uptaḥ pṛthivyāṃ salilādiyogāt kramādupaiti drumarājabhāvam // 115 //
body.translated_text: when planted in the earth, through the conjunction of water and such, gradually attains the state of the king of trees; ||115||

children.translated_text: the auspicious <s>dharma</s>-element in beings, enveloped within the inner sheath of the fruit of ignorance and such,
depending on this or that wholesome [condition], gradually attains the state of the King of Sages. ||116||
Just as through the conditions of water, sunlight, wind, earth, time, and space,
a tree emerges from the opening of the palm-fruit or mango sheath;
so too, the sprout of the seed of perfect awakening (<s>saṃbuddha</s>), situated within the fruit-skin of beings' afflictions,
grows into the tree of <s>Dharma</s> through those various wholesome conditions. ||117||

body.text: pūtivastrasadṛśaḥ kleśāḥ / ratnavigrahavattathāgatadhāturiti /
body.translated_text: The afflictions are like putrid garments; the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element is like a jewel-image [wrapped in them].

children.translated_text: Just as the jewel-image of the Conqueror (<s>Jina</s>), enclosed in foul-smelling, putrid cloth,
having seen it cast away on the road, a divinity would speak of it to a traveler for the sake of its liberation — ||118||
so too, seeing the self-nature of the <s>Sugata</s> (<s>sugatātmabhāva</s>), concealed by the various defilements' stains,

children.text: vilokya tiryakṣvapi advimuktiṃ pratyabhyupāyaṃ vidadhāti tadvat // 119 //
children.translated_text: even in animals, and [perceiving their potential for] liberation, he devises the appropriate means for that. ||119||

body.text:
yadvadratnamayaṃ tathāgatavapurdurgandhavastrāvṛtaṃ
vartmanyujjñitamekṣya divyanayano muktyai nṛṇāṃ darśayet /
body.translated_text: Just as, having seen the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s jewel-body wrapped in foul-smelling cloth and cast away on the road, one with divine vision would reveal it to people for the sake of its liberation,

body.text: tadvat kleśavipūtivastranivṛtaṃ saṃsāravartmojjhitaṃ
body.translated_text: so too, seeing the element (<s>dhātu</s>), wrapped in the putrid cloth of afflictions, cast away on the road of <s>saṃsāra</s>,

body.text: tiryakṣu vyavalokya dhātumavadaddharmaṃ vimuktyai jinaḥ // 120 //
body.translated_text: even in animals, the Conqueror taught the <s>Dharma</s> for the sake of liberation. ||120||

body.text: āpannasattvanārisadṛśāḥ kleśāḥ / kalalamahābhūtagatacakravartivattathāgatadhāturiti /
body.translated_text: The afflictions are like the distressed woman; the <s>Tathāgatadhātu</s> is like the embryonic universal monarch (<s>Cakravartin</s>) within the elements of the egg.

children.translated_text: Just as a certain woman, without protector, would dwell in a shelter for the destitute, of hideous form,

children.text: garbheṇa rājaśriyamudvahantī na sāvabudhyeta nṛpaṃ svakukṣau // 121 //
children.translated_text: yet bearing royal majesty in her womb — she would not know the king in her own belly. ||121||
Birth in existence is like a shelter for the destitute; impure beings are like the pregnant woman;

children.text: tadgarbhavatteṣvamalaḥ sa dhāturbhavanti yasminsati te sanāthāḥ // 122 //
children.translated_text: that stainless element (<s>dhātu</s>) within them is like her embryo; since when it exists, they are [truly] with a protector. ||122||
Just as a woman, her body covered in dirty garments, endowed with a repulsive appearance,
would find extreme suffering in a shelter for the destitute, while a king [dwells] within her womb —
so too, beings whose minds are unquiet due to the power of afflictions, dwelling in the abode of suffering,
though [truly] with protectors, think themselves without protector, even though [those protectors abide] within their own selves. ||123||

body.text: mṛtpaṅkalepasadṛśāḥ kleśāḥ / kanakabimbavattathāgatadhāturiti /
body.translated_text: The afflictions are like a coating of clay and mud; the <s>Tathāgatadhātu</s> is like a golden image.

body.text: hemno yathāntaḥkvathitasya pūrṇaṃ bimbaṃ bahirmṛnmayamekṣya śāntam /
body.translated_text: Just as one who knows, having seen a golden image — full and complete, cooled — covered externally with clay,

body.text: antarviśuddhyai kanakasya tajjñaḥ saṃcodayedāvaraṇaṃ bahirdhā // 124 //
body.translated_text: would remove the outer covering for the sake of purifying the gold within — ||124||

children.translated_text: so too, always beholding the luminosity of the [mind's] nature and the adventitious character of its stains,
the Supreme Awakening (<s>Agrabodhī</s>), [which is] like a mine of jewels, thus purifies the world from its coverings. ||125||
Just as a golden image — stainless, radiant, made of gold — lies within clay,
and one skilled in jewels, knowing it is at rest there, would remove the clay —
so too, knowing the mind to be at rest, resembling pure gold, the All-Knower,
by the method of striking with <s>Dharma</s>-proclamation, removes the covering. ||126||

body.text: udāharaṇānāṃ piṇḍārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: The summarized meaning of the examples:

children.translated_text: In lotus, bees, husks, filth, earth, and then
in fruit-skin, in putrid cloth, in a woman's womb, and in a clay mold — ||127||
like a <s>Buddha</s>, like honey, like an essence, like gold, like a treasure, like a tree,
like a jewel-image, like a universal monarch (<s>Cakravartin</s>), and like a golden image — ||128||
the natural stainlessness of the mind of the element of beings (<s>sattvadhātu</s>),
enclosed in the sheaths of beginningless afflictions, has been taught as beginningless. ||129||

body.text: samāsato 'nena tathāgatagarbhasūtrodāharaṇanirdeśena kṛtsnasya sattvadhātoranādicittasaṃkleśadharmāgantukatvamanādicittavyavadānadharmasahajāvinirbhāgatā ca
body.translated_text: In summary, by this exposition of examples in the <s>Tathāgatagarbha Sūtra</s>, the adventitious character of the beginningless <s>dharmas</s> of mental defilement (<s>cittasaṃkleśa</s>) in the entire element of beings, and the innate inseparability of the beginningless <s>dharmas</s> of mental purification (<s>cittavyavadāna</s>), have been

body.text: paridīpitā / tata ucyate / cittasaṃkleśāt sattvāḥ saṃkliṣyante cittavyavadānādviśudhyanta iti / tatra katamaścittasaṃkleśo yamadhikṛtya navadhā padmakośādidṛṣṭāntadeśanā /
body.translated_text: illuminated. Therefore it is said: 'Through the defilement of the mind, beings are defiled; through the purification of the mind, they are purified.' Now, what is that mental defilement with reference to which the ninefold teaching of the lotus-sheath and other examples [is given]?

children.translated_text: Passion (<s>rāga</s>), hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), delusion (<s>moha</s>), the intense manifestations of these, latent impressions (<s>vāsanā</s>),
stains belonging to the stages of purity [abandoned by] seeing, path-cultivation, and impure and pure grounds — ||130||
are illustrated ninefold by the examples of the lotus-sheath and so forth;
but in their divisions, the categories of the sheaths of boundless secondary defilements [are infinite]. ||131||

body.text: samāsata ime na va kleśāḥ prakṛtipariśuddhe 'pi tathāgatadhātau padmakośādaya iva buddhabimbādiṣu sadāgantukatayā saṃvidyante / katame nava / tadyathā rāgānuśayalakṣaṇaḥ kleśaḥ / dveṣānuśayalakṣaṇaḥ / mohānuśayalakṣaṇaḥ / tīvrarāgadveṣamohaparyavasthānalakṣaṇaḥ / avidyāvāsabhūmisaṃgṛhītaḥ / darśanaprahātavyaḥ / bhāvanāprahātavyaḥ / aśuddhabhūmigataḥ / śuddhabhūmigataśca / tatra ye laukikavītarāgasāntānikāḥ kleśā āniñjyasaṃskāropacayahetavo rūpārūpyadhātunirvartakā lokottarajñānavadhyāsta ucyante rāgadveṣamohānuśayalakṣaṇā iti / ye rāgādicaritasattvasāntānikāḥ puṇyāpuṇyasaṃskāropacayahetavaḥ kevalakāmadhātunirvartakā aśubhādibhāvajñānavadhyāsta ucyante tīvrarāgadveṣamohaparyavasthānalakṣaṇā iti / ye 'rhatsāntānikā anāsravakarmapravṛttihetavo vimalamanomayātmabhāvanirvartakāstathāgatabodhijñānavadhyāsta ucyante 'vidyāvāsabhūmisaṃgṛhītā iti / dvividhaḥ śaikṣaḥ pṛthagjana āryaśca / tatra ye pṛthagjanaśaikṣasāṃtānikāḥ prathamalokottaradharmadarśanajñānavadhyāsta ucyante darśanaprahātavyā
body.translated_text: In summary, these nine afflictions exist as always adventitious in the <s>Tathāgatadhātu</s>, even though it is naturally pure — like the lotus-sheath and so forth around the <s>Buddha</s>-image and so forth. Which nine? They are: (1) the affliction characterized by the latent tendency of passion (<s>rāgānuśaya</s>); (2) that characterized by the latent tendency of hatred; (3) that characterized by the latent tendency of delusion; (4) that characterized by the intense manifestation of passion, hatred, and delusion; (5) that included in the ground of latent impressions of ignorance (<s>avidyāvāsabhūmi</s>); (6) that to be abandoned by seeing (<s>darśanaprahātavya</s>); (7) that to be abandoned by cultivation (<s>bhāvanāprahātavya</s>); (8) that belonging to the impure grounds; and (9) that belonging to the pure grounds. Among these, the afflictions in the continua of those who have attained mundane dispassion (<s>laukikavītarāga</s>), which are the causes for the accumulation of imperturbable formations (<s>āniñjyasaṃskāra</s>) and produce [birth in] the form and formless realms, and which are to be destroyed by supramundane knowledge — these are called 'characterized by the latent tendencies of passion, hatred, and delusion.' Those in the continua of beings with conduct dominated by passion and so forth, which are the causes for the accumulation of meritorious and demeritorious formations and produce [birth] solely in the desire realm, and which are to be destroyed by knowledge [gained through practices] such as contemplation of the impure (<s>aśubhā</s>) — these are called 'characterized by the intense manifestations of passion, hatred, and delusion.' Those in the continua of <s>Arhats</s>, which are the causes for the operation of undefiled <s>karma</s> and produce a stainless mind-made body (<s>manomayātmabhāva</s>), and which are to be destroyed by the knowledge of <s>Tathāgata</s>-awakening — these are called 'included in the ground of latent impressions of ignorance.' There are two kinds of learners (<s>śaikṣa</s>): ordinary persons (<s>pṛthagjana</s>) and noble ones (<s>ārya</s>). Among these, those in the continua of ordinary-person learners, which are to be destroyed by the first supramundane <s>dharma</s>-seeing-knowledge — these are called 'to be abandoned by seeing'

body.text: iti / ya āryapudgalaśaikṣasāntānikā yathādṛṣṭalokottaradharmabhāvanājñānavadhyāsta ucyante bhāvanāprahātavyā iti / ye 'niṣṭhāgatabodhisattvasāntānikāḥ saptavidhajñānabhūmivipakṣā aṣṭāmyādibhūmitrayabhāvanājñānavadhyāsta ucyante 'śuddhabhūmigatā iti / ye niṣṭhāgatabodhisattvasāntānikā aṣṭamyādibhūmitrayabhāvanājñānavipakṣā vajropamasamādhijñānavadhyāsta ucyante śuddhabhūmigatā iti / ete
body.translated_text: . Those in the continua of noble-person learners, which are to be destroyed by the supramundane <s>dharma</s>-cultivation-knowledge of what has been seen — these are called 'to be abandoned by cultivation.' Those in the continua of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have not reached culmination, which are the opponents of the seven knowledge-grounds and are to be destroyed by the cultivation-knowledge of the three grounds beginning with the eighth — these are called 'belonging to the impure grounds.' Those in the continua of <s>Bodhisattvas</s> who have reached culmination, which are the opponents of the cultivation-knowledge of the three grounds beginning with the eighth and are to be destroyed by the knowledge of the <s>vajropama samādhi</s> (diamond-like concentration) — these are called 'belonging to the pure grounds.' These

children.translated_text: nine defilements beginning with passion (<s>rāga</s>) are, in brief, in corresponding order,
illustrated by the nine examples of the lotus-sheath and so forth. ||132||

body.text: vistareṇa punareta eva caturaśītisahasraprakārabhedena tathāgatajñānavadaparyantā bhavanti yairaparyantakleśakośakoṭigūḍhastathāgatagarbha ucyate /
body.translated_text: In detail, however, these same [defilements], in their eighty-four thousand varieties, are boundless — like the knowledge of the <s>Tathāgata</s> — and it is said that the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> is concealed by the boundless categories of defilement-sheaths.

children.translated_text: For ordinary persons, <s>Arhats</s>, learners, and the wise [<s>Bodhisattvas</s>], in order,
impurity [arises] from four, from one, from two, and from two defilements [respectively]. ||133||

body.text: yaduktaṃ bhagavatā / sarvasattvāstathāgatagarbha iti / tatra sarvasattvāḥ saṃkṣepeṇocyante caturvidhāstadyathā pṛthagjanā arhantaḥ śaikṣā bodhisattvāśceti / tatraiṣāmanāsrave dhātau yathākramaṃ caturbhirekena dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ ca kleśamalābhyāmaśuddhiḥ paridīpitā /
body.translated_text: As the Blessed One has said: 'All beings have the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s>.' There, all beings are said to be of four kinds in brief: namely, ordinary persons, <s>Arhats</s>, learners, and <s>Bodhisattvas</s>. For these, impurity in the undefiled element has been illuminated through four, one, two, and two affliction-stains respectively, in corresponding order.

body.text: kathaṃ punarime nava rāgādayaḥ kleśāḥ padmakośādisadṛśā veditavyāḥ / kathaṃ ca tathāgatadhātorbuddhabimbādisādharmyamanugantavyamiti /
body.translated_text: Now, how should these nine defilements beginning with passion be understood as similar to the lotus-sheath and so forth? And how should the similarity of the <s>Tathāgatadhātu</s> to the <s>Buddha</s>-image and so forth be followed?

children.text: tatpadmaṃ mṛdi saṃbhūtaṃ purā bhūtvā manoramam /
children.translated_text: The lotus, born in mud, is at first delightful,
but later becomes unlovely — so too is the pleasure of passion (<s>rāga</s>). ||134||
Just as bees, when angered, sting fiercely,
so too hatred (<s>dveṣa</s>), when it arises in the heart, generates suffering. ||135||

body.text: śālyādīnāṃ yathā sāramavacchannaṃ bahistuṣaiḥ /
body.translated_text: Just as the essence of rice and such is covered externally by husks,

body.text: mohāṇḍakośasaṃchannamevaṃ sārārthadarśanam // 136 //
body.translated_text: so too the seeing of the essential meaning is enclosed in the egg-sheath of delusion (<s>moha</s>). ||136||

children.translated_text: Just as filth is repugnant, so too are sense-pleasures (<s>kāma</s>) to those free from passion;
because [sense-pleasures] are the cause of indulgence in desire, the intense manifestations [of affliction] are like filth. ||137||
Just as those who do not know would not find a treasure hidden beneath the earth,
so too beings, covered by the ground of latent impressions of ignorance (<s>avidyāvāsabhūmi</s>), [do not find] their self-born nature (<s>svayaṃbhūtva</s>). ||138||
Just as by the splitting of the seed-husk, the gradual arising of sprouts and so forth [occurs],
so too the elimination of that to be abandoned by seeing [occurs] through the seeing of reality (<s>tattvadarśana</s>). ||139||
For those whose core of identity-view (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>) has been destroyed, through engagement with the Noble Path,
[the afflictions] to be abandoned by cultivation-knowledge are illustrated by the putrid cloth. ||140||
The stains belonging to the seven [impure] grounds are like the defilement of the womb-sheath;
like the embryo freed from the sheath, non-conceptual knowledge, in its maturation, [is liberated]. ||141||
The stains following the three [pure] grounds should be known as like a coating of clay;
they are to be destroyed by the knowledge of the <s>vajropama samādhi</s> (diamond-like concentration) of the great beings. ||142||
Thus the nine stains beginning with passion are similar to the lotus and so forth;
the similarity of the element (<s>dhātu</s>) to the <s>Buddha</s>[-image] and so forth is through the inclusion of the threefold nature. ||143||

body.text: trividhaṃ svabhāvamadhikṛtya cittavyavadānahetostathāgatagarbhasya navadhā buddhābimbādisādharmyamanugantavyam / trividhaḥ svabhāvaḥ katamaḥ /

children.translated_text: Its nature (<s>svabhāva</s>) is the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, suchness (<s>tathatā</s>), and the lineage (<s>gotra</s>);
it should be known through three, one, and five illustrations [respectively]. ||144||

body.translated_text: With reference to the threefold nature, the ninefold similarity of the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> — the cause of mental purification — to the <s>Buddha</s>-image, honey, essence, and so forth should be followed. What is the threefold nature?

body.text: tribhirbuddhabimbamadhusāradṛṣṭāntairdharmakāyasvabhāvaḥ sa dhāturavagantavyaḥ / ekena suvarṇadṛṣṭāntena tathatāsvabhāvaḥ / pañcabhirnidhitarutnavigrahacakravartikanakabimbadṛṣṭāntaistrividhabuddhakāyotpattigotrasvabhāva
body.translated_text: Through the three illustrations of the <s>Buddha</s>-image, honey, and essence, that element should be understood as having the nature of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. Through the one illustration of gold, as having the nature of suchness (<s>tathatā</s>). Through the five illustrations of treasure, tree, jewel-image, universal monarch (<s>Cakravartin</s>), and golden image, as having the nature of the lineage (<s>gotra</s>) for the arising of the threefold <s>Buddha</s>-body

body.text: iti / tatra dharma kāyaḥ katamaḥ /
body.translated_text: . Now, what is the <s>Dharmakāya</s>?

children.translated_text: The <s>Dharmakāya</s> should be known as twofold: the utterly stainless <s>Dharmadhātu</s>,
and the teaching that is the outflow of that — [teaching] of profound and diverse methods. ||145||

body.text: dvividho buddhānāṃ dharmakāyo 'nugantavyaḥ / suviśuddhśca dharmadhātoravikalpajñānagocaraviṣayaḥ / sa ca tathāgatānāṃ pratyātmamadhigamadharmamadhikṛtya veditavyaḥ / tatprāptihetuśca suviśuddhadharmadhātuniṣyando yathāvainayikaparasattveṣu vijñaptiprabhavaḥ / sa ca deśanādharmamadhikṛtya veditavyaḥ / deśanā punardvividhā sūkṣmaudārikadharmavyavasthānanayabhedāt / yaduta gambhīrabodhisattvapiṭakadharmavyavasthāna nayadeśanā ca paramārthasatyamadhikṛtya vicitrasūtrageyavyākaraṇagāthodānanidānādivividhadharmavyavasthānanayadeśanā ca saṃvṛtisatyamadhikṛtya /
body.translated_text: The <s>Dharmakāya</s> of the <s>Buddhas</s> should be understood as twofold: the thoroughly purified <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, which is the domain of non-conceptual knowledge (<s>avikalpajñāna</s>) — this should be understood with reference to the <s>Tathāgatas</s>' personally realized <s>Dharma</s> (<s>pratyātmādhigamadharma</s>); and its cause of attainment, the outflow of the thoroughly purified <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, which arises as communication directed toward other beings according to their [capacity for] training — this should be understood with reference to the <s>Dharma</s> of teaching. Teaching, moreover, is twofold, differentiated by the method of establishing subtle and coarse <s>dharmas</s>: namely, the teaching of the method of establishing the profound <s>Bodhisattva Piṭaka dharmas</s> with reference to ultimate truth (<s>paramārthasatya</s>), and the teaching of the method of establishing the various <s>dharmas</s> such as <s>sūtras</s>, <s>geyas</s>, <s>vyākaraṇas</s>, <s>gāthās</s>, <s>udānas</s>, <s>nidānas</s>, and so forth, with reference to conventional truth (<s>saṃvṛtisatya</s>).

children.translated_text: Because it is supramundane and because no worldly simile for it is found,
the similarity of the element (<s>dhātu</s>) has been established by the <s>Tathāgata</s> himself. ||146||
The teaching of the subtle and profound method is like honey of a single taste;
the teaching of the diverse method should be known as like the essence within various husks. ||147||

body.text: ityevamebhistribhirbuddhabimbamadhusāradṛṣṭāntaistathāgatadharmakāyena niravaśeṣasattvadhātuparispharaṇārthamadhikṛtya tathāgatasyeme garbhāḥ sarvasattvā itiparidīpitam / na hi sa kaścitsattvaḥ sattvadhātau saīvidyate yastathāgatadharmakāyādvahirākāśadhātoriva rūpam / evaṃ hyāha /
body.translated_text: Thus, by these three illustrations of the <s>Buddha</s>-image, honey, and essence, with reference to the purpose of the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s> pervading the entire element of beings without remainder, it has been illuminated that 'all beings are the embryos of the <s>Tathāgata</s>' (<s>tathāgatasyeme garbhāḥ sarvasattvāḥ</s>). For there is no being in the element of beings that exists outside the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s>, just as no form [exists] outside the space-element (<s>ākāśadhātu</s>). For thus it is said:

body.text:
yathāmbaraṃ sarvagataṃ sada mataṃ tathaiva tatsarvagataṃ sadā matam /
yathāmbaraṃ rūpagateṣu sarvagaṃ tathaiva tatsattvagaṇeṣu sarvagamiti //
body.translated_text: 'Just as space is thought to be all-pervading at all times, so too that [element] is thought to be all-pervading at all times. Just as space is all-pervading in all form-realms, so too that [element] is all-pervading in all assemblies of beings.'

children.translated_text: Because of the unchangeability of its nature, because of its being beneficent, and because of its purity,
the simile of a disc of gold has been given for suchness (<s>tathatā</s>). ||148||

body.text: yaccittamaparyantakleśaduḥkhadharmānugatamapi prakṛtiprabhāsvaratayā vikārānudāhṛterataḥ kalyāṇasuvarṇavadananyathābhāvārthena tathatetyucyate / sa ca sarveṣāmapi mithyātvaniyatasaṃtānānāṃ sattvānāṃ prakṛtinirviśiṣṭānāṃ sarvāgantukamalaviśuddhimāgatastathāgata iti saṃkhyāṃ gacchati / evamekena suvarṇadṛṣṭāntena tathatāvyatibhedārthamadhikṛtya tathāgatastathataiṣāṃ garbhaḥ sarvasattvānāmiti paridīpitam / cittaprakṛtiviśuddhyadvayadharmatāmupādāya yathoktaṃ bhagavatā / tatramañjuśrīstathāgata ātmopādānamūlaparijñātāvī / ātmaṃviśuddhyā sarvasattvaviśuddhimanugataḥ / yā cātmaviśuddhiryā ca sattvaviśuddhiradvayaiṣādvaidhikāro ti / evaṃ hyāha /
body.translated_text: That mind which, though attended by limitless affliction-suffering-phenomena, is by nature luminous (<s>prakṛtiprabhāsvara</s>) and unillustrable by alteration—that, in the sense of being unalterable, like pure gold, is called <s>tathatā</s> (suchness). And that very [suchness], in all beings without exception—even in those of fixed wrong [views] in their mind-streams—being naturally undifferentiated and having arrived at purification from all adventitious defilements, is reckoned as <s>Tathāgata</s>. Thus, through the single simile of gold, with reference to the meaning of the undifferentiatedness of <s>tathatā</s>, it has been illustrated that 'the <s>Tathāgata</s>, that <s>tathatā</s>, is the <s>garbha</s> (embryo) of all these beings.' Taking up the non-duality of the natural purity of mind, as stated by the <s>Bhagavān</s>: 'There, <s>Mañjuśrī</s>, the <s>Tathāgata</s> has fully understood the root of self-grasping. Through self-purification he has followed the purification of all beings. And self-purification and the purification of beings are non-dual; this is not a division.' For thus he says:

children.translated_text: The <s>tathatā</s>, though undifferentiated in all, having arrived at purity,
is <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood; therefore all embodied beings have it as their <s>garbha</s> (embryo).
That <s>gotra</s> (lineage) is to be known as twofold, like a treasure and a fruit-tree:
the one abiding naturally since beginningless [time], and the superior one that has been cultivated. // 149 //

body.text: buddhakāyatrayāvāptirasmādgotradvayānmatā /
body.translated_text: The attainment of the three <s>Buddha</s>-bodies is regarded as [arising] from this twofold <s>gotra</s>:

body.text: prathamātprathamaḥ kāyo dvitī yāddvau tu paścimau // 150 //
body.translated_text: from the first, the first body; from the second, the two latter ones. // 150 //

children.translated_text: The <s>svābhāvikakāya</s> (natural body) is to be understood as like a jewel-embodiment, auspicious,
because [the nature] is uncreated and because it is the basis of quality-gems. // 151 //
The <s>sāmbhogikakāya</s> (enjoyment body) is like a <s>cakravartin</s> (universal monarch), because of being lord of the great <s>Dharma</s>;
the <s>nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation body) is like a golden image, because it is of the nature of a reflection. // 152 //

body.text: ityevamebhiravaśiṣṭaiḥ pañcabhirnidhitaruratnavigrahacakravartikanakabimbadṛṣṭāntaistri vidhabuddhakāyotpattigotrasvabhāvārthamadhikṛtya tathāgatadhātureṣāṃ garbhaḥ sarvasattvānāmiti paridīpitam / trividhabuddhakāyaprabhāvitatvaṃ hi tathāgatatvam / atastatprāptaye hetustathāgatadhāturiti / hetvartho 'tra dhātvarthaḥ / yata āha / tatra ca sattve sattve tathāgatadhāturutpanno garbhagataḥ saṃvidyate na ca te sattvā budhyante iti / evaṃ hyāha /

children.translated_text: The element (<s>dhātu</s>) is beginningless in time, the common basis of all <s>dharmas</s>;

children.text: tasmin sati gatiḥ sarvā nirvāṇādhigamo 'pi ca //
children.translated_text: because it exists, all destinies [of rebirth] and the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s> [are possible].

body.translated_text: Thus, with these remaining five similes—the treasure, the tree, the jewel-embodiment, the <s>cakravartin</s>, and the golden image—with reference to the meaning of the nature of the <s>gotra</s> giving rise to the three <s>Buddha</s>-bodies, it has been illustrated that 'the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element is the <s>garbha</s> of all these beings.' For <s>Tathāgata</s>-hood is precisely the manifestation of the three <s>Buddha</s>-bodies. Therefore, the cause for attaining that is the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element. Here, the meaning of 'element' (<s>dhātu</s>) is the meaning of 'cause' (<s>hetu</s>). As he said: 'In each and every being, the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element has arisen, has entered as an embryo (<s>garbha</s>), and is present; but those beings do not understand.' For thus he says:

body.text: tatra kathamanādikālikaḥ / yattathāgatagarbhamevādhikṛtya bhagavatā pūrva koṭirna prajñāyata iti deśitaṃ prajñaptam / dhāturiti / yadāha / yo 'yaṃ bhagavaṃstathāgatagarbho
body.translated_text: There, how is it beginningless in time? Because the <s>Bhagavān</s> has taught and designated, with reference to the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> itself, that 'its prior limit is not discerned.' 'Element' (<s>dhātu</s>)—because he said: 'This <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>, O <s>Bhagavan</s>,

body.text: lokottaragarbhaḥ prakṛtipariśuddhagarbha iti / sarvadharmasamāśraya iti / yadāha / tasmādbhagavaṃstathāgatagarbho niśraya ādhāraḥ pratiṣṭhāsaṃbaddhānāmavinirbhāgānāmamuktajñānānāmasaṃskṛtānāṃ dharmāṇām / asaṃbaddhānāmapi bhagavan vinirbhāgadharmāṇāṃ muktajñānānāṃ saṃskṛtānāṃ dharmāṇāṃ niśraya ādhāraḥ pratiṣṭhā tathāgatagarbha iti / tasmin sati gatiḥ sarveti / yadāha / sati bhagavaṃstathāgarbhe saṃsāra iti parikalpamasya vacanāyeti / nirvāṇādhigamo 'pi ceti / yadāha / tathāgatagarbhaśced bhagavanna syānna syādduḥkhe 'pi nirvinna nirvāṇecchā prārthanā praṇidhirveti vistaraḥ /
body.translated_text: is a supramundane <s>garbha</s>, a naturally pure <s>garbha</s>.' 'The common basis of all <s>dharmas</s>'—because he said: 'Therefore, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> is the support, the foundation, the ground of <s>dharmas</s> that are connected, inseparable, unfreed knowledge, unconditioned. And of <s>dharmas</s> that are unconnected, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, having the character of separability, freed knowledge, conditioned—of those too, the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> is the support, foundation, and ground.' 'Because it exists, all destinies [of rebirth]'—because he said: 'When, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> exists, that is the designation "<s>saṃsāra</s>."' 'And the attainment of <s>nirvāṇa</s>'—because he said: 'If, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> did not exist, there would be no revulsion toward suffering, no desire, aspiration, or resolve for <s>nirvāṇa</s>,' and so on in detail.

body.text: sa khalveṣa tathāgatagarbho dharmakāyāṃvipralambhastathatāsaṃbhinnalakṣaṇo niyatagotrasvabhāvaḥ sarvadā ca sarvatra ca niravaśeṣayogena sattvadhātāviti draṣṭavyaṃ dharmatāṃ pramāṇīkṛtya / yathoktam / eṣā kulaputra dharmāṇāṃ dharmatā / utpādādvā tathāgatānāmanutpādādvā sadaivaite sattvāstathāgatagarbhā iti / yaiva cāsau dharmatā saivātra yuktiryoga upāyaḥ paryāyaḥ / evameva tatsyāt / anyathā naiva tatsyāditi / sarvatra dharmataiva pratiśaraṇam / dharmataiva yuktiścittanidhyāpanāya cittasaṃjñāpanāya / sā na cintayitavyā na vikalpayitavyādhimoktavyeti /
