body.translated_text: This <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>—not deceptive as to the <s>dharmakāya</s>, having the characteristic of being undivided from <s>tathatā</s>, having the nature of the determined <s>gotra</s>, always and everywhere without remainder in the realm of beings—is to be regarded as established by taking <s>dharmatā</s> (the nature of reality) as authoritative. As stated: 'This, O son of good family, is the <s>dharmatā</s> of <s>dharmas</s>. Whether <s>Tathāgatas</s> arise or do not arise, these beings are always <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>.' And that very <s>dharmatā</s> is here the reasoning, the method, the means, the approach: 'It would be exactly so; otherwise it would not be so.' Everywhere, <s>dharmatā</s> alone is the refuge; <s>dharmatā</s> alone is the reasoning for convincing and instructing the mind. It is not to be thought about, not to be conceptualized, [but] to be accepted on faith.

body.text: śraddhayaivānugantavyaṃ paramārthe svayaṃbhuvām /
body.translated_text: It is to be followed through faith alone, the ultimate truth of the self-born ones;

body.text: na hyacakṣuḥ prabhādīptamīkṣate sūryamaṇḍalam // 153 //
body.translated_text: for one without eyes cannot behold the radiant disc of the sun. // 153 //

body.text: samāsata ime catvāraḥ pudgalāstathāgatagarbhadarśanaṃ pratyacakṣuṣmanto vyavasthitāḥ / katame catvāraḥ / yaduta pṛthagjanaḥ śrāvakaḥ pratyekabuddho navayānasaṃprasthitaśca bodhisattvaḥ / yathoktam / agocaro 'yaṃ bhagavaṃstathāgatagarbhaḥ satkāyadṛṣṭipatitānāṃ viparyāsābhiratānāṃ śūnyatāvikṣiptacittānāmiti / tatra satkāyadṛṣṭipatitā ucyante bālapṛthagjanāḥ / tathā hi te 'tyantasāsravaskandhādīndharmānātmata ātmīyataścopagamyāhakāramamakārābhiniviṣṭāḥ satkāyanirodhamanāsravadhātumadhimoktumapi nālam / kutaḥ punaḥ sarvajñaviṣayaṃ tathāgatagarbhamavabhotsyanta iti / nedaṃ sthānaṃ vidyate / tatra viparyāsābhiratā ucyante śrāvakapratyekabuddhāḥ / tatkasmāt / te 'pi hi nitye tathāgatagarbhe satyuttaribhāvayitavye tannityasaṃjñābhāvanāviparyayeṇānityasaṃjñābhāvanābhiratāḥ / sukhe tathāgatagarbhe satyuttaribhāvayitavye tatsukhasaṃjñābhāvanāviparyayeṇa duḥkhasaṃjñābhāvanābhiratāḥ / ātmani tathāgatagarbhe satyuttaribhāvayitavye tadātmasaṃjñābhāvanāviparyayeṇānātmasaṃjñābhāvanābhiratāḥ / śubhe tathāgatagarbheḥ satyuttaribhāvayitavye tacchubhasaṃjñābhāvanāviparyayeṇāśubhasaṃjñābhāvanā bhiratāḥ / evamanena paryāyeṇa sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhānāmapi dharmakāyaprāptividhuramārgābhiratatvādagocaraḥ sa paramanityasukhātmaśubhalakṣaṇo dhāturityuktam / yathā ca sa vipayāsābhiratānāmanityaduḥkhānātmāśubhasaṃjñānāmagocarastathā vistareṇa mahāparinirvāṇasūtre bhagavatā vāpītoyamaṇidṛṣṭāntena prasādhitaḥ /
body.translated_text: In brief, these four types of persons are established as eyeless with regard to the seeing of the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>. Which four? Namely, the ordinary person (<s>pṛthagjana</s>), the <s>Śrāvaka</s>, the <s>Pratyekabuddha</s>, and the <s>Bodhisattva</s> newly set out on the vehicle. As stated: 'This <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is beyond the domain of those fallen into the view of a self in the aggregates (<s>satkāyadṛṣṭi</s>), of those delighting in the inversions (<s>viparyāsa</s>), and of those whose minds are distracted by emptiness (<s>śūnyatā</s>).' There, those 'fallen into the view of a self in the aggregates' are said to be the childish ordinary persons. For they, having apprehended the thoroughly defiled aggregates and such as self and as belonging to self, are engrossed in the notions of 'I' and 'mine,' and are not even capable of having faith in the cessation of the aggregates, the undefiled element. How much less would they comprehend the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>, which is the domain of the omniscient? This is not possible. There, those 'delighting in the inversions' are said to be the <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>. Why? Because they too, though the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> is permanent and should be further cultivated, delight in cultivating the perception of impermanence through the inversion of not cultivating the perception of permanence; though the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> is blissful and should be further cultivated, delight in cultivating the perception of suffering through the inversion of not cultivating the perception of bliss; though the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> is self and should be further cultivated, delight in cultivating the perception of non-self through the inversion of not cultivating the perception of self; though the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> is pure and should be further cultivated, delight in cultivating the perception of impurity through the inversion of not cultivating the perception of purity. Thus, by this approach, because all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s> delight in a path that is far from attaining the <s>dharmakāya</s>, that element, characterized as supremely permanent, blissful, self, and pure, is said to be beyond their domain. And just as it is beyond the domain of those delighting in the inversions who perceive impermanence, suffering, non-self, and impurity, so it has been established in detail by the <s>Bhagavān</s> in the <s>Mahāparinirvāṇasūtra</s> with the simile of the well-water jewel.

body.text: tadyathāpi nāma bhikṣavo grīṣmakāle vartamāne salilabandhanaṃ baddhvā svaiḥ svairmaṇḍanakoparbhogairjanāḥ salile krīḍeyuḥ / atha tatraiko jātyaṃ vaiḍūryamaṇimantarudake
body.translated_text: 'Just as, O monks, in the summer season, people, having dammed the waters, play in the water with their various ornaments and enjoyments. Then one of them places a genuine <s>vaiḍūrya</s> gem in the water.

body.text: sthāpayet / tatastasya vaiḍūryasyārthe sarve te maṇḍanakāni tyaktvā nimajjeyuḥ / atha yattatrāsti śarkaraṃ kaṭhalyaṃ vā tatte maṇiriti manyamānā gṛhītvā mayā labdho maṇirityutsṛjyotsṛjya vāpītire sthitvā nāyaṃ maṇiriti saṃjñāṃ pravarteyuḥ / tacca vāpyudakaṃ maṇiprabhāvena tatprabheva bhrājeta / evaṃ teṣāṃ tadudakaṃ bhrājamānaṃ dṛṣṭvāho maṇiriti guṇasaṃjñā pravarteta / atha tatraika upāyakuśalo medhāvī maṇiṃ tattvataḥ pratilabheta / evameva bhikṣavo yuṣmābhiḥ sarvamanityaṃ sarva duḥkhaṃ sarvamanātmakaṃ sarvamaśubha miti sarvagrahaṇena bhāvitabhāvitaṃ bahulīkṛtabahulīkṛtaṃ dharmatattvama jānadbhistatsarva ghaṭitaṃ nirarthakam / tasmād bhikṣavo vāpīśarkarakaṭhalyavyavasthitā iva mā bhūtā upāyakuśalā yūyaṃ bhavata / yadyad bhikṣavo yuṣmābhiḥ sarvamanityaṃ sarva duḥkhaṃ sarvamanātmakaṃ sarvamaśubhamiti sarvagrahaṇena bhāvitabhāvitaṃ bahulīkṛtabahulīkṛtaṃ tatra tatraiva nityasukhaśabhātmakāni santīti vistareṇa paramadharmatattvavyavasthānamārabhya viparyāsabhūtanirdeśo yathāsūtramanugantavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Then, for the sake of that <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, all of them, having thrown aside their ornaments, would dive in. Whatever pebbles or grit are there—grasping those and thinking "I have obtained the gem"—they would cast them aside again and again, standing at the bank of the pool, and the notion would arise: "This is not the gem." Yet the pool water would shine with the radiance of the gem, as if with its own radiance. Seeing that water shining thus, the notion of [its] qualities would arise in them: "Ah, the gem!" Then one among them, skillful in means, intelligent, would obtain the gem as it truly is. Even so, O monks, you have cultivated and repeatedly cultivated with the universal apprehension that "all is impermanent, all is suffering, all is without self, all is impure," without knowing the true nature of <s>dharmas</s>—all that has been contrived and is without purpose. Therefore, O monks, do not be like those stuck at the pebbles and grit of the pool; be skillful in means. Whatever, O monks, you have cultivated and repeatedly cultivated with the universal apprehension that "all is impermanent, all is suffering, all is without self, all is impure"—in all of that, the permanent, blissful, pure, and self-natured exist'—and so on in detail; the exposition of the inversion-removal through the establishment of the supreme truth of <s>dharma</s> is to be followed as in the <s>sūtra</s>.

body.text: tatra śūnyatāvikṣiptacittā ucyante navayāna saṃprasthitā bodhisattvastathāgatagarbhaśūnyatārthanayavipranaṣṭāḥ / ye bhāvavināśāya śūnyatāvimokṣamukhamicchanti sata eva dharmasyottarakālamucchedo vināśaḥ parinirvāṇamiti / ye vā punaḥ śūnyatopalambhena śūnyatāṃ pratisaranti śūnyatā nāma rūpādivyatirekeṇa kaścidbhā vo 'sti yamadhigamiṣyāmo bhāvayiṣyāma iti / tatra katamaḥ sa tathāgatagarbhaśūnyatārthanaya ucyate /
body.translated_text: There, those 'whose minds are distracted by emptiness' are said to be the <s>Bodhisattvas</s> newly set out on the vehicle who are lost in the approach to the meaning of the emptiness of the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>. [These are:] those who, desiring the gate of the emptiness-liberation for the destruction of [all] existence, [think:] 'There will be the cutting off, destruction, and complete cessation of an existing <s>dharma</s> at a later time'; or those who take refuge in emptiness through apprehending emptiness [as a thing], [thinking:] 'Emptiness is some entity separate from form and so forth, which we shall realize and cultivate.' There, what is that approach to the meaning of the emptiness of the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>?

body.text: nāpaneyamataḥ kiṃcidupaneyaṃ na kiṃcana /
body.translated_text: There is nothing here to be removed, and nothing whatsoever to be added;

body.text: draṣṭavyaṃ bhūtato bhūtaṃ bhūtadarśī vimucyate // 154 //
body.translated_text: the real is to be seen as it truly is—one who sees the real is liberated. // 154 //

children.translated_text: The element (<s>dhātu</s>) is empty of adventitious [defilements] having the character of separability;
it is not empty of unsurpassed qualities having the character of inseparability. // 155 //

body.text: kimanena paridīpitam / yato na kiṃcidapaneyamastyataḥ prakṛtipariśuddhāt tathāgatadhātoḥ saṃkleśanimittamāgantukamalaśūnyatāprakṛtitvādasya / nāpyatrakiṃcidupaneyamasti vyavadānanimittamavinirbhāgaśuddhadharmaprakṛtitvāt / tata ucyate / śūnyastathāgatagarbho vinirbhāgairmuktajñaiḥ sarvakleśakośaiḥ / aśūnyo gaṅgānadīvālikāvyativṛttairavinirbhāgairamuktajñairacintyairbuddhadharmairiti / evaṃ yadyatra nāsti tattena śūnyamiti samanupaśyati / yatpunaratrāvaśiṣṭaṃ bhavati tatsadihāstīti yathābhūtaṃ prajānāti / samāropāpavādāntaparivarjanādaparyantaṃ śūnyatālakṣaṇamanena ślokadvayena paridīpitam / tatra yeṣāmitaḥ śūnyatārthanayādvahiścittaṃ vikṣipyate visarati na samādhīyate naikāgrībhavati tena te śūnyatāvikṣiptacittā ucyante / na hi paramārthaśūnyatājñānamukhamantareṇa śakyate 'vikalpo dhāturadhigantuṃ sākṣātkartum / idaṃ ca saṃdhāyoktam / tathāgatagarbhajñānameva tathāgatānāṃ śūnyatājñānam / tathāgatagarbhaśca sarvaśrāvakapratyekabuddhairadṛṣṭapūrvo 'nadhigatapūrva iti vistaraḥ / sa khalveṣa tathāgatagarbho yathā dharmadhātugarbhastathā satkāyadṛṣṭipatitānāmagocara ityuktaṃ dṛṣṭipratipakṣatvāddharmadhātoḥ / yathā dharmakāyo lokottaradharma garbhastathā viparyāsābhiratānāmagocara ityuktamanityādilokadharmapratipakṣeṇa lokottaradharmaparidīpanāt / yathā prakṛtipariśuddhadharmagarbhastathā śūnyatāvikṣiptānāmagocara ityuktamāgantukamalaśūnyatāprakṛtitvādviśuddhiguṇadharmāṇāmavinirbhāgalokottaradharmakāyaprabhāvitānāmiti /
body.translated_text: What is illuminated by this? Since there is nothing to be removed from the <s>Tathāgata</s>-element that is naturally pure—because adventitious defilement, the cause of affliction, is by nature empty of this [element]; and since there is nothing to be added here—because inseparable pure qualities, the cause of purification, are its very nature: therefore it is said, 'The <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> is empty of the separable, freed-knowledge, sheaths of all afflictions; it is not empty of the inseparable, unfreed-knowledge, inconceivable <s>Buddha</s>-qualities exceeding the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river.' Thus, what is not present here—seeing that as empty; and what remains here as present—knowing that as truly existent: through avoiding the extremes of superimposition and denial, the boundless characteristic of emptiness has been illuminated by these two verses. There, those whose minds are cast out and scattered, not collected, not one-pointed, away from this approach to the meaning of emptiness—they are said to be 'those whose minds are distracted by emptiness.' For without the gate of the knowledge of ultimate emptiness, the non-conceptual element cannot be realized, cannot be directly experienced. And with this in mind it was said: 'The <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>-knowledge is the emptiness-knowledge of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. And the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> has never been seen before, never been attained before, by all <s>Śrāvakas</s> and <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>,' and so on in detail. This <s>tathāgatagarbha</s>—just as it is the <s>dharmadhātu</s>-<s>garbha</s>, so it is said to be beyond the domain of those fallen into the view of a self in the aggregates, because the <s>dharmadhātu</s> is the antidote to [that] view. Just as it is the <s>garbha</s> of supramundane qualities as <s>dharmakāya</s>, so it is said to be beyond the domain of those delighting in the inversions, because the supramundane qualities are illuminated as antidotes to worldly phenomena such as impermanence. Just as it is the <s>garbha</s> of naturally pure <s>dharmas</s>, so it is said to be beyond the domain of those distracted by emptiness, because the adventitious defilements are by nature empty [of the element], and the pure quality-<s>dharmas</s> are inseparable, manifested by the supramundane <s>dharmakāya</s>.

body.text: tatra yadekanayadharmadhātvasaṃbhedajñānamukhamāgamya lokottaradharmakāyaprakṛtipariśuddhivyavalokanamidamatra yathābhūtajñānadarśanamabhipretaṃ yena daśabhūmisthitā bodhisattvāstathāgatagarbhamīṣatpaśyantītyuktam / evaṃ hyāha /
body.translated_text: There, the seeing of the natural purity of the supramundane <s>dharmakāya</s>, arrived at through the gate of the knowledge of the non-disintegration of the one-approach <s>dharmadhātu</s>—this is what is intended here as the knowledge-vision in accordance with reality, by which it is said that <s>Bodhisattvas</s> abiding on the ten stages 'see the <s>tathāgatagarbha</s> slightly.' For thus he says:

children.text: chidrābhre nabhasīva bhāskara iha tvaṃ śuddhabuddhīkṣaṇair
children.translated_text: Like the sun in a sky with parted clouds, here you are beheld through moments of pure insight,
yet even by the noble ones you are not seen in full, [but only] by partial understanding;
but your <s>Dharmakāya</s>, spread across the sky-expanse of infinite knowable [reality]—
those whose understanding is infinite behold that in its totality, O <s>Bhagavan</s>. //

body.text: yadyevamasaṅganiṣṭhābhūmipratiṣṭhitānāmapi paramāryāṇāmasarvaviṣaya eṣa durdṛśo dhātuḥ / tatkimanena bālapṛthagjanamārabhya deśiteneti / deśanāprayojanasaṃgrahe ślokau / ekena praśno dvitīyena vyākaraṇam /
body.translated_text: If even for the supreme noble ones established on the stage of non-attachment, this element is difficult to see and not within the scope of all—then what purpose is served by teaching it beginning from childish ordinary persons? In the summary of the purpose of teaching, there are two verses: by the first, the question; by the second, the answer.

children.text: śūnyaṃ sarvaṃ sarvathā tatra tatra jñeyaṃ meghasvapnamāyākṛtābham /
children.translated_text: All is empty in every way, everywhere; the knowable appears like clouds, dreams, and illusions—

children.text: ityuktvaivaṃ buddhadhātuḥ punaḥ kiṃ sattve sattve 'stīti buddhairihoktam // 156 //
children.translated_text: having said this, why then have the <s>Buddhas</s> here declared that <s>Buddhadhātu</s> (buddha-nature) exists in each and every being? // 156 //
A contracted mind, contempt toward those of inferior disposition, grasping at the unreal, denial of the true <s>Dharma</s>,

children.text: ātmasnehaścādhikaḥ pañca doṣā yeṣāṃ teṣāṃ tatprahāṇārthamuktam // 157 //
children.translated_text: and excessive self-love—these are five faults; for the abandonment of these in those [who possess them], it has been spoken. // 157 //

body.text: asya khalu ślokadvayasyārthaḥ samāsena daśabhiḥ ślokairveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The meaning of these two verses is to be understood in brief by ten verses.

body.text: viviktaṃ saṃskṛtaṃ sarvaprakāraṃ bhūtakoṭiṣu /
body.translated_text: The isolated, the conditioned, [and what appears] in every way among the true limits of existence,

body.text: kleśakarmavipākārthaṃ meghādivadudāhṛtam // 158 //
body.translated_text: have been illustrated like clouds and so forth for the purpose of [understanding] affliction, action, and ripening. // 158 //

children.translated_text: Afflictions are like clouds; the performance of deeds is like enjoyment in a dream;
the aggregates, which are the ripening of affliction and action, are like magical creations. // 159 //
Having previously established [the teaching] in this way in the [earlier] treatise, now here again in the Uttara [Tantra],
for the abandonment of the five faults, the existence of the element has been illuminated. // 160 //

children.text: tathā hyaśravaṇādasya bodhau cittaṃ na jāyate /
children.translated_text: For without hearing of this, the mind toward awakening does not arise;
in some of low mind, due to the fault of self-contempt. // 161 //

body.text: bodhicittodaye 'pyasya śreyānasmīti manyataḥ

children.translated_text: engages in the perception of inferiority toward those in whom the mind of awakening has not arisen. // 162 //

body.translated_text: Even when the mind of awakening has arisen, one who thinks 'I am superior'

children.translated_text: For one of such views, correct knowledge does not arise; therefore
one grasps the unreal and does not find the true meaning. // 163 //
The unreal are the faults of beings, because they are adventitious and fabricated;
the real is the selflessness of those faults—the qualities whose nature is purity. // 164 //
Grasping the faults as truly existent, and denying the qualities that are truly real,
the wise one does not obtain the great loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) that regards self and beings equally. // 165 //
But from hearing of this, enthusiasm arises in one, along with reverence for the Teacher,
wisdom, knowledge, and great loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>)—from the arising of these five qualities, therefore: // 166 //
Without contempt, seeing equally, faultless, endowed with qualities,
with equal love for self and beings, one swiftly attains <s>Buddhahood</s>. // 167 //

body.text: iti ratnagotravibhāge mahāyānottaratantraśāstre tathāgatagarbhādhikāraḥ prathama paricchedaḥ ślokārthasaṃgrahavyākhyānataḥ samāptaḥ // 1 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter on <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> in the <s>Ratnagotravibhāga Mahāyānottaratantraśāstra</s>, in the form of a commentary summarizing the meaning of the verses. // 1 //

body.text: 2. dvitīya pariccheda
body.translated_text: 2. Second Chapter

body.text: uktā samalā tathatā / nirmalā tathatedānīṃ vaktavyā / tatra katamā nirmalā tathatā yāsau buddhānāṃ bhagavatāmanāsravadhātau sarvākāramalavigamādāśrayaparivṛttirvyavasthāpyate / sā punaraṣṭau padārthānadhikṛtya samāsato veditavyā / aṣṭau padārthāḥ katame /
body.translated_text: The defiled <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) has been explained. Now the undefiled <s>tathatā</s> is to be explained. There, what is the undefiled <s>tathatā</s>? It is that which, in the undefiled element (<s>anāsravadhātu</s>) of the <s>Buddhas</s>, the <s>Bhagavāns</s>, is established as the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>) through the departure of defilements in every aspect. That, moreover, is to be understood in brief with reference to eight topics. What are the eight topics?

children.translated_text: Purity, attainment, freedom, benefit to self and others, the basis of those,
profundity, vastness, and greatness—for as long and in whatever manner that [exists]. // 1 //

body.text: ityete 'ṣṭau padārthā yathāsaṃkhyamanena ślokena paridīpitāḥ / tadyathā svabhāvārtho hetvarthaḥ phalārthaḥ karmārtho yogārtho vṛttyartho nityārtho 'cintyārthaḥ / tatra yo 'sau dhāturavinirmuktakleśakośastathāgatagarbha ityukto bhagavatā / tadviśuddhirāśrayaparivṛtteḥ svabhāvo veditavyaḥ / yata āha / yo bhagavan sarvakleśakośakoṭigūḍhe tathāgatagarbhe niṣkāṅkṣaḥ sarvakleśakośavinirmuktestathāgatadharmakāye 'pi sa niṣkāṅkṣa iti / dvividhaṃ jñānaṃ lokottaramavikalpaṃ tatpṛṣṭhalabdhaṃ ca / laukikalokottarajñānamāśrayaparivṛttihetuḥ prāptiśabdena paridīpitaḥ / prāpyate 'neneti prāptiḥ / tatphalaṃ dvividham / dvividho visaṃyogaḥ kleśāvaraṇavisaṃyogo jñeyāvaraṇavisaṃyogaśca / yathākramaṃ svaparārthasaṃpādanaṃ karma / tadadhiṣṭhānasamanvāgamo yogaḥ / tribhirgāmbhīryaudāryamāhātmyaprabhavitairbuddhakāyairnityamā bhavagateracintyena prakāreṇa vartanaṃ vṛttiriti / uddānam /
body.translated_text: These eight topics are illuminated in order by this verse: namely, the meaning of intrinsic nature (<s>svabhāvārtha</s>), the meaning of cause (<s>hetvārtha</s>), the meaning of result (<s>phalārtha</s>), the meaning of function (<s>karmārtha</s>), the meaning of union (<s>yogārtha</s>), the meaning of activity (<s>vṛttyārtha</s>), the meaning of permanence (<s>nityārtha</s>), and the meaning of inconceivability (<s>acintyārtha</s>). There, that element (<s>dhātu</s>), which was called by the <s>Bhagavān</s> '<s>Tathāgatagarbha</s>' when not freed from the sheath of afflictions—its purification is to be understood as the intrinsic nature of the transformation of the basis. As he said: 'Whoever, O <s>Bhagavan</s>, is without doubt regarding the <s>Tathāgatagarbha</s> concealed within the sheaths of all afflictions, that one is also without doubt regarding the <s>Tathāgata</s>'s <s>Dharmakāya</s> freed from all affliction-sheaths.' The twofold knowledge—the supramundane non-conceptual [knowledge] and the subsequently attained [knowledge]—the worldly-supramundane knowledge that is the cause of the transformation of the basis is illuminated by the term 'attainment.' Attainment (<s>prāpti</s>) means 'that by which one attains.' Its result is twofold: the twofold freedom—freedom from the obscuration of afflictions (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>) and freedom from the obscuration of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>). In due order, the accomplishment of benefit for self and others is the function. The possession of its basis is the union (<s>yoga</s>). The activity in permanence, from the limit of existence, through the three bodies endowed with profundity, vastness, and greatness, in an inconceivable manner, is the activity (<s>vṛtti</s>). The summary:

children.translated_text: From the standpoint of intrinsic nature, cause, result, function, union, and activity,
and from its permanence and inconceivability—[such is] the establishment on the <s>Buddha</s>-stages. // 2 //

body.text: tatra svabhāvārthe hetvarthe cārabhya buddhatve tatprāptyupāye ca ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: There, beginning with the meaning of intrinsic nature and the meaning of cause, regarding <s>Buddhahood</s> and the means of its attainment, there is a verse:

children.text: buddhatvaṃ prakṛtiprabhāsvaramiti proktaṃ yadāgantuka- kleśajñeyaghanābhrajālapaṭalacchannaṃ ravivyomavat /
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhahood</s>, said to be luminous by nature, with its adventitious obscuration of thick cloud-masses of affliction and the knowable, concealed like the sun [behind clouds] and like space [behind obscurations],
endowed with all <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, stainless, permanent, stable, eternal—
it is attained through the basis of the knowledge of non-conceptualization and discernment of <s>dharmas</s>. // 3 //
The meaning of this verse is to be understood in brief by four verses:
<s>Buddhahood</s> is characterized by inseparable pure qualities,
having the dual character of knowledge and abandonment, like the sun and space. // 4 //
Endowed with all the luminous <s>Buddha</s>-qualities exceeding the sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s> river,
uncreated, with inseparable functions. // 5 //
Because of the nature of non-accomplishment, pervasiveness, and adventitious character,
the obscuration of affliction and the knowable is therefore illustrated as being like a cloud. // 6 //
The cause of the separation from the twofold obscuration is the twofold knowledge:
the non-conceptual and the subsequently attained—that knowledge is regarded [as the cause]. // 7 //

body.text: yaduktamāśrayaparivṛtteḥ svabhāvo viśuddhiriti tatra viśuddhiḥ samāsato dvividhā / prakṛtiviśuddhirvaimalyaviśuddhiśca / tatra prakṛtiviśuddhiryā vimuktirna ca visaṃyogaḥ prabhāsvarāyāścittaprakṛterāgantukamalāvisaṃyogāt / vaimalyaviśuddhirvimuktirvisaṃyogaśca vāryādīnāmiva rajojalādibhyaḥ prabhāsvarāyāścittaprakṛteranavaśeṣamāgantukamalebhyo visaṃyogāt / tatra vaimalyaviśuddhau phalārthamārabhya dvau ślokau /
body.translated_text: As was said, 'the intrinsic nature of the transformation of the basis is purification'—there, purification is in brief twofold: natural purity (<s>prakṛtiviśuddhi</s>) and stainless purity (<s>vaimalyaviśuddhi</s>). There, natural purity is liberation but not freedom, because of the non-separation from adventitious defilements of the naturally luminous mind. Stainless purity is both liberation and freedom, because of the complete separation from adventitious defilements of the naturally luminous mind, like water and other things from mud and impurities. There, regarding stainless purity, beginning with the meaning of result, there are two verses:

body.text: hrada iva vimalāmbuḥ phullapadmakramāḍhyaḥ
body.translated_text: Like a lake with pure water, adorned with blooming lotuses,

children.translated_text: like the full moon freed from the mouth of <s>Rāhu</s>,
like the sun with its rays freed from the clouds and other afflictions—
because of being endowed with stainless qualities, that very [nature] shines forth, liberated. // 8 //
Like the honey of the supreme bull among sages, like gold, like a jewel, like a supreme treasure, like a great fruit-tree—
resembling the stainless jewel-body of the <s>Sugata</s>, the supreme sovereign, and a golden image—such is <s>Jinahood</s> (Buddhahood). // 9 //

body.text: asya khalu ślokadvayasyārthaḥ samāsato 'ṣṭābhiḥ ślokairveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The meaning of these two verses is to be understood in brief by eight verses:

children.translated_text: Purity from adventitious afflictions such as passion and the rest, like a lake of water and so forth—
this is the result of non-conceptual knowledge, stated in summary. // 10 //
The demonstration of <s>Buddhahood</s> endowed with excellent qualities of every kind—
the result of subsequently attained knowledge has been illuminated. // 11 //
Like a lake of clear water, through the removal of the turbidity and impurity of passion,
and through the outpouring of the water of <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) upon the lotuses of those to be trained. // 12 //
Through liberation from <s>Rāhu</s>-like hatred, through the rays of great loving-kindness (<s>maitrī</s>) and compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>),
through pervading all beings—it is like the full, stainless moon. // 13 //
Through liberation from the cloud-mass of delusion, through rays of knowledge upon the world,
through dispelling darkness—<s>Buddhahood</s> is like the stainless sun. // 14 //
Because of having qualities both unequaled and equal, because of giving the nectar of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
and because of the departure of the worthless—it is like the essence of the honey of the <s>Sugata</s>. // 15 //

body.text: pavitratvādguṇadravyadāridrayavinivartanāt /
body.translated_text: Because of purity, because of removing the poverty of quality-resources,

body.text: vimuktiphaladānācca suvarṇanidhivṛkṣavat // 16 //
body.translated_text: because of giving the fruit of liberation—it is like a golden treasure and a tree. // 16 //

children.translated_text: Because of the nature of the <s>Dharma</s>-jewel embodiment, because of sovereignty over the supreme bipeds,
and because of the form of a jewel-image—it is like a jewel, a sovereign, and an image. // 17 //

body.text: yattu dvividhaṃ lokottaramavikalpaṃ tatpṛṣṭhalabdhaṃ ca jñānamāśrayaparivṛtterheturvisaṃyogaphalasaṃjñitāyāḥ / tatkarma svaparārthasaṃpādanamityuktam / tatra katamā svaparārthasaṃpat / yā savāsanakleśajñeyāvaraṇavimokṣādanāvaraṇadharmakāyaprāptiriyamucyate svārthasaṃpattiḥ / yā tadūrdhvamā lokādanābhogataḥ kāyadvayena saṃdarśanadeśanāvibhutvadvayapravṛttiriyamucyate parārthasaṃpattiriti / tasyāṃ svaparārthasaṃpattau karmārthamārabhya trayaḥ ślokāḥ /
body.translated_text: As for the twofold knowledge—the supramundane non-conceptual and the subsequently attained—being the cause of the transformation of the basis designated as the result of freedom, its function is said to be the accomplishment of benefit for self and others. There, what is the accomplishment of benefit for self and others? That which, through liberation from the obscurations of affliction and the knowable together with their residual impressions, is the attainment of the unobstructed <s>Dharmakāya</s>—this is called the accomplishment of benefit for oneself. That which, after that, from the limit of existence, effortlessly, through the two bodies, is the activity in the dual capacity of manifestation and teaching—this is called the accomplishment of benefit for others. Regarding the meaning of function in that accomplishment of benefit for self and others, there are three verses:

children.text: anāsravaṃ vyāpyavināśadharmi ca dhruvaṃ śivaṃ śāśvatamacyutaṃ padam /
children.translated_text: Undefiled, pervading, of the nature of destruction, stable, auspicious, eternal, and unfallen—the state
of <s>Tathāgatahood</s>, like space, is the cause of experiences in the six sense-objects of the noble ones. // 18 //
It is the magnificent cause of displaying form-objects at all times, of hearing well-spoken [words],
of smelling the pure moral conduct of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, and of tasting the supreme nectar of the noble true <s>Dharma</s>. // 19 //

body.text: samādhisaṃsparśasukhānubhūtiṣu svabhāvagāmbhīryanayāvabodhane /
body.translated_text: In the experiences of the bliss of <s>samādhi</s>-contact, and in the realization of the profundity of the nature [of things],

body.text: susūkṣmacintāparamārthagavharaṃ tathāgatavyoma nimittavarjitam // 20 //
body.translated_text: the space of <s>Tathāgatahood</s>, the most subtle domain of ultimate reflection, is free from signs. // 20 //

body.text: asya khalu ślokatrayasyārthaḥ samāsato 'ṣṭabhiḥ ślokairveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The meaning of these three verses is to be understood in brief by eight verses:

children.translated_text: The function of the twofold knowledge is to be understood in summary:
the fulfillment of the liberation-body and the purification of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. // 21 //
The liberation-body and the <s>Dharmakāya</s> are each to be understood as twofold in one [respect]:
from the standpoint of being undefiled, being pervading, and being the state of the unconditioned. // 22 //
Being undefiled is due to the cessation of afflictions together with their residual impressions;
pervasiveness of knowledge is regarded as [arising from] non-attachment and non-obstruction. // 23 //
Being unconditioned is due to the nature of ultimate indestructibility;
indestructibility is the general statement—its detailed exposition is through 'stable' and the rest. // 24 //
Destruction is to be known as fourfold, being the opposite of stability and so forth:
dissolution, alteration, extinction, and inconceivable non-declining. // 25 //
Due to the absence of those [four destructions], it is to be known as stable, auspicious, eternal, and unfallen—
that state is stainless knowledge, because it is the abode of pure qualities. // 26 //
Just as space, being without signs, is the condition for seeing form,
and for hearing sound, smelling scent, tasting flavor, and touching the tangible, and for [cognizing] mental objects. // 27 //

body.text: indriyārtheṣu dhīrāṇāmanāsravaguṇodaye /
body.translated_text: In the arising of undefiled qualities in the sense-experiences of the steadfast ones,

body.text: hetuḥ kāyadvayaṃ tadvadanāvaraṇayogataḥ // 28 //
body.translated_text: the twofold body is likewise the cause, through the connection of non-obstruction. // 28 //

body.text: yaduktamākāśalakṣaṇo buddha iti tatpāramārthikamāveṇikaṃ tathāgatānāṃ buddhalakṣaṇamabhisaṃdhāyoktam / evaṃ hyāha / saṃceddvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇaistathāgato draṣṭavyo 'bhaviṣyattadrājāpi cakravartī tathāgato 'bhaviṣyaditi / tatra paramārthalakṣaṇe yogārthamārabhya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: As was said, 'a <s>Buddha</s> has the characteristic of space'—that was said with reference to the ultimate, distinctive characteristic of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. For thus it is said: 'If the <s>Tathāgata</s> were to be seen by the thirty-two marks of a great person, then a <s>cakravartin</s> king would also be a <s>Tathāgata</s>.' There, regarding the meaning of union with respect to the ultimate characteristic, there is a verse:

children.text: acintyaṃ nityaṃ ca dhruvamatha śivaṃ śāśvatamatha
children.translated_text: Inconceivable, permanent, stable, auspicious, eternal,
peaceful, pervading, free from conceptualization, like space,
unattached everywhere, free from the harsh touch of aversion and obstruction,

children.text: na dṛśyaṃ na grāhyaṃ śubhamapi ca buddhatvamamalam // 29 //
children.translated_text: not visible, not graspable, and auspicious—<s>Buddhahood</s> is stainless. // 29 //

body.text: atha khalvasya ślokasyārthaḥ samāsato 'ṣṭābhiḥ ślokairveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The meaning of this verse is to be understood in brief by eight verses:

children.translated_text: Through the liberation-body and <s>Dharmakāya</s>, benefit for self and others has been demonstrated;
the union in that basis of benefit for self and others [is characterized by] qualities such as inconceivability and so forth. // 30 //
It is inconceivable because it is beyond the domain of the three knowledges;
<s>Buddhahood</s>, the domain of omniscient knowledge, [is to be realized] by those who embody knowledge. // 31 //
Beyond the domain of learning because of subtlety, beyond conceptual thought in ultimate reality,
and beyond worldly and other meditation, because of the profundity of <s>dharmatā</s>. // 32 //
Because it has never been seen before by the childish, like the body of one blind from birth,
and even by the noble ones, like the disc of the newborn sun [seen by one] standing in the midst of a birthing chamber. // 33 //
Permanent because of the cessation of arising, stable because of the cessation of cessation,
blissful because of the absence of both, eternal because of abiding in <s>dharmatā</s>. // 34 //

body.text: śāntaṃ nirodhasatyatvādvyāpi sarvāvabodhataḥ /
body.translated_text: Peaceful because of being the truth of cessation, all-pervading because of complete awakening to all,

body.text: akalpamapratiṣṭhānādasaktaṃ kleśahānitaḥ // 35 //
body.translated_text: non-conceptual because of being without foundation, unattached because of the destruction of afflictions. // 35 //

children.translated_text: Unobstructed everywhere because of purification from all cognitive obscurations,
free from rough contact because of softness and workability. // 36 //
Invisible because of being formless, ungraspable because of being signless,
auspicious because of natural purity, stainless because of the removal of stains. // 37 //

body.text: yatpunaretadākāśavadasaṃskṛtaguṇāvinirbhāgavṛttyāpi tathāgatatvāmā bhavagateracintyamahopāyakruṇājñānaparikarmaviśeṣeṇa jagaddhitasukhādhānanimittamamalai stribhiḥ svabhāvikasāṃbhogikanairmāṇikaiḥ kāyairanuparatamanucchinnamanābhogena pravartata iti draṣṭavyamāveṇīkadharmayutatvāditi / tatra vṛttyarthamārabhya buddhakāyavibhāge catvāraḥ ślokāḥ /
body.translated_text: Furthermore, that which, though functioning in an undivided manner with unconditioned qualities like space, as <s>Tathāgata</s>-nature—through the distinction of the inconceivable great skillful means, compassion, and knowledge that purify [beings] from the course of existence—for the purpose of establishing the welfare and happiness of the world, through the three stainless bodies—the <s>svābhāvika</s> (natural), <s>sāṃbhogika</s> (enjoyment), and <s>nairmāṇika</s> (emanation)—operates unceasingly, uninterruptedly, and effortlessly: this is to be seen as being endowed with exclusive qualities (<s>āveṇikadharma</s>). There, beginning with the meaning of activity, in the division of <s>Buddha</s>-bodies, there are four verses:

children.translated_text: Without beginning, middle, or end, undivided, non-dual, liberated in three ways, stainless, non-conceptual,
that which yogins in meditation, through their efforts, behold—the nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. // 38 //

body.text: ameyagaṅgāsikatātivṛttairguṇairacintyairasamairupetaḥ /
body.translated_text: Endowed with inconceivable, incomparable qualities exceeding the immeasurable sands of the <s>Gaṅgā</s>,

body.text: savāsanonmūlitasarvadoṣastathāgatānāmamalaḥ sa dhātuḥ // 39 //
body.translated_text: with all faults uprooted together with their habitual tendencies—that is the stainless element of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>. // 39 //

children.translated_text: With bodies [emanating] rays of the diverse true <s>Dharma</s>, its efforts gathered for the purpose of liberating the world,
in its activities, it is of varied manifestation like the wish-fulfilling jewel-king, yet not of that [varied] nature. // 40 //
That which in the worlds is the cause of descent upon the path of peace, ripening, and prediction,
that reflection, too, is here always contained, like the form-element in the space-element. // 41 //

body.text: eṣāṃ khalu caturṇāṃ ślokānāṃ piṇḍārtho viṃśatiślokairveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The condensed meaning of these four verses is to be understood through twenty verses:

children.translated_text: That which is called <s>Buddhatva</s> (Buddhahood), the omniscience of the self-born ones,
is cessation, the supreme inconceivable attainment, individually realized. // 42 //
Its differentiation is through three bodies—the <s>svābhāvika</s> (natural) and so forth—in [their] activity,
characterized by the qualities of profundity, nobility, and greatness. // 43 //
There, the <s>svābhāvikakāya</s> (natural body) of the <s>Buddhas</s> has five characteristics,
and is to be understood in brief as possessing qualities of five kinds. // 44 //
Unconditioned, undivided, free from the two extremes,
freed from the three obscurations of affliction, cognition, and meditative attainment. // 45 //

body.text: vaimalyādavikalpatvādyogināṃ gocaratvataḥ /
body.translated_text: Because of purity, because of non-conceptuality, because of being the domain of yogins,

body.text: prabhāsvaraṃ viśuddhaṃ ca dharmadhātoḥ svabhāvataḥ // 46 //
body.translated_text: it is luminous and thoroughly pure by the nature of the <s>dharmadhātu</s>. // 46 //

children.translated_text: With immeasurable, innumerable, inconceivable, incomparable qualities,
having reached the perfection of purity—endowed [with these] is the <s>svābhāvikakāya</s> (natural body). // 47 //
Because of sublimity, because of being uncountable, because of being beyond the domain of reasoning,
because of uniqueness, because of the cutting off of habitual tendencies—[these are] immeasurable and so forth, in order. // 48 //
Because of manifesting the form-<s>dharmas</s> of the enjoyment of diverse <s>Dharma</s>,
because of never relinquishing the welfare of beings, as the outflow of the purity of compassion. // 49 //
Non-conceptual, effortless, fulfilling [wishes] according to intention,
the establishment of the <s>sāṃbhogikakāya</s> (enjoyment body) is through the abundant power of the wish-fulfilling gem. // 50 //
In teaching, in appearance, in never relinquishing duty, in being unconditioned,
and in being declared as not of that nature—the variety is spoken of fivefold. // 51 //
Just as the gem's not being of that nature [arises] from the variety of conditions of coloring,
so too the all-pervading [Lord's] not being of that nature [arises] from the variety of conditions of beings. // 52 //
Having surveyed the entire world with great compassion, the knower of the world,
from the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, unceasingly, through emanations of various forms, // 53 //
displays birth-stories (<s>jātaka</s>), taking birth, descent from <s>Tuṣita</s> [heaven],
entering the womb, birth, the stations of craft, and skill. // 54 //

body.text: antaḥpuraratikrīḍāṃ naiṣkramyaṃ duḥkhacārikām /
body.translated_text: Enjoyment and play in the inner palace, renunciation, the practice of austerities,

body.text: bodhimaṇḍopasaṃkrāntiṃ mārasainyapramardanam // 55 //
body.translated_text: approaching the seat of awakening (<s>bodhimaṇḍa</s>), crushing the army of <s>Māra</s>. // 55 //

children.translated_text: Full awakening, the wheel of <s>Dharma</s>, and the act of attaining <s>nirvāṇa</s>—
[all these] he displays in impure fields for as long as existence endures. // 56 //
The knower of skillful means, with the words 'impermanent,' 'suffering,' 'non-self,' and 'peace,'
having caused revulsion in beings toward the three realms of existence, ferries them across to cessation. // 57 //
And those who have descended upon the path of peace and hold the notion of having attained <s>nirvāṇa</s>,
through illuminations of the reality of <s>Dharma</s> such as the <s>Saddharmapuṇḍarīka</s> and others, // 58 //
having turned them from their former attachments through the embrace of wisdom and skillful means,
ripening [them] in the supreme vehicle, [he] prophesies [their] foremost awakening. // 59 //
Because of subtlety, because of the abundance of power, because of conveying the childish caravan [to safety],
profundity, nobility, and greatness are to be known in these, in order. // 60 //
Here, the first is the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, while the two latter are the <s>Rūpakāyas</s>;
just as form [exists] in space, the latter [bodies] abide in the first. // 61 //

body.text: tasyaiva kāyatrayasya jagaddhitasukhādhānavṛttau nityārthamārabhya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: Regarding the activity of that very triad of bodies in establishing the welfare and happiness of the world, beginning with the meaning of permanence, [there is] a verse:

body.text: hetvānantyāt sattvadhātvakṣayatvāt kāruṇyaddhirjñānasaṃpattiyogāt /
body.translated_text: Because of the infinity of causes, because of the inexhaustibility of the realm of beings, because of the connection with the wealth of compassion, firmness, and knowledge,

body.text: dharmaiśvaryānmṛtyumārāvabhaṅgān naiḥsvā bhāvyācchāśvato lokanāthaḥ // 62 //
body.translated_text: because of the sovereignty of <s>Dharma</s>, because of the indestructibility by the <s>Māra</s> of death, because of [his] selfless nature—the Lord of the World is eternal. // 62 //

body.text: asya piṇḍārthaḥ ṣaḍbhiḥ ślokairveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The condensed meaning of this is to be understood through six verses:

children.translated_text: Through the sacrifices of body, life, and enjoyments, through the gathering of the true <s>Dharma</s>,
because of fulfilling the initial vow for the welfare of all beings. // 63 //
Because of the operation of thoroughly purified compassion in <s>Buddhahood</s>,
and because of the manifestation of the bases of supernatural power (<s>ṛddhipāda</s>), through their power to remain. // 64 //
Through knowledge, liberation from the dual grasping of existence and <s>nirvāṇa</s>,
because of the ever-inconceivable connection with the wealth of the bliss of equilibrium. // 65 //
Because of being unstained by worldly phenomena while moving through the world,
because of the non-operation of the <s>Māra</s> of death upon attaining the immortal state of peace. // 66 //
Because of the primordial peace of the sage whose nature is unconditioned,
and because of being eternally the refuge of those without refuge. // 67 //
By the first seven causes, permanence is [established] from the perspective of the <s>Rūpakāya</s>;
and by the last three, permanence of the Teacher is [established] from the perspective of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. // 68 //

body.text:
sa cāyamāśrayaparivṛttiprabhāvitastathāgatānāṃ prāptinayo 'cintyanayenānugantavya iti /
acintyārthamārabhya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: And this method of attainment of the <s>Tathāgatas</s>, brought about by the transformation of the basis (<s>āśrayaparivṛtti</s>), is to be followed through the approach of inconceivability. Beginning with the meaning of inconceivability, [there is] a verse:

body.text: avākyavattvāt paramārthasaṃgrahādatarkabhūmerupamanivṛttitaḥ /
body.translated_text: Because of being inexpressible, because of encompassing the ultimate, because of [its] cessation being on the ground beyond reasoning,

body.text: niruttaratvādbhavaśāntyanudgrahādacintya āryairapi buddhagocaraḥ // 69 //
body.translated_text: because of being unsurpassed, because of not favoring either existence or peace—the domain of the <s>Buddhas</s> is inconceivable even to the noble ones. // 69 //

body.text: asya piṇḍārthaścaturbhiḥ ślokairveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The condensed meaning of this is to be understood through four verses:

children.translated_text: Inconceivable because of being inexpressible; inexpressible because [it is] the ultimate reality;
the ultimate reality because of being beyond dispute; beyond reasoning because it is beyond inference. // 70 //
Beyond inference because of being unsurpassed; unsurpassed because of not being taken up [by anything higher];
not taken up because of being without foundation, because of non-conceptualization of qualities and faults. // 71 //
By five causes, beginning with subtlety, it is inconceivable from the perspective of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>;
by the sixth, because of not being of that nature, it is inconceivable from the perspective of the <s>Rūpakāya</s>. // 72 //
With unsurpassed knowledge, great compassion, and other qualities, the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones) who have gone to the far shore of qualities are inconceivable;

children.text: ataḥ kramo 'ntyo 'yamapi svayaṃbhuvo 'bhiṣekalabdhā na maharṣayo viduriti // 73 //
children.translated_text: therefore, even the great sages who have obtained consecration do not know this final stage of the Self-born One. // 73 //

body.text: iti ratnagotravibhāge mahāyānottaratantraśāstre bodhyadhikāro nāma dvitīyaḥ paricchedaḥ // 2 //
body.translated_text: Thus [ends] the second chapter, named 'The Chapter on Awakening,' in the <s>Ratnagotravibhāga</s>, the treatise on the <s>Mahāyānottaratantra</s>. // 2 //

body.text: 3. tṛtīya pariccheda
body.translated_text: 3. Third Chapter

body.text: uktā nirmalā tathatā / ye tadāśritā maṇiprabhāvarṇasaṃsthānavadabhinnaprakṛtayo 'śāntarnimalā guṇāsta idānīṃ vaktavyā iti / anantaraṃ buddhaguṇavibhāgamārabhya ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: The stainless <s>tathatā</s> (suchness) has been described. Those qualities which, depending on it, are like the radiance, color, and shape of a gem—undifferentiated in nature and unstained from within—are now to be discussed. Next, beginning with the division of <s>Buddha</s>-qualities, [there is] a verse:

children.translated_text: Self-benefit, benefit of others, the ultimate body and the conventional embodiment dependent upon it;
the fruit, from the nature of separation and maturation—this [comprises] sixty-four types of qualities. // 1 //

body.text: kimuktaṃ bhavati /
body.translated_text: What has been said?

children.translated_text: The ultimate body is the foundation of one's own accomplishment;
the conventional body of the sage is the foundation of the accomplishment of others. // 2 //
The first body is endowed with the qualities of separation—the powers and so forth;
the second, however, with the marks of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>) that are maturational. // 3 //

body.text: ataḥ paraṃ ye ca balādayo yathā cānugantavyāstathatāmadhikṛtya granthaḥ /
body.translated_text: Henceforth, the text concerns how the powers and other [qualities] are to be understood with reference to <s>tathatā</s>:

children.translated_text: The powers [are] like a thunderbolt among those veiled in ignorance; fearlessness [is] like a lion among assemblies;
the exclusive qualities of the <s>Tathāgata</s> [are] like the sky; the sage's twofold appearance [is] like the moon in water. // 4 //

body.text: balānvita iti /
body.translated_text: Endowed with the powers:

children.translated_text: Regarding what is possible and impossible, regarding the maturation of actions, regarding the faculties,
regarding the elements, regarding inclinations, and regarding the path leading everywhere, // 5 //

body.text: dhyānādikleśavaimalye nivāsānusmṛtāvapi /
body.translated_text: regarding the purity from defilements of <s>dhyāna</s> and so forth, regarding the recollection of former abodes,

body.text: divye cakṣuṣi śāntau ca jñānaṃ daśavidhaṃ balam // 6 //
body.translated_text: regarding the divine eye, and regarding peace—the tenfold knowledge [constitutes] the powers. // 6 //

body.text: vajravaditi /
body.translated_text: Like a thunderbolt:

children.translated_text: Regarding what is possible and impossible, maturation, elements, the various inclinations of the world, the path,
affliction and purification, the group of faculties, the recollection of former abodes,
the divine eye, and in the method of the destruction of outflows—the indestructible, immovable armor of knowledge
is like a thunderbolt in its power to split, scatter, and cut through the wall-tree [of ignorance]. // 7 //

body.text: caturveśāradyaprāpta iti /
body.translated_text: Endowed with the four fearlessnesses:

children.translated_text: In the full awakening to all <s>dharmas</s>, in the prescription of obstacles,
in the declaration of the path, and in the attainment of cessation—the fearlessness is fourfold. // 8 //
From knowledge of the knowable object in all ways, both for oneself and others, from self-proclamation,

children.text: dheye vastuni hānikāraṇakṛteḥ sevye vidhau sevanāt /
children.translated_text: from accomplishing the cause of abandonment regarding what is to be abandoned, from practice regarding the method to be followed,
from attaining what is to be attained—the unsurpassed, supremely pure—and from causing others to attain,
from the noble ones' truthful speech for their own and others' benefit—[there is] fearlessness in any [situation]. // 9 //

body.text: siṃhavaditi /
body.translated_text: Like a lion:

body.text: nityaṃ vanānteṣu yathā mṛgendro nirbhīranuttastagatirmṛgebhyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Just as the king of beasts always [dwells] fearless, undisturbed, and steady among the animals in the forest-glades,

body.text: munīndrasiṃho 'pi tathā gaṇeṣu svastho nirāsthaḥ sthiravikramasthaḥ // 10 //
body.translated_text: so too the lion-like lord of sages [abides] in assemblies—self-composed, without anxiety, firm in valor. // 10 //

body.text: aṣṭadaśāveṇikabuddhadharmasamanvāgata iti /
body.translated_text: Endowed with the eighteen exclusive qualities of a <s>Buddha</s>:

children.text: skhalitaṃ ravitaṃ nāsti śāsturna muṣitā smṛtiḥ /
children.translated_text: The Teacher has no stumbling, no idle chatter, no lapse of mindfulness,
no unconcentrated mind, and no perception of diversity. // 11 //
No indifference without discernment, no decline of zeal or energy,
of mindfulness, wisdom, liberation, or the vision of liberation-knowledge. // 12 //
Action preceded by knowledge, knowledge of the three times unobstructed—
these are the eighteen exclusive qualities of the Teacher, distinct [from others]. // 13 //

children.text: nāsti praskhalitaṃ ravo muṣitatā citte na saṃbhedataḥ
children.translated_text: There is no stumbling, no idle chatter, no lapse, no disturbance of mind,
no perception [of diversity], no indifference without reflection—the sage has no decline of zeal,
nor of energy, mindfulness, or of the thoroughly pure, stainless wisdom, liberation,
liberation-knowledge-vision—because of the complete perception of all knowable objects. // 14 //

body.text:
sarvajñānupurojavānuparivartyartheṣu karmatrayaṃ
triṣvadhvasvaparāhata suvipulajñānapravṛttirdhruvam /
body.translated_text: The threefold action, which follows omniscience and turns to [all] objects, the unfailing, vast operation of knowledge unobstructed in the three times—for oneself and others—

body.text: ityeṣā jinatā mahākaruṇayā yuktāvabuddhā jinair
body.translated_text: this is the <s>Jinatā</s> (victorious nature), united with great compassion, awakened by the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones),

body.text: yadbodhājjagati pravṛttamabhayadaṃ saddharmacakraṃ mahat // 15 //
body.translated_text: from whose awakening the great, fearlessness-bestowing wheel of the true <s>Dharma</s> has been set in motion in the world. // 15 //

body.text: ākāśavaditi /
body.translated_text: Like space:

children.text: yā kṣityādiṣu dharmatā na nabhasaḥ sā dharmatā vidyate
children.translated_text: Whatever <s>dharmatā</s> (nature) exists in earth and so forth does not exist as the <s>dharmatā</s> of space;

children.text: ye cānāvaraṇādilakṣaṇaguṇā vyomno na te rūpiṣu /
children.translated_text: and whatever qualities characterized by unobstructedness and so forth belong to space—those are not found in material things.
Common to the worlds, comparable to earth, water, fire, wind, and space,
[yet] the exclusive nature of the <s>Buddha</s> is never again common to the worlds. // 16 //

body.text: dvātriṃśanmahāpuruṣalakṣaṇarūpadhārīti /
body.translated_text: Bearer of the thirty-two marks of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇa</s>) in form:

children.translated_text: Well-established [feet], wheel-marked, broad-soled feet,
long fingers, webbed hands and feet. // 17 //
Softness of skin, splendor, youthfulness, a body with seven protuberances,
deer-like shanks, concealment of the private parts like an elephant's sheath. // 18 //
A lion-like upper body, well-connected shoulders without gaps,
rounded shoulders, arms that are round, smooth, and well-proportioned. // 19 //

body.text: pralambabāhutā śuddhaprabhāmaṇḍalagātratā /
body.translated_text: Arms reaching down to the knees, a body surrounded by a halo of pure radiance,

body.text: kambugrīvatvamamalaṃ mṛgendrahanutā samā // 20 //
body.translated_text: an immaculate conch-like neck, a jaw like a lion's, evenly formed. // 20 //

children.translated_text: Forty teeth, clear and evenly-spaced teeth,
perfectly pure and even teeth, the finest white canines. // 21 //
An extensive tongue, infinite and inconceivable supremacy of taste,
a voice like the <s>kalaviṅka</s> bird, and the <s>Brahma</s>-voice of the Self-born One. // 22 //
With eyes beautiful as blue lotuses, bull-like eyelashes, a white and pure <s>ūrṇā</s> adorning the lovely face,
an <s>uṣṇīṣa</s> on the head, exceedingly pure and subtle golden-colored complexion, foremost among beings. // 23 //
With each hair separate, soft, upward-growing, turning clockwise on the body, exceedingly fine,
hair like the pure gem of great <s>Indra</s>'s sapphire, a form like the full circle of the <s>nyagrodha</s> tree. // 24 //
Having the strength and firm nature of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, wholly auspicious, the incomparable great sage,
these thirty-two marks of immeasurable radiance are declared as the signs of the Lord of Men, of the Teacher. // 25 //

body.text: dakacandravaditi /
body.translated_text: "Like a cloudless moon" — thus:

body.text:
vyabhre yathā nabhasi candramaso vibhūtiṃ
paśyanti nīlaśaradambumahāhrade ca /
body.translated_text: Just as in a cloudless sky people behold the splendor of the moon, and in a great lake of clear autumn waters —

body.text: saṃbuddhamaṇḍalataleṣu vibhorvibhūtiṃ
body.translated_text: so too in the realms of the fully awakened maṇḍalas, [they behold] the splendor of the All-pervading One,

body.text: tadvijjinātmajagaṇā vyavalokayanti // 26 //
body.translated_text: those knowers, the hosts of the children of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), behold [it]. // 26 //

body.text: itīmāni daśa tathāgatabalāni catvāri vaiśāradyānyaṣṭādaśāveṇikā buddhadharmā dvātriṃśacca mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇānyakenābhisaṃkṣipya catuḥṣaṣṭirbhavanti /
body.translated_text: Thus, these ten <s>Tathāgata</s>-powers (<s>tathāgatabalāni</s>), four fearlessnesses (<s>vaiśāradya</s>), eighteen unique <s>Buddha</s>-qualities (<s>āveṇika buddhadharmāḥ</s>), and thirty-two marks of a great being (<s>mahāpuruṣalakṣaṇāni</s>), when combined into one, become sixty-four.

children.translated_text: And these sixty-four qualities, each with their respective causes,
are to be understood in numerical order following the <s>Ratnasūtra</s>. // 27 //

body.text: eṣāṃ khalu yathoddiṣṭānāmeva catuḥṣaṣṭestathāgataguṇānāmapi yathānupūrvyā vistaravibhāge nirdeśo ratnadārikāsūtrānusāreṇa veditavyaḥ / yatpunareṣu sthāneṣu caturvidhameva yathākramaṃ vajrasiṃhāmvaradakacandrodāharaṇamudāhṛtamasyāpi piṇḍārtho dvādaśabhiḥ ślokairveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: Of these very sixty-four <s>Tathāgata</s>-qualities as enumerated, the detailed exposition in their proper order is to be understood following the <s>Ratnadārikāsūtra</s>. Moreover, the fact that in these topics the fourfold illustration of vajra, lion, space, and cloudless moon has been given in sequence — the condensed meaning of this is to be understood through twelve verses:

children.translated_text: Because of penetrating, fearlessness, uniqueness, and effortlessness,
the illustrations of vajra, lion, space, and cloudless moon [are given]. // 28 //
With regard to the powers and so forth, [the illustration applies] through six powers, three [fearlessnesses], one [set of unique qualities], and [the marks] in sequence,
because of uprooting the defilements together with their residual impressions, [by virtue of] omniscient attainment. // 29 //
Because of splitting, being unshakable, cutting, and [being impenetrable] like armor, rampart, and tree,
the strength of the sage is said to be vajra-like — heavy, essential, firm, and indestructible. // 30 //

children.text: guru kasmādyataḥ sāraṃ sāraṃ kasmādyato dṛḍham /
children.translated_text: Heavy — why? Because it is essential. Essential — why? Because it is firm.
Firm — why? Because it is indestructible. And because of indestructibility, it is like a vajra. // 31 //
Because of fearlessness, because of being unshakable, because of steadfastness, and because of the excellence of prowess,
the fearlessness of <s>Munisiṃha</s> (the Lion among Sages) in the assemblies of followers is like a lion. // 32 //

body.text: sarvābhijñatayā svastho viharatyakutobhayaḥ /
body.translated_text: Through complete direct knowledge (<s>abhijñā</s>), he dwells at ease, free from fear in all directions;

body.text: nirāsthaḥ śuddhasattvebhyo 'pyātmano 'samadarśanāt // 33 //
body.translated_text: unshakable, because of seeing no equal to himself even among beings of pure nature. // 33 //

children.translated_text: Steadfast, because of the mind's constant absorption (<s>samādhi</s>) in all <s>dharmas</s>;
valiant, because of transcending the grounds of the residual impressions of supreme ignorance. // 34 //
Of worldly beings, <s>Śrāvakas</s>, <s>Pratyekabuddhas</s>, and the wise Self-born Ones,
the illustration is fivefold due to the progressively subtler wisdom of each. // 35 //
Because of being the sustenance of the entire world, [the unique qualities] are like earth, water, fire, and wind;
because of having the characteristic of transcending both worldly and supramundane, they are like space. // 36 //
These thirty-two qualities are manifested by the <s>Dharmakāya</s>,
inseparable like the radiance, color, and shape of a jewel-gem. // 37 //
The thirty-two marks are qualities of the body that bring delight upon being seen;
they belong to the twofold <s>Rūpakāya</s> (form body) — the <s>Nirmāṇakāya</s> (emanation body) and <s>Saṃbhogakāya</s> (enjoyment body). // 38 //
For those in impure stations and those in the <s>Jina</s>-maṇḍala, in the world and beyond,
the twofold pure seeing [of the Buddha] is like [seeing a reflection in] water, [the moon in] the sky, and the disc of the moon. // 39 //

body.text: iti ratnagotravibhāge mahāyānottaratnatraśāstre guṇādhikāro nāma tritīyaḥ paricchedaḥ // 3 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the third chapter, named the Chapter on Qualities (<s>Guṇādhikāra</s>), in the <s>Ratnagotravibhāga Mahāyānottaratantraśāstra</s>. // 3 //

body.text: 4. caturthaḥ paricchedaḥ
body.translated_text: 4. Fourth Chapter

body.text:
uktā vimalā buddhaguṇāḥ / tatkarma jinakriyedānīṃ vaktavyā / sā punaranābhogataścāpraśrabdhitaśca samāsato dvābhyāmākarābhyā pravartata iti /
anantaramanābhogāpraśrabdha buddhakāryamārabhya dvau ślokau /
body.translated_text: The pure <s>Buddha</s>-qualities have been stated. Now the activity of the <s>Jina</s> (<s>jinakriyā</s>), the <s>Buddha</s>-activity, is to be explained. That [activity], in brief, proceeds from two aspects: effortlessly (<s>anābhoga</s>) and without cessation (<s>apraśrabdhi</s>). Next, two verses concerning the effortless and unceasing <s>Buddha</s>-activity:

children.translated_text: In the domain of those to be trained, in the means of training, in the training activity of the trainable domain,

children.text: taddeśakāle gamane ca nityaṃ vibhoranābhogata eva vṛttiḥ // 1 //
children.translated_text: in the place and time thereof, and in going — the activity of the All-pervading One is always effortless. // 1 //
Having fully accomplished the foremost vehicle, with the jewel of knowledge as its womb, endowed with supreme collections of qualities,
resembling the vast, infinite, and centerless sky through the widely extended rays of the sun of merit and knowledge,
perceiving <s>Buddhahood</s> — the stainless treasure of qualities — as undifferentiated in all beings,
the compassion of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), like wind, disperses the net of clouds of afflictive and cognitive obscurations. // 2 //

body.text: etayoryathākramaṃ dvābhyāmaṣṭābhiśca ślokaiḥ piṇḍārtho veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The condensed meaning of these two [verses], in order, is to be understood through two and eight verses [respectively]:

children.text: yasya yena ca yāvacca yadā ca vinayakriyā /
children.translated_text: Of whom, by what means, how much, and when the training activity [takes place] —
because of the absence of conceptual elaboration regarding all of these, the sage is always effortless. // 3 //
Of which trainable domain, by which abundant means,
what training activity, where, and at what place and time — // 4 //
In the setting forth, in its support, in its fruit, in its embrace,
in the covering over of that, and in the condition for its eradication — all [proceeds] without conceptualization. // 5 //

body.text: bhūmayo daśa niryāṇaṃ taddhetuḥ saṃbhṛtidvayam /
body.translated_text: The ten stages (<s>bhūmis</s>) are the setting forth; its cause is the twofold accumulation;

body.text: tatphalaṃ paramā bodhirbodheḥ sattvaḥ parigrahaḥ // 6 //
body.translated_text: its fruit is supreme awakening (<s>bodhi</s>); the embrace of awakening is [directed toward] beings. // 6 //

children.translated_text: The covering over of that [awakening] consists of the endless afflictions, secondary afflictions, and their residual impressions;
compassion (<s>karuṇā</s>) is the condition for its eradication at all times. // 7 //
These six topics are to be understood in order
as being like the great ocean, the sun, space, a treasure, clouds, and wind. // 8 //
The foremost vehicle is like the ocean because of its water of knowledge and gems of qualities;
the twofold accumulation is like the sun because of sustaining all beings. // 9 //
Awakening (<s>bodhi</s>) is like the space-element because of being vast, infinite, and without center;
the element of beings is like a treasure because of containing the qualities of a <s>Samyaksaṃbuddha</s>. // 10 //
Defilement is like a mass of clouds because of being adventitious, pervading, and unproduced [by the element];
compassion, aroused, is like wind because of being the condition for the dispersion of that [defilement]. // 11 //
Because the undertaking is for the benefit of others, because of seeing beings as equal to oneself,
and because the task is not yet fully accomplished, the activity never ceases. // 12 //

body.text: yadanutpādānirodhaprabhāvitaṃ buddhatvamityuktaṃ tatkathamihāsaṃskṛtādapravṛttilakṣaṇādbuddhatvādanābhogāpratipraśrabdhamā lokādavikalpaṃ buddhakārya pravartata iti / buddhamāhātmyadharmatāmārabhya vimatisaṃdehajātānāmacintyabuddhaviṣayādhimuktisaṃjananārtha tasya māhātmye ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: Since it has been stated that <s>Buddhahood</s> is characterized by non-arising and non-ceasing, how then does <s>Buddha</s>-activity proceed — effortless, unceasing, directed toward the world, and non-conceptual — from <s>Buddhahood</s> that is unconditioned and characterized by non-engagement? In order to generate faith in the inconceivable domain of the <s>Buddha</s> among those in whom doubt and hesitation have arisen regarding the greatness of the <s>Buddha</s>, a verse on that greatness:

children.translated_text: The <s>Tathāgata</s> is like <s>Śakra</s> (Indra), like a drum, like a cloud,
like <s>Brahmā</s>, like the sun, like a wish-fulfilling gem, // 13 //

body.text: asya khalu sūtrasthānīyasya ślokasya yathākramaṃ pariśiṣṭena granthena vistaravibhāganirdeśo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: like an echo, like space, and like the earth. The detailed exposition of this verse, which stands as the sūtra-text, is to be understood through the remaining portion of the treatise in proper order.

body.text: śakrapratibhāsatvāditi /
body.translated_text: "Like the reflection of <s>Śakra</s>" — thus:

children.translated_text: Just as if this ground were made of pure <s>vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli),
because of its clarity, <s>Devendra</s> (the Lord of Gods) with his hosts of <s>Apsaras</s> would be seen reflected there — // 14 //
the <s>Vaijayanta</s> palace and the other celestial beings,
their marvelous aerial mansions and those divine splendors. // 15 //
Then the men and women dwelling on the surface of the earth,
seeing that reflection, would make an aspiration such as this: // 16 //
"Before long, this very day, may we become lords of the thirty-three [gods],"
and they would undertake wholesome [deeds] for the attainment of that. // 17 //
Not knowing that "this is [merely] a reflection," those [beings] on earth,
passing away, would be reborn in the heavens through that wholesome action. // 18 //
That reflection, however, is utterly without conceptualization and without effort,
and yet it is present on earth with great purpose. // 19 //
Likewise, in the stainless [mirror of] faith and other [virtues], cultivated through faith and other qualities,
beings behold the <s>Sambuddha</s> (Fully Awakened One) as a reflection in their own minds. // 20 //
Endowed with the marks and minor signs, engaged in various deportments and activities,
walking, standing, sitting, and reclining, // 21 //

body.text: bhāṣamāṇaṃ śivaṃ dharma tūṣṇīṃbhūtaṃ samāhitam /
body.translated_text: teaching the peaceful <s>Dharma</s>, remaining in silence, in meditative absorption,

body.text: citrāṇi prātihāryāṇi darśayantaṃ mahādyutim // 22 //
body.translated_text: displaying various miraculous feats, [the Buddha] of great radiance. // 22 //

children.translated_text: And having seen him, they exert themselves toward <s>Buddhahood</s>, filled with aspiration;
and undertaking its cause, they attain the desired state. // 23 //
That reflection, however, is utterly without conceptualization and without effort,
and yet it is present in the worlds with great purpose. // 24 //
"This is a reflection of one's own mind" — ordinary beings do not
know this; yet for them, the seeing of that image is not fruitless. // 25 //
For, relying on that very seeing, gradually established in this path,
they behold the true <s>Dharmakāya</s>, impartial, with the eye of knowledge. // 26 //
If the earth were vast, everywhere free from uneven ground, with interstices cleansed of impurity,
clear as <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, bright, with qualities of pure gems, a glorious even surface —
because of its purity, the reflection of <s>Surapati</s> (Lord of Gods), the great abode of <s>Indra</s> and the <s>Maruts</s>,
would arise in succession, and with the loss of the earth's qualities, it would set again. // 27 //
For the sake of that [vision], through observances of fasting, vows, and restraints, devoted to generosity and other [perfections],
men and women with resolute minds would cast flowers and the like.
In the mind that is clear as <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, upon attaining the reflection of the Lord of Sages,
the children of the <s>Jinas</s> (Victorious Ones), with joyful minds, produce various [spiritual attainments] — just so. // 28 //
Just as on a pure ground of <s>vaiḍūrya</s> there arises the reflected image of <s>Surendra</s> (Lord of Gods),
so too on the pure ground of the minds of beings arises the reflected image of <s>Munīndra</s> (Lord of Sages). // 29 //

body.text: bimbodayavyayamanāvilatāvilasvacittapravartanavaṃśājjagati pravṛttam /
body.translated_text: The arising and passing of the image — this proceeds in the world from the lineage of the engagement of one's own mind, whether clear or unclear;

body.text: lokeṣu yadvadavabhāsamupaiti bimbaṃ tadvanna tatsaditi nāsaditi prapaśyet // 30 //
body.translated_text: just as an image appears in the worlds, one should see it as neither truly existent nor truly non-existent. // 30 //

body.text: devadundubhivaditi /
body.translated_text: "Like the divine drum" — thus:

children.translated_text: Just as in heaven, for the gods, by the power of their former wholesome [deeds],
a [drum], free from effort, place, bodily form, and conceptualization, // 31 //
with the sounds of "impermanent," "suffering," "non-self," and "peace,"
the divine drum (<s>devadundubhi</s>) repeatedly rouses all the gods who are heedless. // 32 //
Likewise, pervading the entire world without remainder with the sound of the <s>Buddha</s>,
the All-pervading One teaches the <s>Dharma</s> to those with [spiritual] capacity, even though devoid of effort and the like. // 33 //
Just as in heaven the sound of the divine drum arises from the gods' own deeds,
so too the teaching of the <s>Dharma</s> by the Sage arises in the world from [beings'] own deeds.
That sound, devoid of effort, place, body, and mind, brings peace —

children.text: yadvat tadvadṛte catuṣṭayamayaṃ dharmaḥ sa śāntyāvahaḥ // 34 //
children.translated_text: just so, that <s>Dharma</s>, devoid of the fourfold [effort, place, body, mind], brings peace. // 34 //
Just as in the battle against the afflictions of the <s>Asura</s> hosts, in the sport of conquering the <s>Asura</s> army, the sound of the drum,
arising from a cause, bestows fearlessness in the city of the gods,
so too in the world, [the teaching] that quells and pacifies the torment of afflictions and suffering of beings,
arising from causes such as <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation), the formless [attainments], and others, has been proclaimed as the supreme path. // 35 //

body.text: kasmādiha dharmadundubhirevādhikṛtā na tadanye divyāstūryaprakārāḥ / te 'pi hi divaukasāṃ pūrvakṛtakuśalakarmavaśādaghaṭṭitā eva divyaśravaṇamanoharaśabdamanuruvanti /
body.translated_text: Why is the <s>Dharma</s>-drum specifically chosen here and not the other types of divine musical instruments? For those too, by the force of the wholesome deeds previously performed by the celestial beings, without being struck, resound with sounds pleasing to divine hearing.

body.text: taistathāgataghoṣasya catuḥprakāraguṇavaidharmyāt / tatpunaḥ katamat / tadyathā prādeśikatvamahitatvamasukhatvamanairyāṇikatvamiti / dharmadundubhyāḥ punaraprādeśikatvamaśeṣapramattadevagaṇasaṃcodanatayā ca tatkālānatikramaṇatayā ca paridīpitam / hitatvamasurādiparacakropadravabhayaparitrāṇatayā cāpramādasaṃniyojanatayā ca / sukhatvamasatkāmaratisukhavivecanatayā ca dharmārāmaratisukhopasaṃharaṇatayā ca / nairyāṇikatvamanityaduḥkhaśūnyānātmaśabdoccāraṇatayā ca sarvopadravopāyāsopaśāntikaraṇatayā ca paridīüpitam / ebhiḥ samāsataścaturbhirākārairdharmadundubhisādharmyeṇa buddhasvaramaṇḍalaṃ viśiṣyata iti / buddhasvaramaṇḍalaviśeṣaṇaślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: by the dissimilarity from the four kinds of qualities of the voice of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. What then are these? They are: being local, being unhelpful, being unpleasant, and not leading to liberation. The non-local nature of the <s>Dharma</s>-drum, on the other hand, is illuminated by its arousing all the heedless hosts of gods without remainder and by not transgressing the [appropriate] time. Its helpfulness [is illuminated] by its protection from fear of calamity from hostile forces such as <s>Asuras</s>, and by its engagement in heedfulness. Its pleasantness [is illuminated] by its distinguishing from the pleasure of delight in base sense-desires, and by its bringing about the pleasure of delight in the <s>Dharma</s>-garden. Its leading to liberation is illuminated by its uttering the words 'impermanent,' 'suffering,' 'empty,' and 'non-self,' and by its pacification of all calamity and distress. By these four aspects in brief, the sphere of the <s>Buddha</s>'s voice is distinguished through similarity with the <s>Dharma</s>-drum. The verse characterizing the sphere of the <s>Buddha</s>'s voice:

children.translated_text: Being universal, beneficial, pleasant, and endowed with the three miracles (<s>prātihārya</s>),
the voice of the <s>Muni</s> (Sage) is therefore distinguished from divine instruments. // 36 //

body.text: eṣāṃ khalu caturṇāmākārāṇāṃ yathāsaṃkhyameva caturbhiḥ ślokaḥ samāsanirdeśo veditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The summary exposition of these four aspects, in order, by four verses, should be understood:

children.text: śabdā mahānto divi dundubhīnāṃ kṣitisthiteṣu śravaṇaṃ na yānti /
children.translated_text: The great sounds of the celestial drums do not reach the hearing of those dwelling on the earth;

children.text: saṃsārapātālagateṣu loke saṃbuddhatūryasya tu yāti śabdaḥ // 37 //
children.translated_text: but the sound of the instrument of the perfectly enlightened one reaches those in the world who have fallen to the depths of <s>saṃsāra</s>. // 37 //
Many millions of celestial instruments of the gods resound for the increase of the blazing of desire;
but the one voice of the compassionate ones operates to pacify the causes of the fire of suffering. // 38 //

body.text: śubhā manojñā divi tūryanisvanā bhavanti cittoddhativṛddhihetavaḥ /
body.translated_text: The auspicious and pleasant sounds of celestial instruments are causes for the increase of mental agitation;

body.text: tathāgatānāṃ tu rutaṃ mahātmanāṃ samādhicittārpaṇabhāvavācakam // 39 //
body.translated_text: but the utterance of the great-souled <s>Tathāgatas</s> expresses the state of mental absorption in <s>samādhi</s>. // 39 //

children.translated_text: In brief, what is the cause of happiness in heaven and on earth, in infinite world-realms,
the illumination pervading all worlds without remainder—that too has been declared through the great proclamation. // 40 //

body.text: kāyavikurvitena daśadigaśeṣalokadhātuspharaṇamṛddhiprātihāryamiti sūcitam / cetaḥparyāyajñānena tatparyāpannaṃ sarvasattvacittacaritagahanāvabhāsanamādeśanāprātihāryam / vāgghoṣodāharaṇena nairyāṇikīṃ pratipadamārabhya tadavavādānuśāsanamanuśāsti prātihāryam / ityevamavyāhatagaterākāśadhātuvadaparicchinnavartino 'pi buddhasvaramaṇḍalasya yanna sarvatra sarvaghoṣopalabdhiḥ prajāyate na tatra buddhasvaramaṇḍalasyāparādha iti / pratyāyanārthamatatprahitānāmātmāparādhe ślokaḥ /
body.translated_text: By bodily transformation, the miracle of magical power (<s>ṛddhi-prātihārya</s>) pervading all world-realms in the ten directions without remainder is indicated. By the knowledge of reading others' minds (<s>cetaḥparyāya-jñāna</s>), the miracle of telepathic instruction (<s>ādeśanā-prātihārya</s>) that illuminates the depths of the mental conduct of all beings comprised therein [is indicated]. By the utterance of vocal proclamation, the miracle of instruction (<s>anuśāsanī-prātihārya</s>) that teaches guidance and counsel beginning with the path leading to liberation [is indicated]. Thus, even though the sphere of the <s>Buddha</s>'s voice operates without obstruction like the space-element and without limitation, the fact that the perception of all sounds does not arise everywhere is not a fault of the sphere of the <s>Buddha</s>'s voice. The verse [illustrating] the fault of those themselves not directed toward it, for the purpose of convincing [them]:

children.translated_text: Just as one whose hearing is impaired does not experience subtle sounds,
nor do they come entirely within the range of hearing even of one with the divine ear,
so too the <s>Dharma</s>, being subtle, being the domain of the most refined knowledge,
enters the range of hearing only of some—those whose minds are undistorted. // 41 //

body.text: meghavaditi /
body.translated_text: Like a cloud:

children.translated_text: Just as in the rainy season a cloud rains down upon the earth
a mass of water effortlessly, as the cause of the abundance of crops, // 42 //

body.text: karuṇāmbudatastadvat saddharmasalilaṃ jinaḥ /
body.translated_text: so too, from the cloud of compassion, the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror) [rains down] the water of the true <s>Dharma</s>

body.text: jagatkuśalasasyeṣu nirvikalpaṃ pravarṣati // 43 //
body.translated_text: without conceptual discrimination upon the wholesome crops of the world. // 43 //

children.text: loke yathā kuśalakarmapathapravṛtte varṣanti vāyujanitaṃ salilaṃ payodāḥ /
children.translated_text: Just as in the world, when wholesome courses of action prevail, rain-clouds pour down water generated by wind,
so too the <s>Buddha</s>-cloud rains down the rain of the true <s>Dharma</s> through the wind of compassion for the increase of the world's wholesome [qualities]. // 44 //
Bathed in knowledge and compassion for [beings in] existences, abiding in the sky-expanse free from attachment to the perishable and imperishable,
containing the stainless water of <s>samādhi</s> and <s>dhāraṇī</s>, the cloud of the Lord of Sages is the cause of wholesome crops. // 45 //

body.text: bhājanavimātratāyām /
body.translated_text: Regarding the diversity of vessels:

children.text: śītaṃ svādu prasannaṃ mṛdu laghu ca payastatpayodayādvimuktaṃ
children.translated_text: Cool, sweet, clear, soft, and light—such water released from a rain-cloud,
assumes very many different tastes on the earth through contact with saline and other types of ground;
so too, the rain of the noble eightfold water released from the womb of the vast cloud of compassion
assumes many different tastes among beings due to the differences in their mind-streams and dispositions. // 46 //

body.text: nirapekṣapravṛttau /
body.translated_text: Regarding impartial activity:

children.translated_text: Those devoted to the highest vehicle, those of the middle, and those who are hostile—
these three groups are comparable to humans, <s>cātaka</s> birds, and hungry ghosts (<s>pretas</s>). // 47 //

body.text:
grīṣmānte 'mbudhareṣvasatsu manujā vyomnyapracārāḥ khagā
varṣāsvapyativarṣaṇaprapatanātpretāḥ kṣiptau duḥkhitāḥ /
body.translated_text: At the end of summer, when there are no rain-clouds, humans [suffer]; birds cannot range through the sky; in the rainy season too, from the fall of excessive rain, hungry ghosts are afflicted and pained.
