body.text: aprādurbhavanodaye 'pi karuṇāmeghābhradharmāmbhaso
body.translated_text: Even at the non-arising of the rain-water of the <s>Dharma</s> from the cloud-mass of compassion,

body.text: dharmākāṅkṣiṇi dharmatāpratihate loke ca saivopamā // 48 //
body.translated_text: and in a world that yearns for the <s>Dharma</s> yet is obstructed by <s>dharmatā</s>—this same simile applies. // 48 //

children.translated_text: With its coarse falling drops, thunderbolts, and falls of <s>vajra</s> and fire,
the rain-cloud takes no heed of subtle creatures or those dwelling in mountain regions;
likewise, through methods of subtle and coarse reasoning and skillful means, the cloud of wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>) and compassion (<s>kṛpā</s>)
takes no heed whatsoever of the affliction-bound views and latent tendencies (<s>anuśaya</s>). // 49 //

body.text: duḥkhāgnipraśamane /
body.translated_text: Regarding the pacification of the fire of suffering:

children.translated_text: <s>Saṃsāra</s>, with its ceaseless birth and death, [has] fivefold transmigration therein;

children.text: mārgaḥ pañcavidhe ca vartmani sukhaṃ noccārasaugandhyavat /
children.translated_text: the path in these five courses is without happiness, like excrement without fragrance;
that suffering is perpetual, arising from contact with fire, weapons, cold, caustic substances, and the like—

children.text: tacchāntyai ca sṛjan kṛpājaladharaḥ saddharmavarṣaṃ mahat // 50 //
children.translated_text: and for its pacification, the cloud of compassion produces the great rain of the true <s>Dharma</s>. // 50 //
Understanding that among the gods there is the suffering of falling, and among humans the suffering of seeking,
the wise do not desire even the highest sovereignty among gods and humans;
and through the wisdom that comes from faith in and inference from the teaching of the <s>Tathāgata</s>, [they see:]

children.text: duḥkhaṃ heturayaṃ nirodha iti ca jñānena saṃprekṣaṇāt // 51 //
children.translated_text: 'this is suffering, this is the cause, this is cessation'—through seeing with knowledge. // 51 //

children.text: vyādhirjñeyo vyādhihetuḥ praheyaḥ svāsthyaṃ prāpyaṃ bheṣajaṃ sevyamevam /
children.translated_text: The disease is to be known, the cause of disease is to be abandoned, health is to be attained, the medicine is to be applied—thus,

children.text: duḥkhaṃ hetustannirodho 'tha mārgo jñeyaṃ heyaḥ sparśitavyo niṣevyaḥ // 52 //
children.translated_text: suffering, its cause, its cessation, and the path are to be known, abandoned, realized, and cultivated. // 52 //

body.text: mahābrahmavaditi /
body.translated_text: Like great <s>Brahmā</s>:

children.translated_text: In every divine abode, without moving from the <s>Brahmā</s> station,
<s>Brahmā</s> displays a reflection of himself effortlessly. // 53 //
Likewise, the <s>Muni</s>, effortlessly, through emanations (<s>nirmāṇa</s>) in all realms,
without moving from the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, comes into the sight of those capable of being trained. // 54 //

children.text: yadvad brahmā vimānānna calati satataṃ kāmadhātupraviṣṭaṃ
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Brahmā</s>, without ever moving from his palace, having entered the desire-realm (<s>Kāmadhātu</s>),

children.text: devāḥ paśyanti cainaṃ viṣayaratiharaṃ darśanaṃ tacca teṣām /
children.translated_text: the gods behold him, and that vision of him removes their delight in sense-objects;

children.text: tadvat saddharmakāyānna calati sugataḥ sarvalokeṣu cainaṃ
children.translated_text: so too the <s>Sugata</s>, without moving from the true <s>Dharmakāya</s>, in all worlds—

children.text: bhavyāḥ paśyanti śaśvatsakalamalaharaṃ darśanaṃ tacca teṣām // 55 //
children.translated_text: those capable of being trained behold him always, and that vision of him removes all their defilements. // 55 //
Through the power of his own former aspirational vows and through the meritorious influence of the hosts of wind-gods (<s>Marudgaṇa</s>),

children.text: brahmā yathā bhāsamupaityayatnān nirmāṇakāyena tathā svayaṃbhūḥ // 56 //
children.translated_text: just as <s>Brahmā</s> appears effortlessly, so too does the Self-born One (<s>Svayaṃbhū</s>) through the emanation body (<s>Nirmāṇakāya</s>). // 56 //

body.text: anābhāsagamane /
body.translated_text: Regarding the passing into non-appearance:

children.translated_text: Descent [from heaven], entering the womb, birth, entering the father's house,
sport and play, wandering in the forest, vanquishing <s>Māra</s>,
attainment of great awakening (<s>mahābodhi</s>), displaying the path to the city of peace—
having displayed [all this], the <s>Muni</s> does not come within the range of vision of the unfortunate. // 57 //

body.text: sūryavaditi /
body.translated_text: Like the sun:

body.text: sūrye yathā tapati padmagaṇaprabuddhirekatra kālasamaye kumudaprasuptiḥ /
body.translated_text: Just as when the sun shines, at one and the same time there is the opening of clusters of lotuses and the closing of night-lilies (<s>kumuda</s>);
[continued]

body.text: buddhiprasuptiguṇadoṣavidhāvakalpaḥ sūryo 'mbujeṣvatha ca tadvadihāryasūryaḥ // 58 //
body.translated_text: and the sun makes no distinction between the quality and defect in awakening and closing among water-born [flowers]—so too here does the noble sun [of the <s>Buddha</s> act]. // 58 //

body.text: dvividhaḥ sattvadhāturavineyo vineyaśca / tatra yo vineyastamadhikṛtya padmopamatā svacchajalabhājanopamatā ca /
body.translated_text: The realm of beings is twofold: those not yet trainable and those trainable. With reference to those who are trainable, the similes of the lotus and the vessel of clear water [are given].

children.translated_text: Just as the sun, without conceptual discrimination, with its own rays
awakens some lotuses and ripens others, // 59 //
so too, with the rays of the true <s>Dharma</s>, the sun of the <s>Tathāgata</s>
operates without conceptual discrimination among the lotus-like persons to be trained. // 60 //
Having risen in the sky of the seat of awakening (<s>Bodhimaṇḍa</s>) through the two bodies of <s>Dharma</s> and form,
the omniscient sun-maker pervades the world with the rays of knowledge. // 61 //
Because everywhere in the pure water-reservoir of those to be trained,
the reflections of the immeasurable <s>Sugata</s>-sun arise simultaneously. // 62 //

body.text: evamavikalpatve 'pi sati buddhānāṃ trividhe sattvarāśau darśanādeśanāpravṛttikramamadhikṛtya śailopamatā /
body.translated_text: Thus, even though the <s>Buddhas</s> are without conceptual discrimination, with reference to the sequence of appearing, teaching, and acting among the three groups of beings, the simile of the mountain [is given]:

body.text:
sadā sarvatra visṛte dharmadhātunabhastale /
buddhasūrye vineyādritannipāto yathārhataḥ // 63 ///
body.translated_text: Always and everywhere in the extended sky-expanse of the <s>Dharmadhātu</s>, the <s>Buddha</s>-sun's rays fall upon the mountains of those to be trained, each according to their worthiness. // 63 //
[continued]

children.text: udita iha samantāllokamābhāsya yadvat pratatadaśaśatāṃśuḥ saptasaptiḥ krameṇa /
children.translated_text: Just as the seven-horsed [sun], having risen here and illuminated the world on all sides with its extended thousand rays, gradually

children.text: pratapati varamadhyanyūnaśaileṣu tadvat pratipati jinasūryaḥ sattvarāśau krameṇa // 64 //
children.translated_text: shines upon the high, middle, and low mountains—so too does the <s>Jina</s> (Conqueror)-sun [shine] gradually upon the groups of beings. // 64 //

body.text: prabhāmaṇḍalaviśeṣaṇe /
body.translated_text: Regarding the distinctive quality of the halo of light:

children.translated_text: Pervading the sky-expanse of all fields is not found in the [ordinary] sun,
nor does it illuminate the objects of knowledge within the dense darkness of ignorance;
but with streams of rays of various colors arising from each and every hair-pore,
the compassionate ones shine in the world, illuminating the objects of knowledge. // 65 //
At the time of the <s>Buddhas</s>' entry into the city, people deprived of sight
see [the truth], and from that vision they attain the removal of the net of misfortune;
and those blinded by delusion, caught within the ocean of existence, enveloped in the darkness of [wrong] views,
having their minds illuminated by the radiance of the <s>Buddha</s>-sun, behold the unseen state. // 66 //

body.text: cintāmaṇivaditi /
body.translated_text: Like a wish-fulfilling gem (<s>cintāmaṇi</s>):

children.translated_text: The simultaneous fulfillment of all the wishes of those within its range—
this the wish-fulfilling gem accomplishes, though itself without conceptual discrimination, variously. // 67 //
Likewise, having approached the <s>Buddha</s>-wish-fulfilling-gem, those with various dispositions

children.text: śṛṇvanti dharmatāṃ citrāṃ na kalpayati tāṃśca saḥ // 68 //
children.translated_text: hear the manifold <s>dharmatā</s>, yet he does not conceptually construct those [teachings]. // 68 //

body.text: yathāvikalpaṃ maṇiratnamīpsitaṃ dhanaṃ parebhyo visṛjatyayatnataḥ /
body.translated_text: Just as the jewel-gem dispenses desired wealth to others effortlessly, without conceptual discrimination,
[continued]

body.text: tathā muniryatnamṛte yathārhataḥ parārthamātiṣṭhati nityamā bhavāt // 69 //
body.translated_text: so too the <s>Muni</s>, without effort, accomplishes the benefit of others according to their worthiness, always until the end of existence. // 69 //

body.text: durlabhaprāptabhāvāstathāgatā iti /
body.translated_text: <s>Tathāgatas</s> are difficult to encounter:

children.translated_text: Just as obtaining a precious gem in this world is extremely rare,
since it has gone to the ocean depths and abides in the netherworld, [yet] they long for it—
so it should be known as not easily obtained; likewise, extremely rare in the world,
is the sight of the <s>Tathāgata</s> for a mind seized by manifold afflictions. // 70 //

body.text: pratiśrutkāśabdavaditi /
body.translated_text: Like an echo:

children.translated_text: Just as an echo arises from the cognition of another,
is without conceptual discrimination, without deliberate effort, neither internal nor external, // 71 //
so too the utterance of the <s>Tathāgata</s> arises from the cognition of others,
is without conceptual discrimination, without deliberate effort, neither internal nor external. // 72 //
Like space:
Having nothing, without appearance, without support, without refuge,
beyond the range of sight, formless, and without exemplification— // 73 //

children.text: yathā nimnonnataṃ vyomni dṛśyate na ca tattathā /
children.translated_text: just as high and low are seen in space, yet it is not truly so,

children.text: buddheṣvapi tathā sarva dṛśyate na ca tattathā // 74 //
children.translated_text: so too in the <s>Buddhas</s> everything is seen, yet it is not truly so. // 74 //

body.text: pṛthivīvaditi /
body.translated_text: Like the earth:

children.translated_text: Just as all trees, relying on the non-discriminating earth,
attain growth, sprouting, and abundance, // 75 //
so too, relying on the non-discriminating earth of the perfectly awakened ones,
the roots of the world's wholesome [qualities] completely attain growth. // 76 //

body.text: udāharaṇānāṃ piṇḍārthaḥ /
body.translated_text: The summary meaning of the illustrations:

children.translated_text: No one has been seen performing any action without effort; therefore,
for the removal of doubt among those to be trained, the illustration has been given ninefold. // 77 //
The purpose of that [teaching] has been illuminated by the very name of that <s>sūtra</s>,
in which these nine similes have been explained in detail. // 78 //
Adorned with the light of knowledge born of hearing this and other [teachings],
the wise ones swiftly enter the entire domain of the <s>Buddha</s>. // 79 //
Thus, the illustrations beginning with the reflections of <s>Śakra</s> in <s>Vaiḍūrya</s> (lapis lazuli), and so on,
have been given ninefold therein; their summary meaning is to be grasped. // 80 //
Appearing, teaching, pervading, transforming, the outflow of knowledge,
the secrets of mind, speech, and body, and the attainment of those whose nature is compassion. // 81 //
Pacified of all effort and movement, non-conceptual,
their wisdoms [arise] like the appearance of <s>Śakra</s>'s reflection in pure <s>vaiḍūrya</s> [gem]. // 82 //
The thesis is the pacification of effort; the reason is the non-conceptuality of wisdom;
the example is <s>Śakra</s>'s reflection and so forth, for the well-established accomplishment of the intended meaning. // 83 //
And the intended meaning here is ninefold, beginning with manifestation and so forth;
it proceeds effortlessly from the Teacher's birth, disappearance, and passing. // 84 //

body.text: etamevārthamadhikṛtyodāharaṇasaṃgrahe catvāraḥ ślokāḥ /
body.translated_text: With reference to this very meaning, in the summary of illustrations there are four verses:

children.translated_text: He who, like <s>Śakra</s>, like a drum, like a cloud, like <s>Brahmā</s>, like the sun, like a wish-fulfilling gem, like an echo, like space, and like the earth,
accomplishes the benefit of others without effort from [the time of] existence—he is the knower of <s>yoga</s>. // 85 //
Manifesting the sight of reflections like <s>Indra</s>'s jewel, his mighty sound like a divine drum,
the mighty one, a cloud-mass of great knowledge and compassion, pervades the infinite world from the summit of existence. // 86 //
Unfallen from the undefiled state like <s>Brahmā</s>, he manifests in multiple ways through emanations;
always like the solar disc, his radiance streaming forth from knowledge, his mind a pure wish-fulfilling jewel. // 87 //
The speech of the <s>Jinas</s> is like an echo, uttered without syllables;
their body, like space, is pervading, formless, and permanent;
like the earth, the <s>Buddha</s>-stage is here everywhere
the ground for all the healing herbs of pure qualities for the world. // 88 //

body.text: kathaṃ punaranenodāharaṇanirdeśena satatamanutpannā aniruddhāśca buddhā bhagavanta utpadyamānā nirudhyamānāśca saṃdṛśyante sarvajagati caiṣāmanābhogena buddhakāryāpratipraśrabdhieriti paridīpitam /
body.translated_text: How, then, is it illuminated by this exposition of illustrations that the <s>Buddhas</s> and <s>Bhagavāns</s>, though perpetually unarisen and unceased, are seen arising and ceasing throughout the world, and that their <s>Buddha</s>-activity proceeds effortlessly without relaxation?

children.translated_text: The auspicious [quality] in the mind, like <s>vaiḍūrya</s>, is the cause of seeing the <s>Buddha</s>;
the purification of that is the growth of the indestructible faith-faculty. // 89 //

body.text: śubhodayavyayāddhuddhaṃpratibimbodayavyayaḥ /
body.translated_text: From the arising and passing of the auspicious [quality], there is arising and passing of the <s>Buddha</s>-reflection;

body.text: munirnodeti na vyeti śakravaddharmakāyataḥ // 90 //
body.translated_text: the <s>Muni</s> neither arises nor passes away, like <s>Śakra</s>, from the standpoint of the <s>Dharmakāya</s>. // 90 //

children.translated_text: Activity proceeds effortlessly thus—manifestation and the rest—
from the <s>Dharmakāya</s>, because of non-arising and non-cessation, from the abode of existence. // 91 //
This is the summary meaning of these similes; the order, moreover,
is stated such that the latter removes the dissimilarity of the former. // 92 //

children.text: buddhatvaṃ pratibimbābhaṃ tadvanna ca na ghoṣavat /
children.translated_text: <s>Buddhahood</s> is like a reflection, yet unlike it, because it is not [merely] like a sound;
it is like a divine drum, yet unlike it, because it is not in every way the accomplisher of purpose. // 93 //
It is like a great cloud, yet unlike it, because it is not [merely] like a seed bearing fruit;
it is like great <s>Brahmā</s>, yet unlike him, because it does not ultimately ripen [only some]. // 94 //
It is like the solar disc, yet unlike it, because it does not ultimately remove darkness [only];
it is like a wish-fulfilling gem, yet unlike it, because its arising is not difficult to obtain. // 95 //
It is like an echo, yet unlike it, because it is not produced by conditions;

children.text: ākāśasadṛśaṃ tadvanna ca śuklāspadaṃ ca tat // 96 //
children.translated_text: it is like space, yet unlike it, because it is also the ground of pure [qualities]. // 96 //
It is like the disc of the earth, because of being the support and foundation
for the entire wealth of wholesome qualities of the world, both mundane and supramundane. // 97 //

body.text: buddhānāṃ bodhimāgamya lokottarapathodayāt /
body.translated_text: Having attained the awakening of the <s>Buddhas</s>, through the arising of the supramundane path,

body.text: śuklakarmapathadhyānāpramāṇārūpyasaṃbhava iti // 98 //
body.translated_text: arises the pure course of action, <s>dhyāna</s>, the immeasurables, and the formless [attainments]. // 98 //

body.text: iti ratnagotravibhāge mahāyānottaratantraśāstre tathāgatakṛtyakriyādhikāraścaturthaḥ paricchedaḥ ślokārthasaṃgrahavyākhyānataḥ samāptaḥ // 4 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fourth chapter on the enlightened activity of the <s>Tathāgata</s> in the <s>Ratnagotravibhāga Mahāyānottaratantraśāstra</s>, in the form of a commentary summarizing the meaning of the verses. // 4 //

body.text: 5. paṃcamaḥ paricchedaḥ
body.translated_text: 5. Fifth Chapter

body.text: ataḥ parameṣveva yathāparikīrtiteṣu sthāneṣvadhimuktānāmadhimuktyanuśaṃse ṣaṭ ślokāḥ
body.translated_text: Hereafter, regarding the benefits of faith for those who have conviction in the topics as proclaimed, there are six verses:

children.translated_text: <s>Buddhadhātu</s> (buddha-element), <s>Buddhabodhi</s> (buddha-awakening), <s>Buddhadharma</s> (buddha-qualities), <s>Buddhakṛtya</s> (buddha-activity)—
this is the domain of the guides, inconceivable even by pure beings. // 1 //
The wise one who here has the intelligence of faith in the domain of the <s>Jina</s>
becomes a vessel for the multitude of qualities, surpassing the merit-production of all beings through the application of aspiration for inconceivable qualities. // 2 //
One who, aspiring for awakening, would give golden fields adorned with jewels,
equal in number to the atoms of buddha-fields, to the lords of <s>Dharma</s> every day—
and another who would hear even a single word of this, and having heard, would have faith—
that one would obtain far more merit than the former auspicious [act] consisting of generosity. // 3 //
A wise one who, aspiring for supreme awakening, would effortlessly guard
pure moral conduct through body, speech, and mind for many <s>kalpas</s>—
and another who would hear even a single word of this, and having heard, would have faith—
that one would obtain far more merit than the former auspicious [act] consisting of moral conduct. // 4 //
One who here would practice <s>dhyāna</s> (meditation) that extinguishes the fires of affliction in the three worlds,
having reached the far shore of the divine <s>Brahmavihāras</s>, unfallen from the means to awakening—
and another who would hear even a single word of this, and having heard, would have faith—
that one would obtain far more merit than the former auspicious [act] consisting of meditation. // 5 //

body.text: dānaṃ bhogānāvahatyevaḥ yasmācchīlaṃ svargaṃ bhāvanā kleśahānim /
body.translated_text: Since generosity brings [only] enjoyments, moral conduct [brings] heaven, and cultivation [brings] the removal of afflictions,

body.text: prajñā kleśajñeyasarvaprahāṇaṃ sātaḥ śreṣṭhā heturasyāḥ śravo 'yam // 6 //
body.translated_text: <s>prajñā</s> (wisdom) [brings] the complete abandonment of all affliction and knowable [obscurations]—therefore wisdom is supreme; and hearing is its root, therefore hearing is the highest. // 6 //

body.text: eṣā ślokānāṃ piṇḍārtho navabhiḥ ślokairveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The condensed meaning of these verses is to be understood by nine verses:

children.translated_text: Regarding the basis, the transformation thereof, its qualities, and the accomplishment of purpose—
in this fourfold domain of the <s>Jina</s>'s knowledge as proclaimed: // 7 //
Through faith in its existence, attainability, and possession of qualities,
the wise one quickly arrives at the capacity for attaining the state of the <s>Tathāgata</s>. // 8 //

children.text: astyasau viṣayo 'cintyaḥ śakyaḥ prāptuṃ sa mādṛśaiḥ /
children.translated_text: 'That inconceivable domain exists; it can be attained by ones like me;
and once attained, it possesses such qualities'—through this faith and conviction, // 9 //
one becomes a vessel for qualities such as aspiration (<s>chanda</s>), vigor (<s>vīrya</s>), mindfulness (<s>smṛti</s>), meditation (<s>dhyāna</s>), and wisdom (<s>prajñā</s>);
the mind of awakening (<s>bodhicitta</s>) becomes constantly present for this one. // 10 //
Through the constant presence of that mind, the child of the <s>Jina</s> becomes irreversible
and arrives at the complete purification of merit and <s>pāramitā</s> (perfections). // 11 //
Merit consists of the five <s>pāramitās</s>, [classified] in three ways, through non-conceptualization thereof;
its fulfillment and purification [come] through the abandonment of their adversaries. // 12 //

children.text: dānaṃ dānamayaṃ puṇyaṃ śīlaṃ śīlamayaṃ smṛtam /
children.translated_text: Generosity is merit consisting of giving; moral conduct is regarded as merit consisting of moral conduct;

children.text: dve bhāvanāmayaṃ kṣāntidhyāne vīryaṃ tu sarvagam // 13 //
children.translated_text: patience and meditation are merit consisting of cultivation; vigor, however, pervades all. // 13 //

body.text: trimaṇḍalavikalpo yastajjñeyāvaraṇaṃ matam /
body.translated_text: The conceptualization of the triple sphere—that is regarded as the obscuration of the knowable (<s>jñeyāvaraṇa</s>);

body.text: mātsaryādivipakṣo yastat kleśāvaraṇaṃ matam // 14 //
body.translated_text: the adversary consisting of miserliness and so forth—that is regarded as the obscuration of affliction (<s>kleśāvaraṇa</s>). // 14 //

children.translated_text: And the cause of abandoning these is none other than wisdom; therefore

children.text: śreṣṭhā prajñā śrutaṃ cāsya mūlaṃ tasmācchrutaṃ param // 15 //
children.translated_text: wisdom is supreme, and hearing is its root—therefore hearing is the highest. // 15 //
Thus this has been set forth relying on authoritative scripture and reasoning, solely for self-purification,

children.text: dhiyādhimuktyā kuśalopasaṃpadā samanvitā ye tadanugrahāya ca // 16 //
children.translated_text: and for the benefit of those endowed with the attainment of virtue through wisdom and faith. // 16 //
Just as those with eyes see depending on a lamp, lightning, a gem, the moon, and the sun,
so this has been set forth depending on the <s>Muni</s>, the illuminator of the <s>Dharma</s> of great meaning and eloquence. // 17 //
That speech which is connected with meaningful words of <s>Dharma</s> and which serves to remove the defilements of the three realms,
and which demonstrates the benefits of peace—that is declared to be the speech of the sages; otherwise it is the contrary. // 18 //

body.text: yatsyādavikṣiptamanobhiruktaṃ śāstāramekaṃ jinamuddiśadbhiḥ /
body.translated_text: That which is spoken by those of undistracted minds, directing [their attention] to the Teacher, the <s>Jina</s> alone,

body.text: mokṣāptisaṃbhārapathānukūlaṃ mūrdhnā tadapyārṣamiva pratīcchet // 19 //
body.translated_text: and which is conducive to the path of the provisions for attaining liberation—one should accept that too with the crown of the head, as [if it were] the speech of the sages. // 19 //

children.translated_text: Since there is no one anywhere in the world more learned than the <s>Jina</s>,

children.text: sarvajñaḥ sakalaṃ sa veda vidhivattattvaṃ paraṃ nāparaḥ /
children.translated_text: the omniscient one alone knows the supreme truth completely and properly, and no other—

children.text: tasmādyatsvayameva nītamṛṣiṇā sūtraṃ vicālyaṃ na tat
children.translated_text: therefore that <s>sūtra</s> which the sage himself has set forth should not be disturbed,
for that would be damaging the true <s>Dharma</s>, and would destroy the <s>Muni</s>'s method. // 20 //

children.text: āryāṃścāpavadanti tannigaditaṃ dharmaṃ ca garhanti yat
children.translated_text: Those who revile the noble ones and disparage the <s>Dharma</s> proclaimed by them—
all that is an affliction of the deluded, caused by clinging to views;
therefore one should not place one's mind in that which is defiled by the stain of clinging to views—
a clean cloth takes dye, not one smeared with oil and mud. // 21 //
Due to intellectual dullness and lack of the purity of faith, from reliance on wrong conceit,
from being covered by self-identification with misfortune regarding the true <s>Dharma</s>, from grasping the interpretable meaning as the definitive,
from the dominion of views characterized by the greed of attachment, from serving those who are hostile to <s>Dharma</s>—
those of inferior disposition reject the <s>Dharmas</s> of the noble <s>Dharma</s>-bearers and <s>Arhats</s>. // 22 //
One should not fear fire, fierce poison, murder, or even thunderbolts
as much as the wise should fear the loss of the profound <s>Dharma</s>;
fire, serpents, enemies, and thunderbolts may cause separation from life,
but they do not cause one to go to the extremely fearful destiny of the <s>Avīci</s> [hell]. // 23 //

body.text: yo 'bhīkṣṇaṃ pratisevya pāpasuhṛdaḥ syādvuddhaduṣṭāśayo
body.translated_text: One who, by constantly associating with evil companions, has a mind corrupted toward the <s>Buddha</s>,

children.translated_text: a person who has committed the murder of mother, father, and <s>Arhat</s>, and is the foremost splitter of the <s>Saṅgha</s>—
even for that one there may be liberation before long through reflection on the meaning of the <s>Dharma</s>;

children.text: dharme yasya tu mānasaṃ pratihataṃ tasmai vimuktiḥ kutaḥ // 24 //
children.translated_text: but one whose mind is set against the <s>Dharma</s>—whence liberation for that one? // 24 //

children.text: ratnāni vyavadānadhātumamalāṃ bodhiṃ guṇān karma ca
children.translated_text: By properly explaining the seven meaningful topics—the jewels, the element of purification, stainless awakening, qualities, and activity—
whatever merit I have obtained,
may this humanity see the <s>Ṛṣi</s> of infinite life and boundless radiance,
and having seen, through the arising of the stainless <s>Dharma</s>-eye, may they attain supreme awakening. // 25 //

body.text: eṣāmapi daśānāṃ ślokānāṃ piṇḍārthastribhiḥ ślokairveditavyaḥ /
body.translated_text: The condensed meaning of these ten verses too is to be understood by three verses:

children.text: yataśca yannimittaṃ ca yathā ca yadudāhṛtam /
children.translated_text: From what [source], for what reason, in what manner, and what has been set forth—
and what is the outflow-result—has been illuminated in four verses. // 26 //
The means of self-protection, [explained] in two [verses], and the cause of loss, in one;
the cause and the result [are] then illuminated in two verses. // 27 //
Endurance of the cycle of <s>saṃsāra</s> and the attainment of awakening, in brief—
the twofold fruit of teaching for the sake of the <s>Dharma</s> is shown by the last [verse]. // 28 //

body.text: iti ratnagotravibhāge mahāyānottaratantraśāstre 'nuśaṃsādhikāro nāma pañcamaḥ paricchedaḥ ślokārthasaṃgrahavyākhyānataḥ samāptaḥ // 5 //
body.translated_text: Thus ends the fifth chapter, called 'The Benefits,' in the <s>Ratnagotravibhāga Mahāyānottaratantraśāstra</s>, in the form of a commentary summarizing the meaning of the verses. // 5 //
